units.slavonic_incipit: Christ Economou was born in Rendina,
units.slavonic_text: Christ Economou was born in Rendina, Greece in 1890. His grandfather, the village priest, placed him at the psaltiri (chanter’s stand) around the age of nine. Left legally blind by a high fever, Christ memorized from hearing what other chanters had learned from books. Arriving in America at age 21, he served the church in every city in which he lived, always without remuneration for himself and without reimbursment for the materials he purchased for the choir or the chanters. In 1913, Christ became the First Chanter in the “new” church of Sheboygan, Wisconsin. He went on to serve in churches in Washington State, California, Texas, and finally Tulsa, Oklahoma. In Tulsa, Christ organized a women’s choir, possibly the first women’s Greek Orthodox choir in America. Later, men joined and it became a typical four-part choir. He recruited and trained 15 other chanters during his tenure and continued as First Chanter until his death in 1973. During his 74 years of service to the church, Christ missed only two Sundays, and that was because of illness. His devotion and stewardship were recognized by Bishops and Archbishops, and he received the title of Tonsured Anagnostis.

units.slavonic_text: [Biographical Foreword Continued — Printed Page vi]
units.english_text: Although Christ Economou [the cantor] had no formal music training in his youth, he studied Byzantine music most of his life, and received vocal and instrumental music lessons throughout his time in America. He constantly transcribed Byzantine music into Western notation. In 1945, Christ wrote a concise version of the Typikon. The small book spelled out the important points of the services and pointed out mistakes in the original Violakis Typikon. If there were questions or differences in a section, he suggested how they could be resolved.

units.english_text: The study of the Typikon was a passion for my father, Christ Economou. That is why my family and I wanted to see this book published. This scholarly opus, the new bilingual Typikon, is a polychronion of effort and achievement by talented writers blessed by the Holy Spirit. I think it is fitting that the spiritual vision of a man who was physically blind should be realized in such a glorious way.

units.slavonic_text: INTRODUCTION
units.english_text: This treatise was composed after extensive study and deliberation by a committee consisting of four hierarchs and the Head Chanter George Violakis, which was appointed by the Holy Synod of the Patriarchate of Constantinople. It was written in its final form by Violakis himself and published in Constantinople in 1888. Thereafter, the Holy Patriarchate established the Violakis Typikon as the sole authoritative document outlining and stipulating the order (*taxis*) of all the services celebrated within the Church.

units.english_text: Throughout the centuries, the Church has made a continuous effort to make its services more inspiring to its worshipers, thus producing over time several Typika, each one amplifying and refining its predecessor. This sustained effort must have been inspired by St. Paul’s exhortation to us how to conduct our lives as well as how to worship God in His temple: «Πάντα δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω» (“Let all things be done decently and in order.”)[^6] 1 Corinthians 14:40.

units.english_text: It was this desire to preserve and perpetuate the order and beauty of our church services as an intrinsic, vital part of the experience of worship that impelled Dr. George T. Demos, a devoted, highly trained church musician (a medical physician by profession) to republish the Typikon by George Violakis. He wanted to reassert its sacramental authority and bring it anew to the awareness of our Church in this country by casting the book into a bilingual format, the English translation aligned with and facing the original Greek text exactly, page by opposing page. To make the work more meaningful, Dr. Demos added a dictionary of terms related to the Typikon, which he assiduously compiled and adapted from various sources.

units.english_text: After his death, I proceeded to put the work into its final form as we both had conceived it. Its publication was most generously undertaken by Poti Doukas (an aerospace engineer), a gifted member of the Choir of the Assumption Cathedral in Denver, Colorado, and Dr. George Stefanidakis (a retired chemical engineer), a member of the choir and a chanter at Annunciation Cathedral in Houston, Texas. Through his computer expertise, Dr. Stefanidakis carried out several difficult corrections and updated the entire process of printing the final version. In the meantime, James Economou, a former choir director of the Church, in an extraordinary gesture of generosity, had offered to fully finance the publication of the work.

units.slavonic_incipit: After his death, I proceeded to
units.slavonic_text: After his death, I proceeded to put the work into its final form as we both had conceived it. Its publication was most generously undertaken by Poti Doukas (an aerospace engineer), a gifted member of the Choir of the Assumption Cathedral in Denver, Colorado, and Dr. George Stefanidakis (a retired chemical engineer), a member of the choir and a chanter at Annunciation Cathedral in Houston, Texas. Through his computer expertise, Dr. Stefanidakis carried out several difficult corrections and updated the entire process of printing the final version. In the meantime, James Economou, a former choir director of the Church, in an extraordinary gesture of generosity, had offered to fully finance the publication of the work.

units.english_text: Mere words are most inadequate to offer a proper introduction or commentary to this massive work of the Typikon of the Great Church of Christ in both Greek and English. For one to consider the time, the labor, especially, the sacrificial love which contributed to this exceptional ministry of preserving the holy Byzantine tradition of worship and chant is to stand in awe and thanksgiving. Dr. George T. Demos of blessed memory, who worked patiently for sixteen years to achieve this publication, succeeded in surpassing any other work of its kind concerning Greek Orthodox liturgical practice.[^10]

units.slavonic_incipit: I can never say enough about
units.slavonic_text: I can never say enough about Dr. Demos, with whom I had many welcomed encounters, as he attempted to be faithful to the Typikon of the Church. In my twenty years of knowing him, never did he demonstrate any type of frustration in his holy project. His patience was a paramount sign of his deep dedication. The fact that his soul departed this life, while he was sitting at his desk in the early hours of the morning, continuing his work, is the greatest testimony to his commitment and religious fervor.

Not realizing what was involved, I agreed, and twenty years later this volume is the result.

units.slavonic_text: INTRODUCTION TO THE ENGLISH TRANSLATION
units.english_text: It was not just a work of sitting down with a dictionary but a real collaboration that gave me the opportunity for wonderful conversations with Dr. Demos and with Dr. Theodore Bogdanos. Besides the work of parish and family life which would take my attention for most of the time, the hardest part of this task was remembering that we were in a four-hour difference in time zones. The easiest part was the joy of sharing our mutual love of the Typikon and our excitement in discovering footnotes to the footnotes! And comparing various Typika: Jerusalem, etc.

units.slavonic_text: In 1985, the Denver Diocese Choir Federation held its annual conference in Tulsa, Oklahoma. I was the Proistamenos of the Holy Trinity parish there. Sitting in my office during the Conference one afternoon, chatting with some of the conferees, Dr. George Demos scanned the long wall of bookshelves. His eyes settled on a copy of the thesis I wrote for my Master of Divinity. The thesis was titled “The Triodion in the Typicon of the Great Church.” George asked if I would like to translate the rest of the Typikon. Not realizing what was involved, I agreed, and twenty years later this volume is the result.
units.english_text: George Demos’ best direction to me was his insistence that “If you can make me understand it, I know we are on the right track.” I only regret that George did not live to see this work completed. I remember him with great fondness both for his humor and his humanity and his great love for the Church and for this great work of love. May his memory be eternal! Now, my hope is that this English translation of the Typikon will be helpful to all priests, choir directors, chanters and other church musicians.

| Combination | Phonetic Equivalent & Rules of Pronunciation |
| :--- | :--- |

| **αυ** | av as in *savant* when before vowels or the consonants γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν and ρ; otherwise af as in *safari* |
| **ει** | i as the ee in see |
| **ευ** | ev as in *ever* when before vowels or the consonants γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν and ρ; otherwise ef as in *effort* |
| **ηυ** | iv as the ev in *eve* when before vowels or the consonants γ, δ, ζ, λ, μ, ν and ρ; otherwise if as the eef in *beef* |
| **οι** | i as the ee in see |
| **ου** | u as in *Alleluia* |
| **υι** | i as the ee in see |
| **γγ** | ng as in *anger* |
| **γκ** | ng as in *anger* |
| **μπ** | b as in *bell* at the beginning of words; otherwise mb as in *amber* |
| **ντ** | d as in *dart* at the beginning of words; otherwise nd as in *Monday* |

units.slavonic_text: Ἐνίοτε αἱ σημειώσεις αἵτινες εἶναι πολλαχοῦ ἐγκατεσπαρμέναι, διαφωνοῦσι πρὸς ὅσα σχετικὰ σημειοῖ εἰς τὰς μνήμας τῶν Ἁγίων, καὶ πᾶσα ἀσυμφωνία πρέπει νὰ ἐκλείψῃ, ἀρθῇ πᾶσα ἀπορία καὶ διορθωθῇ πᾶσα, ἔστω καὶ ἐπουσιώδης, ἀντίφασις ἢ παραλλαγή.
units.english_text: Ἐπίσης καθότι ὁ Ἑσπερινὸς ἀνήκει τῇ ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ, μεθ' ἧς καὶ συνέχεται ἀναποσπάστως καθ' ὅλα τὰ μέρη, καὶ ἐν ἑκάστῃ δεσποτικῇ ἑορτῇ ἡ ἀπόλυσις τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ ἐστιν ἡ αὐτὴ τῇ τῆς Λειτουργίας, ὁ πρωτοψάλτης Κωνσταντῖνος σημειοῖ ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Ἁγίων Πάντων ὅτι ἡ χρῆσις τοῦ «Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν», κατὰ τὴν ἀπόλυσιν τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Κυριακῆς, οὐ μόνον ἀπᾴδει, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀσυγχώρητός ἐστι, διότι τάχα ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν ἀνέστη κατὰ τὸ μεσονύκτιον. Ἡ Ἐπιτροπὴ καθώρισε καὶ τοῦτο, τῇ στάθμῃ τῆς ἀναλογίας καὶ ἀκριβείας ἀκολουθήσασα, ἥτις τηρεῖται καὶ ἐν πάσαις ταῖς δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς.

units.slavonic_incipit: The synodically appointed five-member Committee consisting
units.slavonic_text: The synodically appointed five-member Committee consisting of the Reverend Metropolitans of Ainos, Samos, Caesarea, Mytiline and the Protopsaltis [highest-ranking chanter] of the Great Church George Violakis, which reviewed the previous Typika of the Church—such as that by the Protopsaltis Constantine—which are in use today, corrected in its report the errors and inaccuracies of these works as follows:
units.english_text: The 9th Hour of every day, continuing the 1st, 3rd, and 6th [Hours] and belonging to that day, which closes ecclesiastically before Vespers, must follow the order that the Committee has prescribed in an analogous situation with the 9th Hour being done before the Vespers of the Sunday of Thomas[^18] as well as before the Vespers of Wednesday and Thursday before the Feast of the Ascension.

units.slavonic_incipit: Occasionally, their various guidelines, which are
units.slavonic_text: Occasionally, their various guidelines, which are scattered in many places in their work, differ on what is appropriate to be performed on the commemorations [feasts] of the saints. Every disagreement, therefore, must cease to exist, every doubt must be clearly articulated and corrected, however secondary or minor the contradiction or variation may be.
units.english_text: Also, since the Vespers belongs to the following day, with which it is joined inseparably in all the places in it, then, on every Feast of the Lord, the Dismissal Prayer of the Vespers is the same as that of the Liturgy. Constantine the Protopsaltis, however, indicates that, in the Vespers of the Sunday of All Saints, the use of “Who did rise from the dead” in the Dismissal Prayer of the Vespers of that Sunday is not only incompatible but also unforgivable since our Lord arose around midnight. The Committee decided on this issue also, following the same standard of analogy and exactness that is observed on all the Feasts of the Lord.

units.slavonic_incipit: ἧττον ὅμως ἡ Ἐπιτροπὴ ἀμφιβάλλει ἂν
units.slavonic_text: ἧττον ὅμως ἡ Ἐπιτροπὴ ἀμφιβάλλει ἂν ῥητῶς ἀρχαῖόν τι Τυπικὸν ἀπαγορεύει τὴν χρῆσιν τῆς τοιαύτης κατανυκτικῆς εὐχῆς ἐν τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Θωμᾶ μέχρι τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς διαστήματι.
units.english_text: Τὸ νέον Τυπικὸν ἠθέλησεν ἐπίσης εἰς τοὺς Κανόνας καὶ τὰ Καθίσματα ἵνα τηρήσῃ τὴν δυνατὴν ἀκρίβειαν, ἐφ' ὅσον αἱ σημεριναὶ περιστάσεις ἐπιτρέπουσιν· ὥστε, διαγραφομένης πιστῶς τῆς τυπικῆς ἀκριβείας, ἀπόκειται τῷ κατὰ τόπον Ἀρχιερεῖ συντέμνειν ἢ παραλείπειν, ἂν ἀπαραίτητος ἀνάγκη καιρῶν, τόπων καὶ περιστάσεων ἐπιβάλλῃ τοῦτο. Ἰδίως περὶ καθισμάτων λέγομεν ὅτι ὁ ἀοίδιμος πρωτοψάλτης Κωνσταντῖνος, ὅτε συνέπιπτεν εἰς Κυριακὴν μνήμη Ἁγίου ἑορταζομένου, ὡς π.χ. τοῦ ἁγ. Ἰωάννου τοῦ Θεολόγου (κστ΄ Σεπτ.), τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων (κθ΄ Ἰουνίου), τῶν Ταξιαρχῶν (η΄ Νοεμβρ.), κτλ. σημειοῖ «τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν καὶ τὸ τελευταῖον τοῦ ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας»· καὶ οὕτως ἐν ταῖς δυσὶ πρώταις Στιχολογίαις οὐδὲν τοῦ ἁγίου ἐλέγετο παρὰ τὴν ἀρχαίαν τάξιν (καθ' ἣν ἐν ἑκάστῃ Στιχολογίᾳ παρενείρετο καὶ ἓν Κάθισμα τοῦ ἁγίου), ἀλλὰ μόνον τὰ μετὰ τὸν Πολυέλεον Καθίσματα τοῦ ἁγίου. Ἐν δὲ μνήμαις ἄλλων ἁγίων, οἷον τοῦ Προφήτου Ἠλιού, τῆς ἁγίας Μαρίνης καὶ ἑτέρων, καταλιμπάνει ὁλοσχερῶς τὰ Καθίσματα τοῦ ἑορταζομένου ἁγίου, ἂν συμπέσῃ Κυριακή. Τὸ νέον Τυπικὸν ἐν ταῖς μνήμαις τῶν ἐπισημότερον ἑορταζομένων ἐκκλησιαστικῶς ἁγίων, ἤτοι τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων, τοῦ Εὐαγγελιστοῦ Ἰωάννου, τοῦ ἁγίου Ἀνδρέου, τῶν Ταξιαρχῶν, ἔχει ἀνὰ ἓν ἐκ τοῦ Ἁγίου ἐν ἑκάστῃ τῶν δύο πρώτων Στιχολογιῶν, καὶ ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ ὅσα μετὰ τὴν τοῦ Πολυελέου Στιχολογίαν ἔχει ὁ ἅγιος.

Τὸ νέον Τυπικὸν οὐδὲν ἐγκαταλείπει ἀσημείωτον ἐξ ἐκείνων δι' ἃ προκύπτει ἀμφιβολία, ἔχον ὑπ' ὄψει τοὺς ἀδαεστέρους τῶν ἐφημερίων καὶ ψαλτῶν μᾶλλον ἢ τοὺς τρίβωνας καὶ εἰδημονεστέρους τῆς τυπικῆς τάξεως.

units.english_text: The writers of the new Typikon also wished to observe all possible accuracy in the Canons and in the Kathismata, as long as today's circumstances allow it, so that, even if the exactness of the order of the Typikon has been faithfully outlined, it is up to the decision of the local hierarch to abridge it or omit from it, if the indispensable need of time, place, and situation demands it. Especially concerning the Kathismata, we say that the ever-memorable Protopsaltis Constantine, whenever the commemoration of a saint fell on a Sunday—such as, for example, the Feasts of St. John the Theologian (September 26), the Holy Apostles (June 29), the Archangels (November 8), etc.—writes “the Resurrection Kathismata in order [should be done] and the last Kathisma should be that of the saint of the day.” Thus, in the first two Sections [Stichologiai] no Kathisma of the Saint was said according to the ancient order (in which in each Section [Stichologia] was inserted also one Kathisma of the Saint), but only the Kathismata of the Saint [that come] after the Polyeleos [should be done]. On the other hand, at the commemorations of other saints—such as the Prophet Elijah, St. Marina, and other saints—the Kathismata of the celebrating saint are entirely omitted if the feast of this celebrating saint happens to fall on a Sunday. At the commemorations of the ecclesiastically more eminent celebrating saints—such as the Holy Apostles, St. John the Evangelist, St. Andrew, the Archangels—the new Typikon has one Kathisma of the Saint in each of the first two Sections [Stichologiai], and, in the third Section [Stichologia], as many Kathismata as the saint has in the Section after the Polyeleos.[^20]

On the other hand, at the commemorations of other saints—such as the Prophet Elijah, St. Marina, and other saints—the Kathismata of the celebrating saint are entirely omitted if the feast of this celebrating saint happens to fall on a Sunday. Also, concerning the Beatitudes [Makarismi], the Typikon of Constantine, still in present use, writes in many places the succinct phrase “the Beatitudes are said” or “the Resurrection Beatitudes are said,” thus alluding to Constantine's statement that the “hymns [Troparia] of the 6th Ode [of the Canon] of the Saint are omitted,” as, for example, on the 2nd and 5th Sunday of Great Lent (while on the 4th [Sunday of Lent] he writes “both the Beatitudes”), as well as on the Feasts of Prophet Elijah and St. Panteleimon. Ὡρῶν τῆς ἑορτῆς τῶν Θεοφανείων, ἤτοι τὸ Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλών, ἢ τὸ τῆς παραμονῆς Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτέ. γʹ) Εἰ τὸ τοῦ Πάσχα Εἰσοδικὸν Ἐν ἐκκλησίαις εὐλογεῖτε τὸν Θεὸν λεκτέον καὶ τὰς μετὰ τὴν Κυριακὴν τοῦ Θωμᾶ ἡμέρας, ὁσάκις ἂν γίνηται Λειτουργία, ἢ τὸ Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν, σημειοῖ ὡς ἡ ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ διάταξις (ἴδε Κυριακὴν Θωμᾶ) καὶ διὰ τὰς Κυριακὰς ἔτι αὐτὰς τοῦ Πεντηκοσταρίου. δʹ) Εἰ παραλειπτέον τὸ ἀλληλούϊα μετὰ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τῆς περικοπῆς τῶν Πράξεων τῶν Ἀποστόλων κατὰ τὴν Διακαινήσιμον Ἑβδομάδα, ὡς εἰθίσθη ἀπό τινων ἐτῶν, καίτοι ἡ ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ διάταξις διαγορεύει τὸ ἐναντίον, προστιθεῖσα καὶ τοὺς στίχους ἔτι τοῦ Ἀλληλούϊα μετὰ τὸ ἀνάγνωσμα.

units.english_text: expert in the order of the Typikon. The Typikon of Constantine indicates for the Midnight Service [Mesonyktikon] of Sunday the three Penitential Hymns beginning with **"Lord, have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us"** (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*). The new Typikon, in accordance with the formulation of the Horologion, prescribes the Ypakoe of the Tone [Tone 1–8]; only for the Sundays of the period of the Triodion has the new Typikon allowed the three Penitential Hymns mentioned above [to be done] instead of the Ypakoe.[^22]

units.english_text: The new Typikon, taking into consideration the many difficulties [ambiguities] herein, included the Antiphons of all the Feasts of the Lord and the [Feasts of the] Theotokos, as well as their Megalynaria, so that these may be readily available to the choirs so that no discord [*chasmodia*] may result in the Church.[^23]

units.slavonic_text: The Committee, before it completes the present report, requests His All-Holiness [the Patriarch] and the Holy Synod to decide on the following questions:
units.english_text: 1. If December 24th falls on a Sunday, whether the Resurrection Hymns are omitted or not in the Vespers and in Matins as is indicated in the Typikon of Constantine, as well as another Typikon issued in 1685 with the title “Typikon of the Ecclesiastical Service.”[^24]

units.slavonic_text: 1. If December 24th falls on a Sunday, whether the Resurrection Hymns are omitted or not in the Vespers and in Matins as is indicated in the Typikon of Constantine, as well as another Typikon issued in 1685 with the title “Typikon of the Ecclesiastical Service.”
units.english_text: 2. If whenever the Feast of Christmas occurs on a Sunday or Monday, whether on the Friday before, when the Great Hours are chanted, we say the Troparion of the Forefeast **"Make ready, Bethlehem"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*), or that of the Eve of the Feast [Paramoni] **"When recorded in the census"** (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε*). This situation is analogous to that involving the Troparion of the Great Hours of the Feast of Epiphany, that is, the Forefeast Troparion **"Make ready, Zabulon"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλών*), versus that of the Eve [Paramoni] **"The Jordan River turned back"** (*Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*).[^25]

This situation is analogous to that involving the Troparion of the Great Hours of the Feast of Epiphany, that is, the Forefeast Troparion **"Make ready, Zabulon"** (*Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλών*), versus that of the Eve [Paramoni] **"The Jordan River turned back"** (*Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*).[^25]

units.slavonic_text: [Original Greek Text: Patriarchal Commission Report Concluded]
units.english_text: εʹ) Εἰ ὁ Ἑσπερινὸς καὶ ὁ Ὄρθρος κατὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς Διακαινησίμου ἑβδομάδος ἄρχονται διὰ τοῦ **«Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ»**, ὡς διαγορεύει τὸ ἐν χρήσει Τυπικόν, ἢ διὰ τοῦ **«Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν»**, ὡς ἀναφέρει τὸ ἀρχαῖον Τυπικὸν τοῦ αχπεʹ καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ τάξις (ὅρα Κυριακὴν τοῦ Πάσχα ἑσπέρας).

units.slavonic_text: Ἐν τέλει δ' ἡ ἐκ τῶν ἄνω ῥηθέντων μελῶν ἐπιτροπὴ ἀποφαίνεται καὶ λέγει, ὅτι ἡ πρώτη ἐπιτροπὴ οὐσιώδεις μεταβολὰς δὲν ἔκαμεν ἐπὶ τοῦ Τυπικοῦ οὔτε ἡ δευτέρα αὕτη, καθὼς καὶ αἱ γενόμεναι τροποποιήσεις ἔγειναν ἐπὶ τῶν παραδεδεγμένων διατυπώσεων, ἐνησχολήθησαν δὲ πάντες εἰς τὴν εὐληπτοτέραν διατύπωσιν τῆς ὕλης, εἰς τὴν ἀναπλήρωσιν τῶν ἐλλειπόντων, εἰς τὴν ἀναπλήρωσιν τῶν ἐλλειπόντων, εἰς τὴν τήρησιν συμμετρίας εἰς πάσας τὰς ἑορτάς, ὥστε νὰ μὴ μείνωσι χάσματα, τὰ ὁποῖα νὰ παρέχωσι δισταγμοὺς εἰς τοὺς ἱεροψάλτας, καὶ ἐν τέλει μετὰ μεγαλειτέρας εὐκολίας διὰ τὴν ἀνεύρεσιν τῆς τυπικῆς τάξεως κατὰ τὰς διαφόρους περιπτώσεις.

units.english_text: 7. Finally, the Committee believes that upon the election of a Patriarch, instead of **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς μακαρίζειν σὲ τὴν Θεοτόκον*), it is preferable to sing **"It is truly right to hymn the Supremely Divine Trinity"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς τὴν Ὑπέρθεον ὑμνεῖν Τριάδα*) and asks that this be established as a practice.[^30]

Finally, the Committee believes that upon the election of a Patriarch, instead of “It is fitting and right to call you blessed, O Theotokos,” it is preferable to sing “It is fitting and right to praise with hymns the supremely divine Trinity” and asks that this be established as a practice.¹
units.english_text: In conclusion, the members of the Committee mentioned above declare and state that the first committee did not make essential changes in the Typikon, neither did the second committee. Only fully studied changes were made upon the given formulations; all members of the Committee were engaged in presenting the material in a comprehendable manner, in the replacing of the deficiencies, in the adherence to the harmony of all the feasts so that there will not remain gaps which would cause doubts to the chanters, and, in the end, there will be greater ease in the recovering of the correct order of the Typikon for the various situations.

Διὸ καὶ τοὺς ψάλλοντας ἐν ἐκκλησίαις, ὁ Κανὼν ἀπαιτεῖ μετὰ προσοχῆς καὶ κατανύξεως ψάλλειν, ἀλλὰ μὴ ἀτάκτως βοᾶν, καὶ τὴν φωνὴν ἐκβιάζεσθαι πρὸς κραυγήν· κραυγὴ δέ ἐστιν ἐπιτεταμένη φωνὴ καὶ βιαίως ἐκρηγνυμένη. units.english_text: “We will that those whose office it is to sing in the churches do not use undisciplined vociferations, nor force nature to shouting, nor adopt any of those modes which are incongruous and unsuitable for the church: but that they offer the psalmody to God, Who is the observer of secrets, with great attention and compunction. For the Sacred Oracle taught that the Sons of Israel were to be pious.”[^31]

units.slavonic_text: “We will that those whose office it is to sing in the churches do not use undisciplined vociferations, nor force nature to shouting, nor adopt any of those modes which are incongruous and unsuitable for the church: but that they offer the psalmody to God, Who is the observer of secrets, with great attention and compunction. For the Sacred Oracle taught that the Sons of Israel were to be pious.”
units.english_text: Zonaras relates the chanters of his time to the sons of Israel, all being the children of God, and holds their reverence and piety in the act of worship as a model to be emulated by the chanters of Zonaras’s own time. Since the chanting in church is essentially a supplication to God, the chanters should sing in a humble and penitent manner, avoiding self-exhibition with musical extravagance such as excessive embellishments or loud voices distracting the worshiper. At the same time, Zonaras insists on good musicianship, condemning formless, arhythmical melodies. The music itself should be appropriate to the sacred place, avoiding any secular or erotic associations. He pleads for solemnity as well as artistic unity in the act of worship.[^32]

units.english_text: Αἱ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐκκλησίαι, οἶκοι προσευχῶν λέγονται· ὅθεν καὶ οἱ προσευχόμενοι παρακαλεῖν τὸν Θεὸν ὀφείλουσι μετὰ δακρύων καὶ ταπεινώσεως, οὐ μὴν μετὰ ἀτάκτου καὶ ἀναιδοῦς σχήματος. Διωρίσαντο γοῦν οἱ Πατέρες, μὴ γίνεσθαι τὰ ἱερὰ ψαλμῳδήματα διὰ βοῶν ἀτάκτων καὶ ἐπιτεταμένων καὶ τὴν φύσιν παραβιαζομένων· μήτε μὴν διά τινων καλλιφωνιῶν, ἀνοικείων τῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ καταστάσει καὶ ἀκολουθίᾳ, οἷά εἰσι τὰ θυμελικὰ μέλη καὶ αἱ περιτταὶ ποικιλίαι τῶν φωνῶν· ἀλλὰ μετὰ πολλῆς κατανύξεως καὶ θεαρέστου τρόπου προσάγειν τῷ Θεῷ τὰς εὐχάς, τῷ εἰδότι τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν καρδιῶν ἡμῶν. Ταῦτα δὲ παρεκελεύσαντο ἀκολούθως τῷ εὐαγγελικῷ ῥητῷ, τῷ διοριζομένῳ, μὴ κατὰ ἐθνικοὺς εὔχεσθαι ἡμᾶς μετὰ βαττολογίας καὶ κραυγῆς, ὡς οἰομένης εἰσακουσθῆναι διὰ τὴν πολυλογίαν ἡμῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ προσάγειν τὸν ὕμνον τῷ Θεῷ· ποιεῖν δὲ καὶ τὰς αἰτήσεις ὁμοίως, ἵνα καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος, ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ, ἀποδώσῃ ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ φανερῷ. Ἐπεὶ δέ, φασί, καὶ ὁ Μωσαϊκὸς νόμος εἶπεν ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ· Εὐλαβεῖς ποιεῖτε τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ, μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τοῦ νόμου τούτου δεξάμενοι τὸ πλήρωμα, ὀφείλομεν εὐλαβέστεροι εἶναι καὶ κατὰ τὰ νενομισμένα πολιτεύεσθαι. Ἐπεὶ δὲ παρὰ διαφόροις ἁγιωτάτοις πατριάρχαις ἐλαλήθη, μὴ μόνον ἐν ταῖς ἑορταῖς γίνεσθαι τοιαῦτα παρὰ τῶν ψαλτῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν παννυχίσι καὶ μνημοσύνοις τεθνεώτων, γεγόνασι διάφορα σημειώματα συνοδικά, ἀφορισμῷ καθυποβάλλοντα τοὺς τοιαῦτα ποιοῦντας, καὶ μὴ διὰ ψαλμῳδημάτων καὶ ἀλληλουαρίων λιτῶν, ψαλλομένων κατὰ τὸ θεμέλιον τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἐκπληροῦντας τὴν παννύχιον ψαλμῳδίαν. Ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τῆς ἐν Καρθαγένη συνόδου [418 ἢ 419 μ.Χ.] κανόνα ρηʹ καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ γραφέντα· ὡσαύτως ἀνάγνωθι καὶ τὸν εἰς τὰ Σεραφεὶμ καὶ τὸν πανηγυρικὸν λόγον τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου, τὸν γραφέντα εἰς τὴν ἑρμηνείαν τοῦ προφητικοῦ ῥητοῦ, τοῦ λέγοντος· «εἶδον τὸν Κύριον καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου ὑψηλοῦ καὶ ἐπηρμένου»· κωλύει γὰρ τὰς θυμελικὰς ψαλμῳδίας καὶ τὰς ὀρχήσεις τῶν χειρονομούντων, καὶ τὰς ἐκτεταμένας ἐκφωνήσεις.

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Balsamon Summary]
units.english_text: Valsamon reminds us that churches are houses of prayer. The faithful should pray to God with contrition and humility, avoiding extravagant, unbecoming deportment or attire. Similarly, those who take an active part in performing a liturgical event—clergymen and chanters—should avoid musical self-exhibition as well as theatrical effects in their ritual movement that do not fit the holy and solemn sacred occasion.

units.slavonic_text: EXEGETICAL COMMENT BY VALSAMON
units.english_text: Like Zonaras, Valsamon invokes Mosaic law and the piety of the sons of Israel as an example for his time. He goes on to state that his contemporaries, having been enlightened by their faith as Christians, should be even more reverent than their Israeli counterparts. To further authenticate his plea for reverence, he refers to the 98th Canon of the Council in Carthage [A.D. 418 or 419] and to a celebratory homily by St. John Chrysostom on the proper manner of worship.[^33]

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Exegetical Comment by Aristinos & Chrysostom]
units.english_text: “The disordered voice of a chanter is not acceptable.” Invoking even the tradition of Israel (and by implication the manner of worship in David’s Tent), Aristinos castigates “loud, jagged voices” that distract the worshiper from meditation and from prayerful reverence toward God, for God knows the silent, secret thoughts of His creatures; He does not need this tawdry loudness.[^34]

units.slavonic_text: “The disordered voice of a chanter is not acceptable.” Invoking even the tradition of Israel (and by implication the manner of worship in David’s Tent), Aristinos castigates “loud, jagged voices” that distract the worshiper from meditation and from prayerful reverence toward God, for God knows the silent, secret thoughts of His creatures; He does not need this tawdry loudness.

units.english_text: “Let us enter herein [into the temple] with fitting reverence, lest instead of receiving remission of sins we depart for home having added to them. What then is required, and what is demanded of us? That those who send up divine hymns offer them constrained with great fear and adorned with piety. For indeed there are some who, despising God and accounting the words of the Spirit as common things, utter disordered shouts and are in no way better disposed than madmen, shaking and tossing about with their whole body and displaying manners alien to a spiritual disposition. O wretched and miserable man! When one ought in fear and trembling to send forth the angelic doxology, and make confession with dread to the Creator, seeking through this forgiveness for offenses committed, you on the contrary introduce here the antics of mimes and dancers, stretching forth your hands in an unruly manner, hopping with your feet, and contorting your entire body! What do hands contribute toward supplication when continually raised aloft in vain distraction and waved about disorderly, accompanied by violent shouting that by its forceful propulsion becomes indistinct and unintelligible? Is this what it means to serve in fear: to be undisciplined and frantic, not even understanding what you are uttering through the disorderly reverberation of your voice? But someone will object: The Prophet exhorts us to praise with a shout of joy, saying: **'Shout with joy unto the Lord...'** (*Ἀλαλάξατε γὰρ τῷ Κυρίῳ*)...”

units.english_text: «Ἐχώμεθα τοίνυν τῆς ἀρετῆς· μὴ μέχρι τέρψεως τὰ λεγόμενα ἔστω, μηδὲ μέχρι παραμυθίας τινός. Οὐκ ἔστι τὸ θέατρον τοῦτο, ἀγαπητέ, κιθαρῳδῶν, οὐδὲ τραγῳδῶν, ἔνθα μέχρι τῆς τέρψεως ὁ καρπός, καὶ τῆς ἡμέρας παραδραμούσης παρῆλθεν ἡ τέρψις. Καὶ εἴλθε ἦν τέρψις μόνη καὶ μὴ καὶ βλάβη μετὰ τῆς τέρψεως· ἀλλ’ ὅμως ἄπεισιν ἐκεῖθεν οἴκαδε ἕκαστος, καθάπερ ἀπό τινος λύμης ἀναμαξάμενος πολλὰ τῶν αὐτόθι· καὶ ὁ μὲν νέος ἀπολαβών τινα τῶν σατανικῶν ἀσμάτων μέλη, ὅσα ἴσχυσε τῇ μνήμῃ καταθέσθαι, συνεχῶς ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας ᾄδει· ὁ δὲ πρεσβύτης, ἅτε δὴ σεμνότερος, τοῦτο μὲν οὐ ποιεῖ, τῶν δὲ ἐκεῖσε λεγομένων ῥημάτων μέμνηται πάντων. Ἐντεῦθεν οὐδὲν ἔχοντες ἄπιτε. Καὶ πῶς οὐκ αἰσχύνης ἄξιον; » (Τοῦ αὐτοῦ Ὁμιλ. Χ. εἰς τὰς Πράξ. τῶν Ἀποστ. ἔκδ. Migne τόμ. 60).

units.slavonic_text: “Let us then hold fast to virtue; let not these words end only in delight, and in a certain elevation of the spirits. This is not the theater, for singers, and tragedians, and musicians, where the fruit consists only in the enjoyment and where the enjoyment itself passes with the passing day. Nay, would that it were enjoyment alone, and not mischief also with the enjoyment! But so it is: each man carries home with him much of what he has witnessed there, sticking to him like the infection of a plague: and one indeed, of the younger sort, having culled such snatches of song here and there of those satanic plays, as he could fix in his memory, goes singing them about the house: while another, a senior, and forsooth too staid for such levity, does not this indeed, but what is there spoken, boththe preachments and the very words, he remembers it all; and another again, some filthy and absurd ditty. From this place depart, taking nothing with you.” {The meaning is} “He cannot carry away in his memory the preaching which he hears in Church; but the preachments (proclamations) which he hears in the theater he remembers, every word,”} [**]
units.english_text: “‘Let us then hold fast to virtue; let not these words end only in delight, and in a certain elevation of the spirits. This is not the theater for singers, tragedians, and musicians, where the fruit consists only in enjoyment, and where the enjoyment itself passes with the passing day. Nay, would that it were enjoyment alone, and not harm also with the enjoyment! But so it is: each man carries home with him much of what he has witnessed there, clinging to him like the contagion of a plague. And one indeed of the younger sort, having culled such snatches of song here and there from those satanic melodies as he could fix in his memory, continually sings them about the house; while another, an elder, being more dignified, does not do this indeed, but remembers every word spoken there. Yet departing from this place [the church], you carry away nothing! And how is this not worthy of utter shame?’” (Saint John Chrysostom, *Homily X on the Acts of the Apostles*, Migne ed., Vol. 60).[^37]

units.english_text: ...εὐφραίνεσθαι; Βούλει τὴν ἡμέραν ἀναλίσκειν; Ἐγώ σοι δίδωμι πότον πνευματικόν· ἡ γὰρ μέθη καὶ τὴν εὔσημον ἐκκόπτει φωνὴν τῆς γλώσσης τῆς ἡμετέρας ψελλίζειν παρασκευάζουσα, καὶ ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ πάντα ἁπλῶς διαστρέφουσα. Μάθε ψάλλειν, καὶ ὄψει τοῦ πράγματος τὴν ἡδονήν· οἱ ψάλλοντες γὰρ πνεύματος πληροῦνται ἁγίου, ὥσπερ οἱ ᾄδοντες τὰς σατανικὰς ᾠδὰς πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου. Τί ἐστιν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ; τουτέστι, μετὰ συνέσεως προσέχοντες· οἱ γὰρ οὐ προσέχοντες ἁπλῶς ψάλλουσι, τὰ ῥήματα φθεγγόμενοι, τῆς καρδίας ῥεμβομένης ἑτέρωθι.» (Τοῦ αὐτοῦ Ὁμιλ. ΧΙΧ. εἰς τὴν πρὸς Ἐφεσίους ἐπιστολήν, Migne τόμ. 62).

units.english_text: «Σὺ οὖν, τέκνον κανονάρχα, ὡς τοῦ μεγάλου καὶ πρώτου ἔργου κατάρχων τῆς θείας Λειτουργίας καὶ ὑμνῳδίας, διεγερτὴς τῶν ψαλλόντων ἕκαστα, καθὼς διατέτακταί σοι, ἀποπληρῶν τὰ καθίσματα, τὰ στιχηρά, συνείδησιν τηρῶν ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ. Νῆφε καὶ ἀδολέσχει, καὶ δικαίῳ λόγῳ καὶ τὰς ἑορτασίμους ἡμέρας καὶ τὰς ἐπιλοίπους διέξαγε πρὸς ἕκαστον τῶν ἀδελφῶν, ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τόδε ψάλλειν, ἢ ἀναγινώσκειν τόδε, καὶ ἐν τῇδε τόδε· ἐπιτηρῶν καὶ τὸ εὔφωνον καὶ τὸ εὔλαλον καὶ ταχύλαλον τοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος, πρὸς τὸ καὶ τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας ἐπιξενουμένου ὠφελεῖσθαι· συναναλαμβανόμενος ἑαυτὸν πάντα εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν ποίει ἵνα χορεύσῃς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων καὶ τῆς σῆς ἀδελφότητος, εἴπερ καταξιωθείης ἔχειν τοιαύτην κατάστασιν· εὐστόχως δὲ καὶ ἀφύρτως καὶ τὴν τῶν ψαλμῶν στιχολογίαν ἐκτέλει, ὑποστηρίζων καὶ ἐμβιβάζων, καὶ ἐπὶ λόγοις σφαλεροῖς ἐπανορθῶν, καὶ πρὸς ἓν μέλος πάντας διακρατῶν, κατὰ τὸν ἦχον τῆς ψαλμῳδίας...

units.english_text: ...another in the fear of Christ.’ [Ephesians 5:18–21]. ‘Do you wish,’ he says, ‘to be cheerful, do you wish to spend the day well? I give you spiritual drink; for drunkenness cuts off even the clear articulation of our tongue, causing us to stammer and lisp, and distorts our eyes and our whole frame together. Learn to chant psalms, and you shall see the delightfulness of the employment! For those who chant psalms are filled with the Holy Spirit, even as those who sing satanic songs are filled with an unclean spirit. What is meant by *with your hearts to the Lord*? It means, paying heed with spiritual understanding; for those who do not attend closely merely chant outwardly, uttering the words with their mouth while their heart wanders elsewhere.’” (Saint John Chrysostom, *Homily XIX on the Epistle to the Ephesians*, Migne ed., Vol. 62).[^38]

I give you spiritual drink; for drunkenness even cuts off the articulate sound of our tongue; it makes us lisp and stammer, and distorts the eyes, and the whole frame together. Learn to sing psalms, and you shall see the delightfulness of the employment. For they who sing psalms are filled with the Holy Spirit, as they who sing satanic songs are filled with an unclean spirit. What is meant by ‘with your hearts to the Lord’? It means, with close attention and understanding. For they who do not attend closely, merely sing, uttering the words, while their heart is roaming elsewhere.” [***]
units.english_text: Our Holy Father Theodore the Studite addresses chanters and canonarchs, exhorting them to refine and further spiritualize their tasks. He first reminds them of the lofty, sacramental character of their ministry. He urges them to obey the established order of service and to be always conscious of the significance and the liturgical form of all types of hymns: e.g. Kathismata, Stichera.[^39]

units.english_text: In chanting and reciting, they should use a clear, well-rounded voice, following Saint Paul’s exhortation that everything in the act of divine worship should be done decently and in order (*kata taxin*). The chanter should exercise restraint and avoid extravagance, such as singing a very high note and then, for theatrical effect, descending suddenly to a very low note. The good chanter should help other aspiring chanters to develop their God-given talent. Thus, God will compensate the chanter’s humanly limited service with infinite blessings.

units.slavonic_incipit: The fourth of Our Holy Fathers
units.slavonic_text: The fourth of Our Holy Fathers among the Saints, Theodore the Studite addresses chanters and canonarchs [****] exhorting them to refine and further spiritualize their tasks. He first reminds them of the lofty, sacramental character of their ministry. He urges them to obey the established order of service and to be always conscious of the significance and the form of all types of hymns: e.g. kathismata, stichira. In chanting and reciting, they should use a clear, well-rounded voice, following St. Paul’s exhortation that everything in the act of worship should be done with beauty and order (efschimonos ke kata taxin). The chanter should exercise restraint and avoid extravagance, such as singing a very high note and then, for effect, descend suddenly to a very low note. The good chanter should help other aspiring chanters to develop their God-given talent. Thus, God will compensate his humanly limited and finite service with infinite blessings.

units.english_text: ...μήτε ὑπερανάγων, μήτε καταρρίπτων, ἀλλὰ μεσότητι προσυπάγων· οὕτω γὰρ καὶ διδασκόμεθα ὑπὸ τῶν Πατέρων· θέλημα ἔχων καὶ ἔργον ποιούμενος τὰ ἀποτυπωθέντα στιχηροκαθίσματα ἐκμαθεῖν τὴν ἀδελφότητα· μάλιστα τοὺς δυναμένους καὶ προσιόντας σοι ἐν πολλῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ, πληθύνων τὸ τάλαντον, ὃ παρὰ Θεοῦ σοι κεχάρισται· ἵνα ἀκούσῃς τῆς εὐλογημένης ἐκείνης φωνῆς· Εὖ δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἧς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω».

units.english_text: Ὁ ΙΕ΄ τῆς ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ Συνόδου [364 μ.Χ.] κανὼν οὐδόλως ἐπιτρέπει νὰ ψάλλῃ ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ ὁ τυχών, ἀλλὰ καθῆκον τοῦτο θεωρεῖ τῶν κανονικῶν ἤτοι τῶν ἐν τῷ κλήρῳ συνηριθμημένων καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ προκεχειρισμένων ψαλτῶν· διότι ἀταξία ὁμολογουμένως συμβαίνει καὶ χασμῳδία ὅταν ψάλλῃ ὁ τυχὼν ἀμαθὴς καὶ ἄμουσος, τοὐναντίον δὲ εὐταξία καὶ συγκίνησις, ὅταν ψάλλωσιν οἱ μουσικῆς ἔμπειροι καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς τάξεως γνῶσται.

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: On Chanters & Guiding Criteria]
units.english_text: Violakis cites the 15th Canon of the Council of Laodicea [A.D. 364], which strictly forbids anyone to chant in church services except canonical chanters who are numbered among the clergy and appointed to this ministry. To avoid disorder and musical confusion (*chasmodia*), only highly trained and experienced chanters are permitted to sing, in order to create ecclesiastical order (*eutaxia*) and evoke in the faithful holy compunction and reverence.[^40]

provenance.verbatim_source: Violakis cites the 15th Canon of the Council of Laodicea [A.D. 364], which strictly forbids anyone to chant in church services except canonical chanters who are numbered among the clergy and appointed to this ministry. To avoid disorder and musical confusion (*chasmodia*), only highly trained and experienced chanters are permitted to sing, in order to create ecclesiastical order (*eutaxia*) and evoke in the faithful holy compunction and reverence.[^40]

units.slavonic_text: Violakis cites the 15th Canon of the Ecumenical Council in Laodicea [A.D. 364] which forbids anyone to chant in church services except ordained chanters who have musical training and talent. To avoid disorder and confusion in sound (chasmodia), only highly tutored and experienced chanters should be allowed to chant in order to create ordered beauty (eftaxia) and elicit in the churchgoer the proper emotions (sygkinisis).
units.english_text: 1. Chanters should be selected only if they harmonize with one another in vocal timbre and in musical artistry.

provenance.verbatim_source: 1. Chanters should be selected only if they harmonize with one another in vocal timbre and in musical artistry.

units.slavonic_text: 3. Certain lessons should be assigned for the training of chanters. 4. The members of the chant group should perform their task in a solemn and reverent manner avoiding affectation and impropriety. 5. The members of the chant group should practice clear diction so that those who attend the services understand the sacred text and respond to it with the appropriate feelings. 6. The rhythm and speed of each hymn should be written down for every section of the hymn, so that the chanters may study them beforehand. 7. The ison part of the ison holders should be written in a separate line in the hymn.
units.english_text: 4. Sacred gravity and reverence must be observed by all members of the choir, avoiding any theatrical affectation or laxity.

units.slavonic_text: [Original Greek Text: Pretheory of the Typikon — The Ninth Hour (p. 36)]
units.english_text: Ἡ πρὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ἀναγινωσκομένη θ΄ ὥρα ἐστὶ σφραγὶς τῆς Ἀκολουθίας τῆς ἤδη ληγούσης ἐκκλησιαστικῶς ἡμέρας. Καὶ ἂν ἡ ἡμέρα ᾖ Δεσποτικὴ ἢ Θεομητορικὴ ἑορτὴ ἢ μεθέορτος ἢ μνήμη ἑορταζομένου Ἁγίου, Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ Κοντάκιον λέγονται ἐν ταύτῃ τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἢ τοῦ Ἁγίου· εἰ δὲ μή, τὸ τοῦ τυχόντος Ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ἀντὶ Κοντακίου λέγεται τὸ **«Βλέπων ὁ Λῃστὴς τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς»**. *Δόξα*, **«Ἐν μέσῳ δύο λῃστῶν»**. *Καὶ νῦν*, **«Τὸν Ἀμνὸν καὶ Ποιμένα»**. Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας Ἀπολυτίκιον **«Ἀπόστολοι μάρτυρες»** καὶ Κοντάκιον **«Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως»**· τῇ δὲ Κυριακῇ ἑσπέρας τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ἀντὶ Κοντακίου ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ Ἤχου. units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Pre-Theory of the Typikon — The Ninth Hour (p. 37)]
units.english_text: The Ninth Hour, read daily before Vespers, is the seal of the services of the ecclesiastically closing day. If the day is a Feast of the Lord or of the Mother of God, a post-festal day, or the commemoration of a celebrated Saint, the Dismissal Troparion and Kontakion of the feast or of the Saint are said at this Hour. If not, the Troparion of the ordinary Saint of the day is said; and instead of a Kontakion, there is said: **"The thief, beholding the Author of life"** (*Βλέπων ὁ Λῃστὴς τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς*); *Glory...*, **"In the midst of two thieves"** (*Ἐν μέσῳ δύο λῃστῶν*); *Now and forever...*, **"The Lamb and Shepherd"** (*Τὸν Ἀμνὸν καὶ Ποιμένα*). On Saturday evening: Troparion **"Apostles, martyrs"** (*Ἀπόστολοι μάρτυρες*), and Kontakion **"As the first-fruits of nature"** (*Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως*). On Sunday evening: the Resurrection Troparion, and instead of a Kontakion, the Ypakoe of the Tone [Tone 1–8]. Throughout Bright Week and on the Saturday of Bright Week at evening before the Vespers of St. Thomas, as well as on Wednesday of the Apodosis of the Feast of Pascha at evening before the Vespers of the Ascension, the Paschal Ninth Hour is read, that is: **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), **"They who were with Mary came before the dawn"** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον*), etc., as set forth in the *Horologion* (*Ὡρολόγιον*). On the Tuesday evening of the Blind Man, before the Vespers of the Apodosis of Pascha, the ordinary three-psalm Ninth Hour is read, and there are said: the Troparion **"The Word, co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit"** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον*, Tone 5) and the Kontakion...

units.english_text: ...**"Blinded in the eyes of my soul"** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*). During Great Lent, the Ninth Hour is read as appointed in the *Horologion*, with the Beatitudes (*Μακαρισμοί*) and their concluding prayers. The dismissal at the Ninth Hour is always the Small Dismissal (see below, §16), together with the characteristic invocation of the feast whose Troparion and Kontakion were said.

units.slavonic_text: 40 Θεοῦ τυγχάνων³, ἀναγινώσκεται εἰς ἅπαντας τοὺς Ἑσπερινοὺς τοῦ ὅλου ἐνιαυτοῦ· ἀργεῖ δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Πάσχα (τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Ἀγάπης) καθ᾿ ὅλην τὴν Διακαινήσιμον ἑβδομάδα, ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῆς Ἀποδόσεως τοῦ Πάσχα. Ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Θωμᾶ μέχρι τῆς Ἀποδόσεως τοῦ Πάσχα, ἀναγινώσκεται μέν, ἀλλ᾿ ἄνευ τοῦ Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν, διότι ψάλλεται ἀντ᾿ αὐτοῦ τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἅπαξ ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος, καὶ δὶς ἐκ τῶν χορῶν. Ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τῆς Ἀναλήψεως καὶ ἐφεξῆς, συνάπτεται εἰς τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν τρὶς κατὰ τὸν τύπον τοῦ Ὡρολογίου.
units.english_text: ³ Ὅτι περὶ τῶν ψαλμῶν ἐν γένει καὶ τῶν τοῦ Δαβὶδ ἰδίᾳ ὁ χρυσοῦς τὴν γλῶτταν Ἰωάννης εἶπε, καλὸν θεωροῦμεν ἵνα ἐπισυνάψωμεν ἐνταῦθα πρὸς συχνὴν ἀνάγνωσιν καὶ μελέτην παντὸς χριστιανοῦ, μάλιστα δὲ τῶν κληρικῶν, οἷς ἐστιν ἐγχειρίδιον ἱερὸν τὸ Ψαλτήριον. «Τίνος ἕνεκεν ὁ ψαλμὸς εἰς τὸν βίον εἰσενήνεκται τὸν ἡμέτερον καὶ μετ᾿ ᾠδῆς μάλιστα αὕτη ἡ προφητεία λέγεται; . . . ἄκουσον. Πολλοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατιδὼν ὁ Θεὸς ῥᾳθυμοτέρους ὄντας καὶ πρὸς τὴν τῶν πνευματικῶν ἀνάγνωσιν δυσχερῶς ἔχοντας καὶ τὸν ἐκεῖθεν οὐχ ἡδέως ὑπομένοντας κάματον, ποθεινότερον ποιῆσαι τὸν πόνον βουλόμενος καὶ τοῦ καμάτου τὴν αἴσθησιν ὑποτεμέσθαι, μελῳδίαν ἀνέμιξε τῇ προφητείᾳ, ἵνα τῷ ῥυθμῷ τοῦ μέλους ψυχαγωγούμενοι πάντες μετὰ πολλῆς τῆς προθυμίας τοὺς ἱεροὺς ἀναπέμπωσιν αὐτῷ ὕμνους· οὐδὲν γὰρ οὐδὲν οὕτως ἀνίστησι ψυχὴν καὶ πτεροῖ καὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπαλλάττει καὶ τῶν τοῦ σώματος ἀπολύει δεσμῶν καὶ φιλοσοφεῖν ποιεῖ καὶ πάντων καταγελᾶν τῶν βιωτικῶν ὡς μέλος συμφωνίας καὶ ῥυθμῷ συγκείμενον θεῖον ᾆσμα. Οὕτω γοῦν ἡμῶν ἡ φύσις πρὸς τὰ ᾄσματα καὶ τὰ μέλη ἡδέως ἔχει καὶ οἰκείως, ὡς καὶ τὰ ὑπομάζια παιδία κλαυθμυριζόμενα καὶ δυσχεραίνοντα οὕτω κατακοιμίζεσθαι . . . Ποιοῦσι δὲ τοῦτο καὶ γυναῖκες καὶ ὁδοιπόροι καὶ γηπόνοι καὶ ναῦται, τῷ ᾄσματι τὸν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων πόνον παραμυθήσασθαι σπεύδοντες, ὡς τῆς ψυχῆς, εἰ μέλους ἀκούσειε τῆς ᾠδῆς, ῥᾷον ἅπαντα ἐνεγκεῖν δυναμένης τὰ ὀχληρὰ καὶ ἐπίπονα . . . Ἀπὸ τῶν ψαλμῶν τῶν πνευματικῶν πολὺ μὲν τὸ κέρδος, πολλὴ δὲ ἡ ὠφέλεια, πολὺς δὲ ὁ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ πάσης φιλοσοφίας ὑπόθεσις γένοιτ᾿ ἂν τῶν τε ῥημάτων τὴν ψυχὴν ἐκκαθαιρόντων, τοῦ τε ἁγίου Πνεύματος τῇ τὰ τοιαῦτα ψαλλούσῃ ταχέως ἐφιπταμένου ψυχῇ· οἱ γὰρ μετὰ συνέσεως ψάλλοντες τὴν τοῦ Πνεύματος καλοῦσι χάριν . . . Ἔνθα μὲν ᾄσματα πορνικὰ δαίμονες ἐπισωρεύονται, ἔνθα δὲ μέλη πνευματικὰ ἡ τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐφίπταται χάρις καὶ τὸ στόμα καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἁγιάζει . . . Καὶ καθάπερ πολλοὶ τῶν πλουτούντων τὴν σπογγίαν βαλσάμου πλήσαντες, οὕτω τὰς τραπέζας ἀπομάσσουσιν, ἵνα εἴ τις ἀπὸ τῶν αἰδεσμάτων γένηται κηλίς, παρασυρεῖσα καθαρὰν δείξῃ τὴν τράπεζαν, οὕτω δὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς ποιῶμεν, ἀντὶ βαλσάμου τὸ στόμα ἐμπλήσαντες μελῳδίας πνευματικῆς, ἵνα εἴ τις ἐγένετο κηλὶς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀδηφαγίας ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ, διὰ τῆς μελῳδίας ἀποσμήξωμεν ἐκείνης καὶ λέγωμεν κοινῇ στάντες· «Εὔφρανας ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐν τοῖς ποιήμασί σου . . .» Οὕτως οἱ τὸν Δαβὶδ καλοῦντες μετὰ τῆς κιθάρας, ἔνδον τὸν Χριστὸν δι᾿ αὐτοῦ καλοῦσιν. Ὅπου δὲ ὁ Χριστός, δαίμων μὲν οὐδεὶς ἐπεισελθεῖν, μᾶλλον δὲ οὐδὲ πρακύψαι τολμήσειέ ποτε, εἰρήνη δὲ καὶ ἀγάπη καὶ πάντα ὥσπερ ἐκ πηγῶν ἥξει τὰ ἀγαθά . . . Ἔνθα ψαλμὸς καὶ εὐχὴ καὶ προφητῶν χορεία καὶ διάνοια τῶν ᾀδόντων θεοφιλής, οὐκ ἄν τις ἁμάρτοι τὴν σύνοδον ταύτην προσειπὼν Ἐκκλησίαν. Κἂν μὴ εἰδῇς τὴν δύναμιν τῶν ῥημάτων, αὐτὸ τέως τὸ στόμα παίδευσον τὰ ῥήματα λέγειν· ἁγιάζεται γὰρ καὶ διὰ ῥημάτων ἡ γλῶττα ὅταν μετὰ προθυμίας ταῦτα λέγηται. Ἐὰν εἰς ταύτην ἑαυτοὺς καταστήσωμεν τὴν συνήθειαν, οὐδὲ ἑκόντες οὐδὲ ῥᾳθυμοῦντές ποτε ποιησόμεθα τὴν καλὴν ταύτην λειτουργίαν, τοῦ ἔθους καὶ ἄκοντας ἡμᾶς ἀναγκάζοντος καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν τὴν καλὴν ταύτην ἐπιτελεῖν λατρείαν.» (Χρυσόστ. Ἑρμ. εἰς τὸν ψαλμὸν ΜΑ ἔκδ. Migne τόμ. 55).

units.slavonic_text: 41 doxology to God, 3. is read at all Vespers of the year; it is omitted, however, from the Vespers of Easter Sunday {also known as the Vespers of Agapi} and during all of Bright Week, as well as the Vespers of the Leave-taking of Easter. From the Vespers of the Sunday of Thomas until the Leave-taking of Easter, the Introductory Psalm is read, however without “O come let us worship” since, in its place, “Christ is risen” is sung, once by the Clergy from within the Sanctuary and twice by the Choirs. Beginning with the Vespers of the Ascension, and thereafter, “O come let us worship” (repeated three times) is again added to the Introductory Psalm as prescribed in the Orologion.

units.slavonic_text: 3. That concerning the psalms in general and those of David in particular which the golden tongued John said, we deem it beneficial to append here towards continual reading and study by every Christian, especially the clergy, for whom the Psalter is a sacred handbook: All that John Chrysostom said regarding the Psalms in general and, specifically, on the Psalms of David, we deem worthy to be mentioned here so that it may be frequently read and studied by every Christian and especially the clergy, to whom the sacred Psalter is a worthy handbook. “For what reason was the psalm introduced by our Church for daily use and why is the prophecy said with melody?....Listen. When God saw that many men were rather indolent, that they came unwillingly to Scriptural readings and did not endure the labor this involves, wishing to make the labor more grateful and to take away the sensation of it, He blended melody with prophecy in order that, delighted by the modulation of the chant, all might with great eagerness give forth sacred hymns to Him. For nothing so uplifts the mind, giving it wings and freeing it from the earth, releasing it from the chains of the body, affecting it with love of wisdom, and causing it to scorn all things pertaining to this life, as modulated melody and the divine chant composed of number. To such an extent, indeed, is our nature delighted by chants and songs that even infants at the breast, if they be weeping or afflicted, are by reason of it lulled to sleep.... This they do, the women, travelers, peasants, and sailors, striving to lighten with a chant the labor endured in working, for the mind suffers hardships and difficulties more easily when it hears songs and chants.... From the spiritual psalms, however, proceeds much of value, much utility, much sanctity, and every inducement to philosophy, for the words purify the mind and the Holy Spirit descends swiftly upon the mind of the singer. For those who sing with understanding invoke the grace of the Spirit.... Demons congregate where there are licentious chants, but where there are spiritual ones there the grace of the Spirit descends, sanctifying mouth and mind.... And just as not a few wealthy persons wipe off their tables with a sponge filled with balsam, so that if any stain remain from the food, they may remove it and show a clean table; so should we also, filling our mouths with spiritual melody instead of balsam, so that if any stain remain in our mind from the abundance, we may thereby wipe it away. And all standing, let us say together: 'For Thou, O Lord, hast made me glad through Thy work....' So those who invoke David with his lyre call inwardly on Christ. Where Christ is, let no demon enter; let him not even dare to look in passing. Peace, delight, and all good things flow here as from fountains.... For where there are psalms, and prayers, and the dance of the prophets, and singers with pious intentions, no one will err if he call the assembly a Church. Even though the meaning of the words be unknown to you, teach your mouth to utter them meanwhile. For the tongue is made holy by the words when they are uttered with a ready and eager mind. Once we have acquired this habit, neither through free will nor through carelessness shall we neglect our beautiful office; custom compelling us, even against our will, to carry out daily worship.” (St. John Chrysostom, Interpretation on Psalm 41. Edition Migne vol. 55.)
units.english_text: «For what reason was the psalm introduced into our life, and why is this prophecy uttered especially with song?... Listen. When God saw that many men were rather indolent, that they came unwillingly to spiritual reading and did not readily endure the labor it involves, wishing to make the labor more desirable and to alleviate the sense of toil, He blended melody with prophecy, in order that, delighted by the rhythm of the chant, all might with great eagerness offer up sacred hymns to Him. For nothing so uplifts the soul, giving it wings, freeing it from the earth, delivering it from the bonds of the body, inclining it toward the love of wisdom, and causing it to look down upon all earthly concerns, as harmonized song and divine melody composed in meter. To such an extent, indeed, is our nature drawn to songs and chants that even nursing infants, when weeping and distressed, are lulled to sleep thereby.... This also do women, travelers, laborers, and sailors, hastening to comfort the toil of their labors with song, knowing that if the soul hears a melodious chant, it is able more easily to bear all grievous and burdensome things.... From spiritual psalms, great is the profit, abundant the benefit, profound the sanctification, and a foundation for all true philosophy is established, both as the words purify the soul and as the Holy Spirit swiftly descends upon the soul that chants such hymns. For those who chant with understanding invoke the grace of the Spirit.... Where licentious songs are sung, demons congregate; but where spiritual songs resound, the grace of the Spirit alights, sanctifying both mouth and soul.... And just as many wealthy persons, filling a sponge with balsam, wipe their tables clean, so that if any stain remain from the food, it may be wiped away and leave the table clean; so let us also do, filling our mouth with spiritual melody instead of balsam, so that if any stain has arisen in the soul from gluttony, we may wipe it away through that melody, and standing together let us say: **"Thou, O Lord, hast made me glad through Thy deeds..."** [Psalm 91:5 LXX]. Thus those who summon David with his harp summon Christ through him within themselves. And where Christ is present, no demon dares to enter, nor even to look in passing; but peace, love, and all good things flow forth as from fountains.... Where there is a psalm, and prayer, and the choir of prophets, and a mind pleasing to God among the singers, one would not err in calling such a gathering a Church. Even if you do not understand the inner power of the words, nevertheless teach your mouth to speak the words; for the tongue is sanctified by the holy words when they are uttered with a willing mind. If we establish ourselves in this habit, neither deliberately nor through carelessness will we ever neglect this beautiful ministry, custom compelling us even against our will to perform this noble worship daily.» (St. John Chrysostom, *Homily on Psalm 41*, Migne, *PG*, vol. 55).

units.english_text: **4.** Κατὰ πᾶν Σάββατον ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ στιχολογεῖται τὸ Α΄ Κάθισμα τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου, καὶ Θεομητορικῆς ἑορτῆς τυχούσης, ἢ μνήμης ἑορταζομένου Ἁγίου. Οὐ στιχολογεῖται δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἐφεξῆς Δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς καὶ ἂν ἔτι συμπέσωσιν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῇ, ἤτοι τῇ ἑορτῇ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως, τῇ τῶν Θεοφανίων καὶ τῆς Μεταμορφώσεως, ἐν αἷς οὐδὲ Ἀναστάσιμα ψάλλονται· ἐπίσης οὐ στιχολογεῖται καὶ ἐν τῇ Κυριακῇ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, ὡς οὐδὲ ἐν ταῖς μεθεόρτοις Ἑσπερινοῖς τῶν Χριστουγέννων καὶ τῶν Θεοφανίων, ὅταν αἱ ἑορταὶ αὗται συμπέσωσιν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Σαββάτου, προηγοῦνται ὅμως ἐν τούτοις τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα στιχηρά. Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἐφεξῆς Δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς, ἤτοι τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Βαΐων, τῇ Κυριακῇ τοῦ Θωμᾶ καὶ τῇ ἑορτῇ τῆς Ὑψώσεως τοῦ Σταυροῦ (ὅταν τύχῃ αὕτη ἐν Κυριακῇ), τὸ μὲν Ψαλτήριον στιχολογεῖται, ἀλλὰ τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα καταλιμπάνονται.

units.english_text: **4.** At every Saturday Vespers, the First Kathisma of the Psalter [Psalms 1–8 LXX] is chanted,[^59] even if a Feast of the Mother of God or the commemoration of a celebrated Saint occurs. It is not chanted, however, on the following Feasts of the Lord (even if they should occur on a Sunday): the Feast of the Nativity of Christ, Theophany, and the Transfiguration, at which none of the Resurrection hymns are sung; likewise, it is not chanted on Pentecost Sunday, nor at the post-festal Vespers of Christmas and Theophany when these Feasts fall on a Saturday (although at these Vespers the Resurrection Stichera take precedence). On the following Feasts of the Lord—namely, Palm Sunday, the Sunday of St. Thomas, and the Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross (when it falls on a Sunday)—the Psalter is chanted, but the Resurrection hymns are omitted.

units.slavonic_text: 4. At every Saturday Vespers, the First Kathisma of the Psalter is chanted, even if it is a Feast of the Theotokos or the commemoration of a celebrating Saint. It is not chanted, however, on the following Feasts of the Lord (even if they should occur on a Sunday): Christmas, Epiphany, and the Transfiguration at which [Feasts] none of the Resurrection Hymns are sung; also it is not chanted on the Sunday of Pentecost, as well as the Post-feast Vespers of Christmas and Epiphany. However, when these Feasts fall on Saturday, the Resurrection Hymns precede the hymns of the Post-feast. On the following Feasts of the Lord — Palm Sunday, Sunday of Thomas, and the Feast of the Elevation of the Holy Cross (when it falls on a Sunday) — the Psalter is chanted but the Resurrection Hymns are omitted.

units.slavonic_text: St Basil the Great says: “He blended the delight of melody with doctrines in order that through the pleasantness and softness of the sound we might unawares receive what was useful in the words, according to the practice of the wise physicians, who, when they give the more bitter medicines to the sick, often smear the rim of the cup with honey.... A psalm is the tranquility of souls, the arbitrator of peace, restraining the disorder and turbulence of thoughts.... A psalm forms friendships, unites the divided, mediates between enemies; to children it is safety, to men in their prime an adornment, to the old a solace, to women their most fitting ornament, respite from daily toil, the voice of the Church” (St Basil the Great, Homily on Psalm 1). Theodoret of Cyrus: “Divine grace, having mingled benefit with the sweetness of the melody it made divine teaching thrice-desirable and most beloved.” Gregory of Nyssa: “Since that which is natural is agreeable to our nature and it has been proven that music is inherent to our nature, for this reason, David the great mixed music with philosophy regarding the virtues, as if having poured sweet honey on divine doctrine.” These are the reasons that our holy Church holds the Psalms of David as the foundation of certain individual and public prayers and by which in ancient times all the Psalms were chanted as today we chant Psalms 140, 141 and others.

units.slavonic_text: 45 Presentation of the Lord and the Annunciation)⁴ and at the Commemorations of celebrating Saints occurring during the four days of the week {i.e. Tuesday through Friday} in the Vespers, the First Stasis of the Psalter is chanted, that is the first three psalms. It is not chanted when these Feasts fall either on a Saturday or a Monday, because in the Vespers of these two days chanting of the Psalter is not done.
units.english_text: **6.** In daily Vespers, the verses of Psalms 140, 141, 129, and 116 LXX—namely, **"Lord, I have cried unto Thee, hear me"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*),[^62] **"I cried unto the Lord with my voice"** (*Φωνῇ μου πρὸς Κύριον*), **"Out of the depths have I cried unto Thee, O Lord"** (*Ἐκ βαθέων ἐκέκραξά σοι*), and **"Praise the Lord, all ye nations"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*)—are chanted in full in the appointed Tones [Tone 1–8]. In the Vespers of Great Feasts, it is customary for the sake of brevity to omit the verses beginning from **"Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth"** (*Θοῦ, Κύριε, φυλακήν*) and onward, and for the First Choir to pass directly to the verse appropriate to the appointed number of the subsequent Stichera [10, 8, or 6].

units.english_text: **7.** At every Saturday Vespers before Sunday, and at every Sunday Matins throughout the entire year, the Resurrection hymns of the Octoechos are chanted without fail—namely: Stichera, Doxastika, Dismissal Troparia, Triadika, Kathismata, Ypakoe, Antiphons, Canons, Kontakia, Ikoses, Exapostilaria, Eothina Gospels, Beatitudes, etc.[^63] These take precedence over the services of the Feasts of the Mother of God and their Apodoses (Leave-takings), as well as over the Apodoses of Feasts of the Lord, post-festal Sundays, and commemorations of Saints when they fall on a Sunday. units.english_text: ...τῶν μεθεόρτων Κυριακῶν, καὶ τῶν ἑορταζομένων Ἁγίων, ὅταν συμπίπτωσιν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῇ. Ψάλλονται δὲ οὕτως· ἐν μὲν ταῖς κυρίαις τῶν ἑορτῶν ἡμέραις καὶ ταῖς τῶν Ἀποδόσεων αὐτῶν, πρῶτον ἑσπέρια Στιχηρὰ Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄, εἶτα ς΄ τῆς τυχούσης Θεομητορικῆς ἑορτῆς· ἐν δὲ ταῖς μεθεόρτοις Κυριακαῖς καὶ πάσαις ταῖς τῶν ἑορταζομένων Ἁγίων μνήμαις, Ἀναστάσιμα ς΄ καὶ μεθέορτα ἢ τοῦ Ἁγίου δ΄. Ὅταν δὲ συμπίπτῃ ἐν μεθεόρτῳ Κυριακῇ ἢ ἐν τῇ Ἀποδόσει Δεσποτικῆς ἢ Θεομητορικῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ἑορταζόμενος Ἅγιος, τότε ψάλλονται Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄, τῆς ἑορτῆς γ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου γ΄. Ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἐφεξῆς Ἁγίων ἑορταῖς ἤτοι, τῇ ἑορτῇ τῶν Ἀρχαγγέλων, τοῦ Γενεσίου τοῦ Προδρόμου, τῶν Κορυφαίων Ἀποστόλων Πέτρου καὶ Παύλου, τοῦ Εὐαγγελιστοῦ Ἰωάννου (Σεπτεμβρίου κς΄), τῶν Τριῶν Ἱεραρχῶν (ἂν μὴ συμπίπτῃ ἡ ἑορτὴ αὐτῶν ἔν τινι Κυριακῇ Τριῳδίου), τῶν Ἁγίων Πατέρων τῆς Δ΄ καὶ Ζ΄ Συνόδου, καὶ τῶν Ἁγίων Δημητρίου καὶ Νικολάου, ψάλλονται κατ᾿ ἐξαίρεσιν Ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῶν Ἁγίων ς΄. Ὅταν δὲ ὁ τυχὼν ἐν Κυριακῇ Ἅγιος στερῆται Δοξαστικοῦ, ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ ψάλλονται Ἀναστάσιμα ζ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου γ΄. Καταλιμπάνονται δὲ ἅπαντα τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα ἐν ταῖς ἑξῆς Μ. Δεσποτικαῖς ἑορταῖς, ἤτοι τῇ ἑορτῇ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως, τῶν Θεοφανίων, τῶν Βαΐων, τοῦ Θωμᾶ, τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, τῆς Μεταμορφώσεως, τῆς Ὑψώσεως τοῦ Σταυροῦ, καὶ τῇ Κυριακῇ πρὸ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως, ὅταν συμπίπτῃ τῇ κδ΄ τοῦ Δεκεμβρίου, ὅτε ὅμως ψάλλεται ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ μετὰ τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, καὶ ἐν τῇ Λειτουργίᾳ μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ τυχόντος ἤχου, ὡς καὶ τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον, καὶ δ΄ τῶν Αἴνων Ἀναστάσιμα.

units.english_text: ...of Afterfeast Sundays and celebrated Saints, whenever they coincide on a Sunday.[^64] They are chanted as follows: on the principal days of the feasts and on their Apodoses: first 4 evening Resurrection Stichera, then 6 of the occurring Feast of the Mother of God; on Afterfeast Sundays and all commemorations of celebrated Saints: 6 Resurrection Stichera and 4 afterfeast or of the Saint. But whenever a celebrated Saint coincides on an Afterfeast Sunday or on the Apodosis of a Feast of the Lord or of the Mother of God, then 4 Resurrection Stichera, 3 of the feast, and 3 of the Saint are chanted. On the feasts of the following Saints, namely: the Feast of the Archangels [November 8], the Nativity of the Forerunner [June 24], the Prime Apostles Peter and Paul [June 29], the Evangelist John (September 26), the Three Hierarchs [January 30] (unless their feast coincides on a Sunday of the Triodion), the Holy Fathers of the Fourth [July 13–19] and Seventh [October 11–18] Ecumenical Councils, and Saints Demetrius [October 26] and Nicholas [December 6], by exception 4 Resurrection Stichera and 6 of the Saints are chanted. When the Saint occurring on Sunday lacks a Doxastikon, at Vespers 7 Resurrection Stichera and 3 of the Saint are chanted. All the Resurrection hymns are omitted on the following Great Feasts of the Lord, namely: the Feast of the Nativity of Christ, Theophany, Palm Sunday, St. Thomas Sunday, Pentecost, the Transfiguration, the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, and the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ when it coincides on December 24, on which day, however, at Matins after **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*), and at the Divine Liturgy after the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion of the occurring Tone [Tone 1–8] is chanted, as well as the Exaposteilarion, and 4 Resurrection Stichera of the Praises (*Ainoi*).

units.slavonic_text: 47 on the day of the Feast and the Leave-taking, first 4 Resurrection Stichira, then 6 of the feast of the Theotokos; on Post-feast Sundays and all commemorations of Saints, 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 Stichira of the Post-feast or of the Saint. When a Saint's commemoration occurs on a Sunday of a Post-feast or on the Leave-taking of a Feast of the Lord or Theotokos then, we chant 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 Stichira of the feast, and 3 Stichira of the Saint. On the commemorations of the following Saints: The Archangels [November 8], the Nativity of the Forerunner [June 24], the Apostles Peter and Paul [June 29], the Evangelist John (September 26), the Three Hierarchs [January 30] (if it does not fall on a Sunday of the Triodion), the Holy Fathers of the 4th [July 13 - 19] and 7th [October 11 - 18] Synods, and Saints Demetrios [October 26] and Nicholas [December 6] the following order is used: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 6 Stichira of the Saint. When the Saint whose commemoration occurs on a Sunday does not have a Doxastikon, then 7 Resurrection Stichira are sung and 3 of the Saint. All of the Resurrection Hymns are omitted on the following Feasts of the Lord, that is, Christmas, Epiphany, Palm Sunday, Sunday of Thomas, Pentecost, Transfiguration, Elevation of the Holy Cross and the Sunday before Christmas, when it occurs on December 24th, in which case, in the Matins after “God is the Lord,” and in the Liturgy, after the Entrance, the Apolytikion of the Mode is sung. In Matins we also sing the Exapostilarion and the 4 Resurrection Stichira of the Praises.

units.english_text: ...first four Sundays of the Triodion: for *Glory...*, that of the Triodion is chanted; for *Now and forever...*, that of the feast. When the Feast of the Annunciation coincides on the Third Sunday of Great Lent, on Lazarus Saturday, or on Easter Sunday: the Doxastikon of the Triodion or Pentecostarion is chanted first; for *Now and forever...*, that of the feast. If, however, it coincides on Palm Sunday or on Bright Monday, for *Glory...*, *Now and forever...*, only that of the feast is said. When the feasts of Saints George [April 23], John the Theologian (May 8), and Constantine and Helen [May 21] occur on any Sunday of the Pentecostarion, or on a Feast of the Lord (with the exception of Pentecost Sunday): for *Glory...*, that of the Saints is chanted; for *Now and forever...*, that of the occurring Sunday or feast. If the Saint occurring on Sunday lacks a Doxastikon, for *Glory...*, *Now and forever...*, the Theotokion of the Tone is chanted. But if he is a great martyr and coincides on an Afterfeast Sunday of a Feast of the Lord or of the Mother of God: for *Glory...*, that of the Saint is chanted; for *Now and forever...*, the first Theotokion of the Tone (Dogmatikon) [Tone 1–8].

units.slavonic_text: 49 Triodion, the Doxastikon of the Triodion, then Now and ever of the Feast. When the Feast of the Annunciation occurs on the Third Sunday of Lent, on the Saturday of Lazarus, or on the Sunday of Easter, the Doxastikon of the Triodion or Pentikostarion is chanted first, then Now and ever of the Feast. If, however, the Feast of the Annunciation occurs on Palm Sunday or Monday of Bright Week, Glory, Now and ever of the Feast only is said. When the Feasts of Saint George [April 23], John the Theologian (May 8) and Constantine and Helen [May 21] occur on any Sunday of the Pentikostarion, or a Feast of the Lord (with the exception of the Feast of Pentecost), the Doxastikon of the Saint is sung, then Now and ever of the particular Sunday or feast. If the Saint whose commemoration occurs on a Sunday does not have a Doxastikon at Vespers, we sing Glory, Now and ever, with the First Theotokion of the Mode. If the Saint being commemorated is a great martyr and his feast occurs on a Post-feast of the Lord or the Theotokos, then we sing the Doxastikon of the Saint, Now and ever the first Theotokion of the Mode.
units.english_text: **9.** At Saturday Vespers, even if Feasts of the Mother of God or of the Lord occur (with the exception of the two feasts of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany), the Prokimenon chanted is **"The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty"** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν*, Psalm 92:1 LXX);[^66] except for the afterfeast Vespers of Great Feasts of the Lord falling on a Saturday, or on any other day of the week, at which are always chanted the Great Prokimena: **"Who is a god as great as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders"** (*Τίς θεὸς μέγας ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν; σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια*, Psalm 76:14 LXX) and **"Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He willed, He hath done"** (*Ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐν τῇ γῇ, πάντα ὅσα ἠθέλησεν ἐποίησεν*, Psalm 113:11 LXX), with their verses. At the Vespers of Holy Saturday, after the reading of the Apostle (Epistle), the Prokimenon **"Arise, O God, judge the earth"** (*Ἀνάστα ὁ Θεός, κρῖνον τὴν γῆν*, Psalm 81:8 LXX) is chanted with its appointed verses.

units.english_text: **11.** Ἄν ὑπάρχῃ Ἀρτοκλασία, μετὰ τὴν ἐκφώνησιν Εἴη τὸ κράτος τῆς βασιλείας σου, ψάλλεται ὑπὸ τοῦ β΄ χοροῦ ἓν κατ᾿ ἐκλογὴν Στιχηρὸν ἐκ τῆς Λιτῆς, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μεταξὺ ἐξέρχεται ἀπὸ τοῦ βορείου κλίτους ὁ Διάκονος καὶ ὁ Ἱερεὺς καὶ ἔρχονται φέροντες εἰς χεῖρας λαμπάδας, καὶ ἵστανται ἐν τῷ μέσῳ τοῦ ναοῦ, ὅπου εἰσὶ προτεθειμένοι οἱ ἄρτοι, οἶνος καὶ ἔλαιον· ὁ Διάκονος τότε λέγει τὸ Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός... Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκκλησίαν ταύτην, τὴν πόλιν (ἢ χώραν) ταύτην κτλ., οἱ χοροὶ ψάλλουσιν εὐλαβῶς καὶ πραείᾳ τῇ φωνῇ τὸ Κύριε ἐλέησον ὡς ἡ τάξις· ὁ Ἱερεὺς Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός... Μ. Προκείμενα ψάλλονται ὡσαύτως καὶ ἐν τοῖς Ἑσπερινοῖς τῆς Διακαινησίμου ἑβδομάδος, ὡς διατυποῦνται ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ. Εἰρήνη πᾶσι· ὁ Χορὸς Καὶ τῷ πνεύματί σου· ὁ Διάκονος Τὰς κεφαλὰς ἡμῶν... ὁ χορὸς Σοὶ Κύριε· ὁ Ἱερεὺς (ἢ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς) Δέσποτα Πολυέλεε... εἶτα ὁ Ἱερεὺς θυμιᾷ σταυροειδῶς στρεφόμενος περὶ τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ψάλλων τὸ Θεοτόκε Παρθένε... Ἐν πάσαις ἀνεξαιρέτως ταῖς Δεσποτικαῖς καὶ Θεομητορικαῖς ἑορταῖς ὡς καὶ ἐν ταῖς τῶν Ἁγίων μνήμαις, ἐὰν γίνηται Ἀρτοκλασία, ψάλλεται πάντοτε τὸ Θεοτόκε Παρθένε. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐν τῇ Διακαινησίμῳ ἑβδομάδι, ἀντὶ τοῦ Θεοτόκε Παρθένε ψάλλεται τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη. Τούτου πληρωθέντος, λέγει ὁ Διάκονος Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν· ὁ χορὸς Κύριε ἐλέησον· ὁ Ἱερεὺς εὐλογεῖ τοὺς ἄρτους, λέγων τὴν εὐχὴν Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν... εἶτα ψάλλεται τρὶς τὸ Πλούσιοι ἐπτώχευσαν, καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτὸ τὰ Ἀπόστιχα.

units.slavonic_text: 51 Commemoration of a celebrating Saint. Before the reading the Deacon exclaims “Wisdom! Let us be attentive!” The Apostolos Selections, which are read on the Feasts of the Apostles Peter and Paul [June 29], John the Theologian [May 8], James the Brother of the Lord [October 23], and Andrew the First-called [November 30] are customarily read in the same manner of delivery as the Apostolos selections [e.g. the Epistles of Paul] in the Liturgy, and the Deacon exclaims “Let us be attentive! Wisdom! Let us be attentive!”
units.english_text: **11.** If an Artoklasia (Blessing of the Loaves) is held,[^68] after the exclamation **"Blessed and glorified be the majesty of Thy kingdom..."** (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος τῆς βασιλείας σου...*), a chosen Sticheron from the Litiya is chanted by the Second Choir; meanwhile, the Deacon and the Priest exit through the north door [of the iconostasis] holding candles in their hands, and stand in the middle of the temple before the Tetrapod, where the loaves, wheat, wine, and oil have been prepared. The Deacon then intones the litany: **"Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy..."** (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός...*), **"Again we pray for the preservation of this holy temple, this city (or village)..."** (*Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκκλησίαν ταύτην...*), etc. The choirs chant **"Lord, have mercy"** reverently and in a subdued voice as the rubrics appoint. The Priest intones: **"Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth..."** (*Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός...*). (Great Prokimena are likewise chanted at the Vespers of Bright Week, as set forth in the Pentecostarion). The Priest: **"Peace be to all."** Choir: **"And to thy spirit."** Deacon: **"Let us bow our heads unto the Lord."** Choir: **"To Thee, O Lord."** The Priest (or the Hierarch): **"O Master, abundant in mercy..."** (*Δέσποτα Πολυέλεε...*). Then the Priest censes crosswise, circling the Tetrapod with the loaves and chanting: **"O Mother of God and Virgin, rejoice, Mary full of grace, the Lord is with thee; blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, for thou hast borne the Savior of our souls"** (*Θεοτόκε Παρθένε...*). On all Feasts of the Lord and of the Mother of God without exception, as well as on commemorations of Saints, if an Artoklasia is held, **"O Mother of God and Virgin"** is always chanted. But throughout Bright Week, instead of **"O Mother of God and Virgin,"** **"Christ is risen from the dead"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) is chanted. This being completed, the Deacon says: **"Let us pray to the Lord."** Choir: **"Lord, have mercy."** The Priest blesses the loaves, reciting the prayer: **"O Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who didst bless the five loaves in the wilderness and therewith feed five thousand..."** (*Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*). Then **"The rich have become poor and gone hungry, but they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing"** (*Πλούσιοι ἐπτώχευσαν*, Psalm 33:11 LXX) is chanted thrice, and after it, the Aposticha.

Ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τοῦ Σαββάτου τῶν τεσσάρων μετὰ τὴν Κυριακὴν τοῦ Θωμᾶ Κυριακῶν ψάλλεται ἐν πρώτοις τὸ τοῦ ἤχου πρῶτον Ἀπόστιχον (ὅπερ ἄρχεται ἀπὸ τοῦ α΄ χοροῦ), εἶτα ψάλλονται τὰ δ΄ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερὸν μετὰ τῶν στίχων αὐτῶν.
units.english_text: **13.** Ἐν ταῖς συμπιπτούσαις ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῇ Θεομητορικαῖς ἑορταῖς, ταῖς μεθεόρτοις Κυριακαῖς αὐτῶν τε καὶ τῶν Δεσποτικῶν ἑορτῶν καὶ τῶν προεορτίων αὐτῶν ὡς καὶ τῶν Ἀποδόσεων αὐτῶν, τῇ Γ΄ Κυριακῇ τῶν Νηστειῶν, τῇ Κυριακῇ τῶν Μυροφόρων, τῇ ἑορτῇ τῶν Θεοπατόρων Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννης καὶ τῇ τῶν Ταξιαρχῶν (ὅταν συμπίπτωσιν ἐν Κυριακῇ) Δοξαστικὸν τῶν Ἀποστίχων ψάλλεται μόνον τὸ τῆς τυχούσης ἑορτῆς ἄνευ θεοτοκίου. Ὅταν ἡ ἑορτὴ τῆς Ὑπαπαντῆς καὶ ἡ Ἀπόδοσις αὐτῆς συμπίπτῃ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν τεσσάρων πρώτων Κυριακῶν τοῦ Τριῳδίου, ψάλλεται Δόξα τὸ τῶν Ἀποστίχων τοῦ Τριῳδίου, Καὶ νῦν τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Καὶ ἡ τοῦ Εὐαγγελισμοῦ ἑορτὴ ὅταν συμπίπτῃ τῇ Γ΄ Κυριακῇ τῶν Νηστειῶν ἢ τῇ τῶν Βαΐων, ψάλλονται τὰ τοῦ Τριῳδίου Ἀπόστιχα, Δοξαστικά, Καὶ νῦν τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς· ἐὰν δὲ συμπέσῃ τῷ Πάσχα, τότε ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ λέγεται Δόξα τῆς ἑορτῆς, Καὶ νῦν Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα. Ἐν ταῖς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῆς συμπιπτούσαις Ἁγίου μνήμαις, Δόξα τῶν Ἀποστίχων ψάλλεται τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, Καὶ νῦν θεοτοκίον ἐκ τῆς Ὀκτωήχου σύμφωνον τῷ ἤχῳ τοῦ Δοξαστικοῦ. Ὅταν δὲ αἱ τῶν ἑορταζομένων Ἁγίων μνῆμαι συμπίπτωσιν ἐν μεθεόρτῳ Κυριακῇ, ἢ Ἀποδόσει Δεσποτικῆς τινος ἢ Θεομητορικῆς ἑορτῆς, Δόξα Ἀπόστιχον ψάλλεται τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου, Καὶ νῦν τὸ τῆς τυχούσης ἑορτῆς. Τοῦ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῆς τυχόντος Ἁγίου μὴ ἔχοντος εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα Δοξαστικόν, Δόξα Καὶ νῦν ψάλλεται τὸ τῶν Ἀποστίχων θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου.

units.slavonic_text: 53 omitted even if it is a Feast of the Theotokos, Pre-feast or Post-feast Sundays and Leave-takings of Feasts of either the Lord or the Theotokos, or commemorations of celebrating Saints. In the Saturday Vespers of the four Sundays following the Sunday of Thomas, the first Apostichon of the Mode is sung by the First Choir, followed by the four Stichira “A sacred Pascha” with their verses.
units.english_text: **13.** On Feasts of the Mother of God coinciding on Sunday, on their Afterfeast Sundays, on Feasts of the Lord and their Forefeasts and their Apodoses, on the Third Sunday of Great Lent [Veneration of the Precious Cross], on the Sunday of the Myrrh-Bearers, on the feast of the Holy Ancestors of God Joachim and Anna [September 9], and on the Archangels [November 8 (when it falls on Sunday)], only the Doxastikon of the Aposticha of the occurring feast is chanted, without a Theotokion.[^70] When the Feast of the Meeting of the Lord or its Apodosis coincides on one of the first four Sundays of the Triodion: for *Glory...*, that of the Aposticha of the Triodion is chanted; for *Now and forever...*, that of the feast. When the Feast of the Annunciation coincides on the Third Sunday of Great Lent or on Palm Sunday: the Aposticha and Doxastikon of the Triodion are chanted; for *Now and forever...*, that of the feast. If it coincides on Pascha Sunday, then at Vespers: *Glory...*, of the feast; *Now and forever...*, **"It is the day of Resurrection"** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). On commemorations of Saints occurring on a Sunday: for *Glory...* of the Aposticha, that of the Saint is chanted; for *Now and forever...*, the Theotokion from the Octoechos in the same Tone [Tone 1–8] as the Doxastikon of the Saint. But when the commemorations of celebrated Saints coincide on an Afterfeast Sunday or on the Apodosis of a Feast of the Lord or of the Mother of God: for *Glory...* of the Aposticha, that of the Saint is chanted; for *Now and forever...*, that of the occurring feast. If the Saint occurring on Sunday has no Doxastikon at the Aposticha, for *Glory...*, *Now and forever...*, the Theotokion of the Aposticha of the Tone is chanted.

units.english_text: **14.** Daily at Vespers before the Dismissal, **"Now let Your servant depart in peace, O Master, according to Thy word"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*, Luke 2:29–32) is said with the Trisagion Prayers.[^71] But throughout Bright Week and at the Vespers of the Apodosis of Pascha, after **"It is the day of Resurrection,"** instead of the Trisagion Prayers, **"Christ is risen from the dead"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) is chanted thrice according to its customary melody (and not according to the melody of **"It is the day of Resurrection"**), and the Dismissal immediately follows.

units.english_text: **15.** At Saturday Vespers, the Resurrection Dismissal Troparia of the Octoechos are chanted before the Dismissal Troparia of Feasts of the Mother of God coinciding on Sunday, of Afterfeast Sundays, and of the Apodoses of Feasts of the Lord and of the Mother of God.[^72] They are chanted as follows: on the principal Feasts of the Mother of God and on their Apodoses: the Resurrection Troparion once, and that of the feast twice. On Afterfeast Sundays: both the Resurrection Troparion and that of the feast once; but at Matins, the Resurrection Troparion is said twice and that of the feast once. If the Feast of the Annunciation coincides on the Third Sunday of Great Lent, there are chanted: first the Resurrection Troparion, second that of the Cross, and third that of the feast; on Lazarus Saturday: that of the feast twice, and that of Lazarus once; on Palm Sunday: that of the feast, that of Lazarus, and again that of the feast. On Forefeast Sundays of Feasts of the Lord and of the Mother of God, at evening the Resurrection Troparion and the Forefeast Troparion are chanted once each; but in the morning at **"God is the Lord,"** the first is doubled. When the commemoration of a celebrated Saint occurs on an Afterfeast Sunday or on the Apodosis of a Feast of the Lord or of the Mother of God, there are chanted: first the Resurrection Troparion, then that of the Saint, and last that of the occurring feast. When a Saint lacking a Doxastikon occurs at Saturday Vespers...
