units.english_text: ... Dismissal Troparion: **"Buried with Thee through Baptism, O Christ our God..."** (*Συνταφέντες σοι*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers [**"In confirming the common Resurrection..."** twice, "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Buried with Thee through Baptism..."** once]. Then the Psalter [Kathisma 2, Pss. 9–16 LXX, and Kathisma 3, Pss. 17–23 LXX] and the Polyeleos [Kathisma 19, Pss. 134–135 LXX]. The Sessional Hymns [Kathismata] in order from the Triodion: after the first Kathisma: **"In spirit carrying branches, with cleansed souls let us praise Christ in faith like children..."** (*Μετὰ κλάδων νοητῶς*) and another Sessional Hymn: **"Thou didst raise Lazarus from the tomb after four days, O Lord..."** (*Τετραήμερον ἤγειρας*); after the second Kathisma: **"O Christ our Savior, Thou didst shed tears in secret over Thy friend Lazarus lying dead..."** (*Δάκρυα προέχεας, Σωτήρ*) and **"O ye peoples and nations, rejoice together!..."** (*Λαοὶ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη συνευφράνθητε*). After the Polyeleos: the festal Sessional Hymn: **"He Who sits upon the throne of the Cherubim, for our sake sits upon a foal..."** (*Ὁ ἐπὶ θρόνου Χερουβίμ*) twice. The First Antiphon of the Hymns of Ascent [Anavathmoi] of Tone 4: **"From my youth up many passions have warred against me..."** (*Ἐκ νεότητός μου*). The Prokimenon: **"Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings hast Thou perfected praise"** (*Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον*, Ps. 8:2 [LXX]); verse: **"O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is Thy name in all the earth!"** (*Κύριε ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν, ὡς θαυμαστὸν τὸ ὄνομά σου*, Ps. 8:1 [LXX]). **"Let every breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*), and the Matins Gospel: Matthew 21:1–11, 15–17 (The Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem and the Children in the Temple). We do not chant **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"**, but immediately Psalm 50 is read plain [chyma]. "Glory...": **"Today Christ entereth the city of Bethany..."** (*Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς εἰσέρχεται ἐν πόλει Βηθανίᾳ*); "Both now and ever...": the same; then the verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy..."** (Ps. 50:1 [LXX]), and the Idiomelon: **"Today the grace of the Holy Spirit hath gathered us together..."** (*Σήμερον ἡ χάρις τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος*). The Canon: **"The springs of the deep appeared dry..."** (*Ὤφθησαν αἱ πηγαὶ τῆς ἀβύσσου*) in six without verses, except "Glory... Both now and ever..." at the last two Troparia. After the Third Ode, the Hypakoe: **"Praising with branches, first the peoples cried aloud with hymns of praise..."** (*Μετὰ κλάδων ὑμνήσαντες*) read plain. After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"Upborne upon the throne in heaven and upon a foal on earth, O Christ God..."** (*Τῷ θρόνῳ ἐν οὐρανῷ*), the Oikos: **"Since Thou didst bind Hades, O Immortal One..."** (*Ἐπειδὴ ᾍδην ἔδησας*), the Menologion of the Saints of the day from the Menaion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion. The Katavasiai: **"The springs of the deep appeared dry..."** (*Ὤφθησαν αἱ πηγαὶ τῆς ἀβύσσου*). In place of **"More honorable than the Cherubim"**, the Ninth Ode of the Canon is chanted in its entirety with its Megalynaria. Then: **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (*Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*) three times in place of the Exaposteilarion. Immediately after this, the Prayer over the Palms [and Branches] is read by the Superior [Proestos]. Directly the First Choir chants: **"Let every breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*) and the appointed verses of the Praises [Lauds]³⁶ with the four Idiomela: [**"O Lord, great multitudes spread their...**[^438]

units.english_text: 36. In the Great Church, while the Praises are being chanted, the presiding Hierarchs venerate first the Icon of the Palms, and then approaching the Patriarch they kiss his right hand and receive from him the palms and olive branches, as do all the officiating clergy and dignitaries.

units.english_text: 65.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικὸν *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν· Σῶσον ἡμᾶς... ὁ ἐπὶ πώλου ὄνου* κτλ. τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια *Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*, καὶ *Συνταφέντες σοι*, εἶτα τὸ Κοντάκιον *Τῷ θρόνῳ ἐν οὐρανῷ*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, ὁ Εἱρμὸς τῆς θ' *Θεὸς Κύριος*, Κοινωνικὸν *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Ἀλληλούϊα*. *Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*, *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_text: 65.    At the Divine Liturgy, the Festal Antiphons of Palm Sunday [First Antiphon: Ps. 114 LXX with refrain "Through the prayers of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us"; Second Antiphon: Ps. 115 LXX with refrain "Save us, O Son of God, Who didst sit upon the foal of an ass, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"; Third Antiphon: Ps. 117 LXX with the Dismissal Troparion: "In confirming the common Resurrection..."]. The Entrance Hymn [Isodikon]: **"Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord! God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us: Save us, O Son of God, Who didst sit upon the foal of an ass, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου...*, Ps. 117:26–27 [LXX]). After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: **"In confirming the common Resurrection before Thy Passion..."** (*Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*) and **"Buried with Thee through Baptism, O Christ our God..."** (*Συνταφέντες σοι*). Then the Kontakion: **"Upborne upon the throne in heaven and upon a foal on earth, O Christ God..."** (*Τῷ θρόνῳ ἐν οὐρανῷ*). The Trisagion Hymn: **"Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us"** (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*). The Epistle [Apostolos]: Philippians 4:4–9 ("Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice!..."), and the Gospel: John 12:1–18 (The Anointing at Bethany and the Triumphal Entry). At "Especially [among the all-holy]...", the Heirmos of the Ninth Ode: **"God the Lord hath appeared unto us; let us appoint a festival, and rejoicing come, let us magnify Christ with palms and branches, crying aloud with voices of praise: Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord!..."** (*Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν*). The Communion Hymn [Koinōnikon]: **"Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord. Alleluia!"** (*Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου. Ἀλληλούϊα*, Ps. 117:26 [LXX]). In place of **"We have seen the true Light"**, we chant the Dismissal Troparion: **"In confirming the common Resurrection..."** (*Τὴν κοινὴν Ἀνάστασιν*); then: **"Blessed be the name of the Lord"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and the Dismissal.

units.english_text: 66.    On Sunday evening, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 [LXX]), we chant the three Aposticha Idiomela of yesterday: **"Rejoice and be glad, O city of Zion!..."** (*Χαῖρε καὶ εὐφραίνου*) twice, **"Today the Savior cometh unto Jerusalem..."** (*Σήμερον ὁ Σωτὴρ εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἔρχεται*) twice, and **"O Thou Who sittest upon the Cherubim and art praised by the Seraphim!..."** (*Ὁ τοῖς Χερουβὶμ ἐποχούμενος*) twice. "Glory...": **"Rejoice and be glad, O city of Zion!..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"O Thou Who sittest upon the Cherubim..."**. Little Entrance with the censer, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Great Prokimenon of the day: **"Turn not away Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble; hear me speedily: attend unto my soul, and deliver it!"** (*Μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἀπὸ τοῦ παιδός σου*, Ps. 68:18–19 [LXX]). Then the three appointed Aposticha: **"Passing from one divine feast to another divine feast, let us hasten, O believers..."** (*Ἐκ βαΐων εἰς βάϊα πιστοί*); verse: **"Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven..."** (Ps. 122:1 [LXX]); **"It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God..."** (*Φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας Θεοῦ ζῶντος*, Heb. 10:31); verse: **"Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us..."** (Ps. 122:3 [LXX]); **"O evil and adulterous generation, that hath not kept faith with its husband!..."** (*Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλίς*); "Glory...": **"Passing from one divine feast to another divine feast..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God..."**. After **"Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*, Luke 2:29), we immediately chant the Canon of Compline: **"Emulating the chaste wisdom of Joseph..."** (*Ἰωσὴφ τὴν σωφροσύνην ζηλώσαντες*) with the verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!"**. After the Ninth Ode, the Heirmos: **"Childbirth without corruption is alien to mothers, and virginity is strange to childbearing women..."** (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν μητέρων ἡ παρθενία*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos, Mary full of grace, the Lord is with thee..."** (*Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*), and the rest of Small Compline as on other Sundays of Great Lent.[^439]

Save us, O Son of God, Who did sit upon the foal of an ass, {as we sing unto You, Alleluia.}” {After the Entrance,} the Apolytikia: “O Christ God, when You did raise Lazarus” and “{O Christ God, when we were} buried with You in Baptism.” Then the Kontakion “{Upborne upon} the heavenly throne.” The Trisagios Hymn, Apostolos {Phillipians 4:4-9} and the Gospel {John 12:1-18.} At “Especially,” the Irmos of the Ninth [Ode] “God the Lord {has appeared unto us; let us celebrate the Feast.}” The Kinonikon “Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord. Alleluia.” {Instead of “We have seen the [True] Light,”} the Apolytikion “The common resurrection,” “Blessed be the name of the Lord,” and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 67.    The Priest: **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*); the Superior [Proestos]: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι. Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*); the Reader: **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times); **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times) and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 [LXX]: **"The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble..."** (*Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος*), and Psalm 20 [LXX]: **"The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."** (While these Psalms are being read slowly, the Priest censes the people with the hand-censer [*katzion*]). After the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; then the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, despise not our petitions, O Good One..."** (*Προστασία φοβερὰ καὶ ἀκαταίσχυντε*). The Dean or presiding Reader [Proistamenos] recites the Six Psalms. After the Great Litany, the Great Alleluia is chanted with its appointed verses: **"From night until morning my spirit seeks Thee early, O God, for Thy commandments are a light upon the earth"** (*Ἐκ νυκτὸς ὀρθρίζει*, Isa. 26:9 [LXX]), twice in slow melody and twice in brief melody. Then the Dismissal Troparion: **"Behold, the Bridegroom comes in the middle of the night, and blessed is the servant whom He finds watching..."** (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Νυμφίος ἔρχεται*) three times (twice slowly and once rapidly). At the end of the first time we say: **"...through the protection of the Bodiless Hosts, save us!"** (*Προστασίαις τῶν Ἀσωμάτων σῶσον ἡμᾶς*);³⁸ at the second time we join the commemoration of the Patron Saint of the Church, saying: **"...through the intercessions of Saint [N.] (or: the Saints), save us!"** (*Πρεσβείαις τοῦ Ἁγίου ἢ τῶν Ἁγίων σῶσον ἡμᾶς*); and at the third time: **"...through the Theotokos, have mercy on us!"** (*Διὰ τῆς Θεοτόκου ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*). Then the Kathismata of the Psalter,³⁹ and next the three appointed Sessional Hymns [Kathismata] of the Triodion are chanted slowly in sequence: the first two once each, and the third twice. Immediately the Priest exclaims: **"And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel..."**, and...[^440]

units.slavonic_text: --- 37. This dismissal is used until Holy Wednesday both in Matins and in the Liturgy. 38. On Great and Holy Tuesday: “...through the intercessions of the Forerunner save us.” On Great and Holy Wednesday: “...by the power of Your Cross, save us.” 39. The Psalter of the day is customarily omitted in most of the Churches at these Matins services, either for the sake of brevity or because there are Five Kathismata designated for every day of the first three days of the Great and Holy Week, and it is read separately in the morning by the Priest; but the function of prayer is that at least part of the Five Kathismata be read for the hearing of the laity, in as much as we viewed the Psalter from the beginning as the basis of our ecclesiastical prayers and the necessary daily spiritual food of each and every Christian, as was noted in the Provisions [Protheoria] Paragraph 3, note 3.
units.english_text: 39. The Psalter of the day is customarily omitted in most holy churches during these Matins services, either for the sake of brevity or because five Kathismata are appointed for each of the first three days of Holy Week, and it is read privately in the morning by the Priest; nevertheless it is devoutly to be wished that at least a portion of the five Kathismata be read in the hearing of the people also, inasmuch as the Psalter has ever been regarded as the foundation of our ecclesiastical prayers and the daily spiritual sustenance of every Christian, as was noted in the Introductory Chapter [Protheoria] § 3, footnote 3.

units.english_text: ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, μεθ' ὃ ὁ Ν' ψαλμὸς καὶ τὰ Τριῴδια ἀνὰ ς' ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ, καὶ αὖθις ὁ Εἱρμὸς ἀργῶς. ἡ Αἴτησις, τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου· εἶτα ἡ η' Ὠδὴ μετὰ τοῦ Εἱρμοῦ, καὶ ἀντὶ μὲν τοῦ *Δόξα*, λέγομεν *Εὐλογοῦμεν Πατέρα, Υἱὸν καὶ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα τὸν Κύριον*, εἰς δὲ τὸν Εἱρμὸν *Αἰνοῦμεν, εὐλογοῦμεν καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον*· εἶτα *Τὴν θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτὸς* καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ' Ὠδὴ μετὰ τοῦ Εἱρμοῦ αὖθις· εἰς τὸ τέλος ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ', καὶ ψάλλομεν τὰ β' τῶν Αἴνων Ἰδιόμελα εἰς δ', Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, *Κύριε ἐρχόμενος*. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους⁴⁰, ἱστῶμεν Στίχους δ', καὶ ψάλλομεν τὰ β' τῶν Αἴνων Ἰδιόμελα εἰς δ'. Δόξα καὶ νῦν, *Κύριε ἐρχόμενος*, τὸ *Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει* χῦμα καὶ μετὰ τὸ *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*, ἄρχεται τῶν Ἀποστίχων ὁ α' Χορός, εἶτα *Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, Κοντάκιον *Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο*, *Κύριε ἐλέησον* ιβ' ⁴¹, *Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*, *Ἐπουράνιε βασιλεῦ*, τὰς τρεῖς Μ. μετανοίας, ἡ Ἀπόλυσις *Ἐρχόμενος ὁ Κύριος ἐπὶ τὸ ἑκούσιον πάθος* καὶ τὸ *Δι' εὐχῶν*⁴².

units.english_text: ... reads the Gospel [Matthew 21:18–43: The Cursing of the Barren Fig Tree and the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers]. After the Gospel, Psalm 50 is read; then the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion] in six Troparia in each Ode, and again the Heirmos slowly as Katavasia. The Small Litany, the Kontakion: **"Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph..."** (*Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο*), the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion. Then the Eighth Ode with its Heirmos; and instead of **"Glory..."**, we say: **"We bless the Lord: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit"** (*Εὐλογοῦμεν Πατέρα, Υἱὸν καὶ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα τὸν Κύριον*). Before the Heirmos is repeated as Katavasia, we sing: **"We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord"** (*Αἰνοῦμεν, εὐλογοῦμεν καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον*). Then the Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode is chanted with its Heirmos again. At the conclusion, the Small Litany and the Exaposteilarion: **"I see Thy bridal chamber adorned, O my Savior, and I have no wedding garment that I may enter therein; enlighten the robe of my soul, O Giver of Light, and save me!"** (*Τὸν νυμφῶνά σου βλέπω, Σωτήρ μου, κεκοσμημένον*) three times. At the Praises:⁴⁰ we set 4 verses, and we chant the two Idiomela of the Praises (twice each): [**"O Lord, coming unto Thy voluntary Passion..."** (*Κύριε, ἐρχόμενος πρὸς τὸ πάθος*) and **"O Lord, coming unto Thy Passion, Thou didst establish the hearts of Thy Disciples..."**]. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"O Lord, coming unto Thy Passion, Thou didst say unto Thy Disciples: Watch and pray..."** (*Κύριε, ἐρχόμενος πρὸς τὸ πάθος, τοὺς ἰδίους ἐστήριξας Μαθητάς*). The Small Doxology: **"To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God..."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) read plain. After the litany: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*), the First Choir begins the Aposticha. Then: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to sing unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph..."**, **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times);⁴¹ the Priest: **"Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"** (*Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*); the Reader: **"Confirm, O God, the holy Orthodox faith..."**; then the Prayer: **"O Heavenly King, strengthen our faithful civil authorities..."** (*Ἐπουράνιε βασιλεῦ*); the three Great Prostrations with the Prayer of Saint Ephrem the Syrian, and the Dismissal: **"May the Lord, coming unto His voluntary Passion for our salvation, Christ our true God..."** (*Ἐρχόμενος ὁ Κύριος ἐπὶ τὸ ἑκούσιον πάθος*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).⁴²[^441]

units.slavonic_text: Triodion} are chanted according to the following order: Kathisma Four of the Psalter and “Your Passion, as a perfect light raises and shines upon the world this present day.... from” Kathisma Five and “O invisible Judge, how have You been seen and gone to be killed by iniquitous men....” Kathisma Six and “The present day brings the light of the first fruits of the Passion of the Lord....” Glory, Now and ever. Repeat “The present day...” and immediately the Priest: “Let us supplicate the Lord our God,” and he reads the Gospel {Matthew 21:18-43.} {Reader:} Psalm 50; then the First Ode of the Triodion Canon (each verse repeated) and immediately slowly the Irmos “{Let us sing a song to the Lord” is repeated as a Katavasia.} The [Small] Litany, Kontakion, Ikos, Minologion and the Postscript of the Triodion. Then the Eighth Ode with its Irmos and, instead of Glory, we say “We bless Father, Son and Holy Spirit, the Lord.” Before the Irmos of the Eighth Ode is repeated as a Katavasia, the following verse is added: “We praise, we bless and worship the Lord.” Deacon: “{We magnify} the Theotokos and Mother of Light, {and honor her in hymns.}” Chanters: immediately the Ninth Ode with its Irmos. The Small Litany; Exapostilarion {“I see Your bridal chamber”} (3 times). At the Praises:⁴⁰ we sing the two Idiomela of the Praises (twice each). Glory, Now and ever, “O Lord, going to Your Passion”; the Small Doxology “To You belongs all glory” (read). After the Petitions: “Let us complete our morning supplication {to the Lord}.” The First Choir begins the Aposticha. At the conclusion of the Aposticha, the Priest: “It is a good thing to confess unto the Lord.” The Reader: the Trisagion, then the Kontakion “Jacob lamented {the loss of Joseph,}” “Lord have mercy” (12 times).⁴¹ Priest: “Wisdom. You Who are blessed, Christ our God, now and ever and to the ages of ages.” “O Heavenly King, {strengthen our faithful kings,}” the three Great Prostrations, and the Dismissal “{Glory to You, our God and our Hope, glory to You.} May Christ, our True God, the Lord, Who willingly came to His Passion for our salvation... Through the prayers {of our Holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy upon us and save us}.”⁴²

units.slavonic_text: --- 40. At the “Praise,” [of the Praises] the Patriarch or the Archbishop kisses the Holy Icon of the Passion and, blessing the people with the choirs singing the “For many years,” he ascends immediately the Parathrone (Parathronion.) 41. See footnote 31. 42. This order of the Service is observed on the following two days, that is, on Holy Tuesday and Holy Wednesday, either in in the morning or in the evening, when the Matins of the Bridegroom takes place. If in the evening, then the Psalter is usually omitted and, instead, is read the following morning.
units.english_text: 42. This order of the service is observed on the following two days, namely on Great and Holy Tuesday and Great and Holy Wednesday, whether the Matins of the Bridegroom takes place in the morning or in the evening. In the latter case, however, the Psalter is customarily read in the morning.

provenance.verbatim_source: 42. This order of the service is observed on the following two days, namely on Great and Holy Tuesday and Great and Holy Wednesday, whether the Matins of the Bridegroom takes place in the morning or in the evening. In the latter case, however, the Psalter is customarily read in the morning.

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Holy Week: Great Monday (Hours, Presanctified, Compline) and Great Tuesday (Matins, Hours, Presanctified, Compline Opening) (§§ 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74 Opening) (p. 751)]
units.english_text: 68.    In the morning, the five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8]; then the plain Hours with the Dismissal Troparion: **"Behold, the Bridegroom comes..."** (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Νυμφίος ἔρχεται*) and the Kontakion: **"Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph..."** (*Ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὠδύρετο*). At the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes [Makarismoi] are chanted; and after the Prayer: **"All-Holy Trinity, Consubstantial Might..."** (*Παναγία Τριάς*), the Dismissal is given, and Vespers begins.

units.english_text: 69.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]) and the Eighteenth Kathisma: **"Unto the Lord"** (*Πρὸς Κύριον*, Pss. 119–133 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 [LXX]), we chant the six Idiomela of the Praises and the Aposticha. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Finding the Egyptian woman another Eve, the serpent hastened through speech to trip up Joseph..."** (*Δευτέραν Εὔαν τὴν Αἰγυπτίαν εὑρὼν ὁ δράκων*). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Old Testament Readings of the day: Exodus 1:1–20 [LXX] and Job 1:1–12 [LXX]. Then **"Let my prayer arise"** (*Κατευθυνθήτω*), and immediately after it: **"Wisdom! Stand upright! Let us hear the Holy Gospel"**, and the Gospel is read [Matthew 24:3–35: The Discourse on the Mount of Olives], and in sequence the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts.

units.slavonic_text: 68.    In the morning, the five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathisma Four, Five, Six, Seven, and Eight] then the Hours with the Apolytikion “Behold, the Bridegroom comes....” and the Kontakion “Jacob lamented.” At the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes are chanted; after the prayer “All-holy Trinity,” the Dismissal, and Vespers begin. 69.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm {103} and Kathisma 18 [of the Psalter], at “Lord, I have cried,” we sing the six Idiomela of the Praises and the Aposticha. Glory, Now and ever, “Finding the Egyptian woman another Eve.” The Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” and the Readings of the day: {Exodus 1:1-20 and Job 1:1-12.} Then the “Let my prayer arise” and immediately after it “Wisdom! Arise, let us hear [the Holy Gospel...]” and the Gospel {Matthew 24:3-35} and the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts. 70.    In the evening, as is customary, we read the Great Compline. After the Doxology “Glory to God in the Highest,” the Second Choir begins the Triodion Canon; after the Irmos of the Ninth Ode “The Establisher of the law,” the Trisagion, then “O Lord of Hosts” and the rest of the Great Compline. At the Forgiveness Rite, we chant “When the Virgin beheld Your unjust slaughter, O Christ, [she wailed].”
units.english_text: 70.    In the evening, Great Compline is read, as is customary. After the Doxology: **"Glory to God in the highest..."** (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*), the Second Choir begins the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion]; after the Heirmos of the Ninth Ode: **"Him that was prefigured upon the mountain..."** (*Τὸν προδηλωθέντα ἐν ὄρει*), the Trisagion Prayers, and following this: **"O Lord of hosts, be with us..."** (*Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*), and the rest of Great Compline. At the rite of Mutual Forgiveness, we chant: **"When the Virgin beheld Thy unjust slaughter, O Christ, she lamented: Woe is me, my Child!..."** (*Σφαγήν σου τὴν ἄδικον, Χριστέ*).

units.slavonic_text: GREAT WEDNESDAY
units.english_text: In the morning, another five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata 14, 15, 16, 19, and 20], and thus the entire Psalter is completed, omitting the two Kathismata (17 and 18): the former because it is to be read on Great Saturday, and the latter because it is frequently read at every Presanctified Liturgy, and indeed was read on the three preceding days of this week. Likewise the plain Hours are read, as on the two preceding days; and after the Prayer: **"All-Holy Trinity..."** (*Παναγία Τριάς*), the Dismissal is given, and Vespers begins.

units.slavonic_text: 75.    The Service of Matins and of this day is chanted unalterably⁴³ according to the rubrics of Paragraph 67. In the morning, another five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata Fourteen, Fifteen, Sixteen, Nineteen and Twenty] and in this way the entire Psalter is completed, omitting the two Kathismata (Seventeen and Eighteen), the former because it will be read on Great Saturday, and the latter because it is read frequently in every Presanctified Liturgy and because it was already read on three days of this week. Also the Liti Hours are read as on the two previous days, and after the Prayer “All-Holy Trinity” the Dismissal and then Vespers begin. 76.    In Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (103) and “To the Lord” [Kathisma 18], at “Lord, I have cried,” we chant 10 Verses and all the Stichira which were chanted as Praises and Aposticha in Matins. Glory, Now and ever, “The woman who had fallen into many sins.” The Entrance with the Gospel, “O Gladsome Light,” the Readings {Exodus 2:11-23 and Job 2:1-10}. Then “Let my prayer arise,” the Gospel {Matthew 26:6-16} and the rest of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts, which is also the last one in Great Lent. 77.    In the evening, the Small Compline is read. Then, after “It is meet,” the Three-Ode Canon “Furnished and ready” with the Verse “Glory to You our God, glory to You.” After the Irmos of the Ninth Ode “Past description is the childbirth from a conception without seed.” The
units.english_text: 76.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]) and the Eighteenth Kathisma: **"Unto the Lord"** (*Πρὸς Κύριον*, Pss. 119–133 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we set 10 verses, and we chant all the Stichera which were chanted as Praises and Aposticha at Matins. "Glory... Both now and ever...": the Doxastikon: **"O Lord, the woman who had fallen into many sins, having recognized Thy divinity, O Lord, taking upon herself the office of a myrrh-bearer..."** (*Κύριε, ἡ ἐν πολλαῖς ἁμαρτίαις*). units.english_text: 78.    Μετὰ τὸν Ἑξάψαλμον καὶ τὴν Μ. Συναπτήν, ψάλλομεν μετὰ Στίχων τὸ *Ἀλληλούϊα* εἰς ἦχον πλ. δ' τετράκις, καὶ τὸ Τροπάριον *Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι Μαθηταὶ* ἐκ γ' καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Ὄρθρου τῆς ἡμέρας, εἶτα ὁ Ν' ψαλμός, καὶ ὁ Κανὼν ἄνευ Στίχων μετὰ τῆς Καταβασίας ἐν τέλει ἑκάστης Ὠδῆς. Ἀπὸ γ' Ὠδῆς τὰ Καθίσματα· ἀφ' ς' τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου. Μετὰ τὸν Εἱρμὸν τῆς η' Ὠδῆς, γίνεται ἡ Ἐκφώνησις *Τὴν θεοτόκον* καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ' Ὠδή, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον ἐκ γ', οἱ Αἶνοι εἰς δ', Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, *Ὃν ἐκήρυξεν Ἀμνόν*, τὸ *Σοὶ Δόξα πρέπει* χῦμα, *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν*, καὶ τὰ δ' Ἀπόστιχα, Δόξα, *Ὁ τρόπος σου δολιότης*, Καὶ νῦν, *Μυσταγωγῶν σου Κύριε*, *Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Τροπάριον τῆς Προφητείας, καὶ ἡ Προφητεία. Ἐκτενής, καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_text: 78.    After the Six Psalms and the Great Litany, we chant the Alleluia with its verses in Tone 8 four times, and the Troparion: **"When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold his goods, O lover of money, who for the sake thereof hanged himself! Flee from the insatiable soul that dared such things against the Master! O Lord, Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!"** (*Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι Μαθηταὶ*) three times. Immediately the Matins Gospel of the day is read: Luke 22:1–39 [LXX: The Institution of the Holy Eucharist and the Discourse at the Last Supper]. Then Psalm 50 is read, and the Canon is chanted without verses, with its Katavasia at the end of each Ode. After the Third Ode, the Sessional Hymns [Kathismata]: **"He Who created the lakes, the springs and the seas, desiring to teach us the highest humility, girded Himself with a towel and washed the feet of the Disciples..."**; "Glory...": **"Having humbled Thyself through compassion, Thou didst wash the feet of Thy Disciples..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"Eating, O Master, with Thy Disciples, Thou didst mystically reveal Thy holy slaughter..."**. After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion: **"Having taken the Bread into his hands, the traitor extends them secretly to receive the price of Him Who fashioned man with His own hands; and Judas remained incorrigible, having dipped his hand into the dish with Christ..."**, the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion on the Mystical Supper, the Washing of the Disciples' Feet, the Agony in the Garden, and the Betrayal of Judas. After the Heirmos of the Eighth Ode is chanted as Katavasia, the Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode is chanted. Then the Exaposteilarion: **"I see Thy bridal chamber adorned, O my Savior..."** (*Τὸν νυμφῶνά σου βλέπω*) three times. At the Praises [Lauds], we chant the four Stichera: [**"The assembly of the Jews hastens together to deliver the Creator and Fashioner of all unto Pilate..."**, **"Judas the transgressor, having dipped his hand into the dish with Thee at supper..."**, **"Judas, being a treacherous servant, deceitfully devised betrayal..."**, and **"Judas, servant and deceiver, disciple and plotter, friend and devil, was made manifest from his deeds..."**]. "Glory... Both now and ever...": the Doxastikon: **"The Lamb whom Isaiah proclaimed comes of His own will to the slaughter..."** (*Ὃν ἐκήρυξεν Ἀμνόν*). The Small Doxology: **"To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God..."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) read plain. The litany: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν*), and the four Aposticha with verses from Psalm 40 LXX: [**"Today the evil Sanhedrin has assembled together against Christ..."**; verse: **"He that eats of my bread has lifted up his heel against me"** (Ps. 40:9 [LXX]); **"Today Judas hides his treachery under the pretense of love for the poor..."**; verse: **"When he went abroad, he spoke of the same"** (Ps. 40:6 [LXX]); **"Thy deceitful manner is revealed unto the end..."**; verse: **"An evil word have they poured out against me"** (Ps. 40:8 [LXX]); and **"O believers, let none of us who are uninitiated draw near to the Master's table..."**]. "Glory...": **"Thy deceitful manner..."**; "Both now and ever...": **"Initiating Thy Disciples, O Lord, Thou didst teach them, saying: O my friends, see that no fear separate you from Me..."** (*Μυσταγωγῶν σου, Κύριε*). Then: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord..."** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Troparion of the Prophecy: **"Thou Who didst endure slaps for the human race, O Christ God, deliver us from corruption and save our souls"**, and the Old Testament Prophecy: Jeremiah 11:18–12:5, 9–11, 14–15 [LXX: The Prophecy of the Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter]. The Augmented Litany [Ektenis], and the Dismissal.

provenance.verbatim_source: 78.    After the Six Psalms and the Great Litany, we chant the Alleluia with its verses in Tone 8 four times, and the Troparion: **"When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold his goods, O lover of money, who for the sake thereof hanged himself! Flee from the insatiable soul that dared such things against the Master! O Lord, Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!"** (*Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι Μαθηταὶ*) three times. Immediately the Matins Gospel of the day is read: Luke 22:1–39 [LXX: The Institution of the Holy Eucharist and the Discourse at the Last Supper]. Then Psalm 50 is read, and the Canon is chanted without verses, with its Katavasia at the end of each Ode. After the Third Ode, the Sessional Hymns [Kathismata]: **"He Who created the lakes, the springs and the seas, desiring to teach us the highest humility, girded Himself with a towel and washed the feet of the Disciples..."**; "Glory...": **"Having humbled Thyself through compassion, Thou didst wash the feet of Thy Disciples..."**; "Both now and ever...": *

units.english_text: 79.    At Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 [LXX]), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the five Idiomela of the Praises, repeating the first one for six. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Judas is truly the offspring of vipers, who ate the manna in the wilderness and murmured against the Nourisher..."** (*Γέννημα ἐχιδνῶν*). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Old Testament Readings: Exodus 19:10–19 [LXX], Job...[^444]

Then the Small Litany, the Trisagion Hymn, the Epistle (1 Corinthians 11:23–32: The Institution of the Holy Eucharist), and the Gospel (Matthew 26:2–20; John 13:3–17; Matthew 26:21–39; Luke 22:43–45; Matthew 26:40–27:2: The Composite Passion Gospel of the Mystical Supper), and in sequence the rest of the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. In place of the Cherubic Hymn, the Communion Hymn, and **"We have seen the true light"**, is chanted: **"Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, receive me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of the Mystery to Thine enemies, neither will I give Thee a kiss as did Judas, but like the thief do I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!"** (*Τοῦ δείπνου σου τοῦ μυστικοῦ*). Then: **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and the Dismissal: **"Glory to Thee, our God, our hope, glory to Thee. May He Who out of exceeding goodness showed humility to be the most excellent way when He washed the feet of the Disciples, and condescended unto the Cross and burial for our sake, Christ our true God..."** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς . . . ὁ δι' ὑπερβάλλουσαν ἀγαθότητα*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).

The “Receive me today, {O Son of God}” is sung in place of the Cherubic Hymn, the Communion Hymn [Kinonikon] and “We have seen the [True] Light.” Then, “Blessed be the name [of the Lord],” and Dismissal: “Glory to You, our God {and our Hope, glory to You . . .} You Who because of Your exceeding goodness, did reveal humility as a virtuous way when You did wash the feet of Your Disciples; and did condescend to endure Crucifixion and Burial for our sakes, O Christ, our True God,” etc. Then Through the prayers {of our holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ, our God, have mercy upon us and save us}.”
units.english_text: 80.    On Holy and Great Thursday evening, around the First Hour of the night [7:00 p.m.], the Priest having given the blessing, the Superior [Proestos] says: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι. Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; the Reader: **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times), **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times) and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 [LXX]: **"The Lord hear Thee in the day of trouble..."** (*Ἐπακούσαι σου Κύριος*), and Psalm 20 [LXX]: **"The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."** (these are read slowly until the Priest finishes censing with the hand-censer [*katzion*]); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, despise not our petitions, O Good One..."**; and the Superior [Proestos] reads the Six Psalms. The Great Litany; then the brief Alleluia is chanted four times with its verses, and the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold his goods, O lover of money, who for the sake thereof hanged himself! Flee from the insatiable soul that dared such things against the Master! O Lord, Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!"** (*Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι μαθηταὶ*) twice slowly and once rapidly. Then the First Gospel of the Testament [John 13:31–18:1: The Farewell Discourse of Christ to the Disciples] is read by the Archbishop [or the Priest]; at the conclusion, having blessed the people with the three-stemmed candlestick [*trikirion*], while the choirs chant: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he ascends the throne, and the choirs chant the Antiphons, beginning with: **"The rulers of the peoples took counsel together against the Lord and against His Anointed"** (*Ἄρχοντες λαῶν*) until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"Sustaining the disciples at the supper, Thou didst say: One of you will betray Me..."** (*Ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ τοὺς μαθητάς*).[^445]

units.slavonic_text: 80.    On Holy and Great Thursday evening, around the First Hour of the night [7 p.m.] the Priest having given the opening blessing, the Proestos says “Glory to You, our God, glory to You. O Heavenly King, {Comforter.}” The Reader: the Trisagion. The Priest: “For Yours is [the Kingdom and the Power].” The Reader: “[Amen.] Lord, have mercy” (12 times), [Glory, Now and ever,] “O come let us worship [and bow down]” (3 times) and the Psalms “May the Lord answer you [in the day of trouble]” (Psalm 20) {and “The King shall have joy in Your strength” (Psalm 21)} (these are done slowly until the Priest has completed censing with the small hand censer), then the Trisagion, the Troparia “Lord, save Your people,” etc. {Glory, “O Christ our God, who was of Your own will.” Now and ever, “O awesome and ever-present protection.”} The Proestos reads the Exapsalmos, the Great Litany and then is sung the quick “Alleluia” (in 4) [with its verses], and the Troparion “When the glorious disciples” (twice slowly and once quickly). The reading of the First Gospel of the Testament {John 13:31-18:1} is done by the Archbishop {or Priest}, at the conclusion of which the Archbishop blesses the people with the Trikiri [three-stemmed candelabra of the Bishop], the choir singing “For many years, [Master].” Then the Archbishop ascends the Throne and the Choirs sing the Antiphons beginning with “The princes of the people [assembled against the Lord and his annointed]” until the Kathisma “Sustaining the disciples at the supper.”

units.english_text: ... Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"Sustaining the disciples at the supper, Thou didst say: One of you will betray Me; but Judas the transgressor did not wish to understand"** (*Ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ τοὺς μαθητάς*). After this, the Second Gospel [John 18:1–28: The Betrayal and Arrest in Gethsemane, and Jesus before Annas] is proclaimed; at the conclusion, the Second Choir chants: **"Glory to Thy forbearance, O Lord, glory to Thee!"** (*Δόξα τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σου Κύριε δόξα σοι*) (which is repeated at the end of each of the remaining Gospels). Then begins the Fourth Antiphon until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"What reason has made thee, O Judas, a traitor of the Savior? Did He cast thee off from the choir of the Apostles? Did He deprive thee of the gift of healings?..."** (*Ποῖός σε τρόπος Ἰούδα*). Then follows the Third Gospel [Matthew 26:57–75: Jesus before Caiaphas and the Denial of Peter]. Then the choir chants the Seventh Antiphon until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"O how did Judas, who was once Thy disciple, devise betrayal against Thee?..."** (*Ὢ πῶς Ἰούδας ὁ ποτέ σου μαθητής*). Then the Fourth Gospel [John 18:28–19:16: Jesus before Pilate and the Condemnation to Death] is read; then the Second Choir begins the Tenth Antiphon until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"When Thou, O God, didst stand before Caiaphas, and wast delivered unto Pilate, the Judge of all: the powers of heaven shook with fear..."** (*Ὅτε παρέστης τῷ Καϊάφᾳ ὁ Θεός*). Then the Fifth Gospel [Matthew 27:3–32: The Despair of Judas, Pilate Washes His Hands, and Simon of Cyrene Bears the Cross] is proclaimed; after this, the First Choir begins Antiphon Thirteen: **"The assembly of the Jews requested Pilate to crucify Thee, O Lord..."** (*Ὁ δῆμος τῶν Ἰουδαίων*), continuing through Antiphon Fourteen. At this point takes place the Procession of the Holy Cross, as has now become customary almost everywhere: the Priest, carrying the Holy Crucifix and preceded by candle-bearers and the hand-censer [*katzion*], exits from the Sanctuary and proceeds in solemn procession around the temple, chanting in a recitative melody: **"Today is hung upon the Tree, He Who suspended the earth upon the waters"** (*Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου, ὁ ἐν ὕδασι τὴν γῆν κρεμάσας*) three times, which is repeated by the choir. The Antiphons continue until the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma]: **"Thou hast ransomed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with the spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality upon mankind. O our Savior, glory to Thee!"** (*Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου*); then the Sixth Gospel [Mark 15:16–32: The Mocking by the Soldiers and the Crucifixion at Golgotha] is read. Then the First Choir begins the Beatitudes [Makarismoi], at the conclusion of which is chanted the Prokimenon in Tone 4 three times: **"They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"** (*Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς*, Ps. 21:18 [LXX]), and the Seventh Gospel [Matthew 27:33–54: The Crucifixion, the Darkness, and the Death of Jesus] is read. Then Psalm 50 [LXX], and the Eighth Gospel [Luke 23:32–49: The Penitent Thief and the Death of Christ] is read; then the First Choir begins the Canon of the Triodion: **"Early in the morning my soul rises unto Thee, O Word of God..."** (*Πρὸς σὲ ὀρθρίζω*) by Saint Cosmas the Melodist, with four Troparia at each Ode, without biblical verses, and at the end of each Ode the Heirmos is chanted slowly as Katavasia. After Ode 5 is sung, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us; for Mary beheld Him upon the Tree and said: Even though Thou dost endure the Cross, Thou art my Son and my God!"** (*Τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρωθέντα*), the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion. Then Ode 8 of the Canon, at the end of which the Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode is sung. The Small Litany, the Exaposteilarion in Tone 3: **"The wise thief in a single hour Thou didst account worthy of Paradise, O Lord; enlighten me also by the wood of the Cross, and save me!"** (*Τὸν λῃστὴν αὐθημερὸν*) three times. The Ninth Gospel [John 19:25–37: Jesus Commends His Mother to John, "It Is Finished", and the Piercing of His Side] is then read. At the Praises: the three Idiomela with their verses are sung, repeating the first: Verse 1: **"Praise Him for His mighty acts, praise Him according to the multitude of His greatness!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐπὶ ταῖς δυναστείαις αὐτοῦ*, Ps. 150:2 [LXX]); Idiomelon 1: **"Two evil deeds has My first-born son Israel committed: he has forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and has dug for himself a broken cistern..."** (*Δύο καὶ πονηρὰ ἐποίησεν*). Verse 2: **"Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet, praise Him with lute and harp!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν ἤχῳ σάλπιγγος*, Ps. 150:3 [LXX]); Idiomelon 1 repeated. Verse 3: **"Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him with strings and pipes!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν τυμπάνῳ καὶ χορῷ*, Ps. 150:4 [LXX]); Idiomelon 2: **"Every member of Thy holy flesh endured dishonor for our sake: the head with thorns, the face with spittings, the cheeks with buffetings, the mouth with vinegar mingled with gall, the ears with impious blasphemies, the back with scourgings, the hand with the reed, the whole body with extension upon the Cross, the limbs with nails, and the side with the spear. O Thou Who didst suffer for us and didst free us from passions, Who didst condescend to us in Thy love for mankind and didst raise us up: O Almighty Savior, have mercy on us!"** (*Ἕκαστον μέλος τῆς ἁγίας σου σαρκός*)...[^446]

units.english_text: Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, τὸ ι΄ Εὐαγγέλιον καὶ εὐθὺς *Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*, *Πληρώσωμεν*, καὶ τὸ ια΄ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ εὐθὺς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, μεθ' ἃ τὸ ιβ΄ Εὐαγγέλιον ὑπὸ τοῦ Διακόνου ἀπὸ τοῦ ἄμβωνος, τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*, τὸ *Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς* ἐκ γ΄, εἶτα *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός . . . ὑπὲρ τῶν εὐσεβῶν καὶ ὀρθοδόξων χριστιανῶν . . . ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἀρχιεπισκόπου ἡμῶν . . . Ὅτι ἐλεήμων καὶ φιλάνθρωπος*, *Σοφία*, *Ὁ ὢν Εὐλογητός*, τὸ *Στερεώσαι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς* ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως ἢ τοῦ Προεστῶτος, ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν δόξα σοι*, *ὁ ἐμπτυσμοὺς καὶ μάστιγας καὶ κολαφισμοὺς καὶ σταυρὸν καὶ θάνατον ὑπομείνας διὰ τὴν τοῦ κόσμου σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς . . .* κτλ. καὶ τὸ *Δι' εὐχῶν*.

units.english_text: ... Verse 4: **"Praise Him with sounding cymbals, praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that has breath praise the Lord!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν κυμβάλοις εὐήχοις*, Ps. 150:5–6 [LXX]); Idiomelon 3: **"Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, all creation trembled; the foundations of the earth shook with fear of Thy might; for when Thou wast lifted up today, the Hebrew race perished..."** (*Σταυρωθέντα σε θεωροῦσα*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"They stripped Me of My garments and clothed Me in a scarlet robe; they placed upon My head a crown of thorns and gave a reed into My right hand, that I might smash them like a potter's vessels"** (*Ἐξέδυσάν με τὰ ἱμάτιά μου*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"I gave My back to scourgings, and My cheeks to blows, and I turned not My face from the shame of spittings; I stood before the tribunal of Pilate and endured the Cross for the salvation of the world"** (*Τὸν νῶτόν μου ἔδωκα εἰς μάστιγας*). Then the Tenth Gospel [Mark 15:43–47: Joseph of Arimathea Obtains the Body of Jesus and Lays It in a Tomb] is read, and immediately: **"To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God, and to Thee we send up glory: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) read plain. The Deacon: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*), and the Eleventh Gospel [John 19:38–42: The Burial of Jesus by Joseph and Nicodemus] is proclaimed. Then, immediately, the Aposticha: 1. **"All creation was altered with fear when it beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ; the sun was darkened, and the foundations of the earth were shaken..."** (*Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις ἠλλοιοῦτο φόβῳ*); the Verse: **"They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"** (*Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου*, Ps. 21:18 [LXX]); 2. **"Why does the impious and lawless people imagine vain things? Why did they condemn to death the Life of all?..."** (*Λαὸς δυσσεβὴς καὶ παράνομος*); the Verse: **"They gave Me gall for My food, and for My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink"** (*Ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ βρῶμά μου χολὴν*, Ps. 68:21 [LXX]); 3. **"Today, seeing Thee, O Word, hanging upon the Cross, the blameless Virgin wept with maternal sorrow..."** (*Σήμερον σὲ θεωροῦσα ἡ ἄμεμπτος Παρθένος*); the Verse: **"God is our King before the ages; He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth"** (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων*, Ps. 73:12 [LXX]); 4. **"Beholding Thee, the Creator and God of all, lifted up upon the Tree, all creation trembled..."** (*Ἐπὶ ξύλου βλέπουσα κρεμάμενον*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Lord, when Thou didst ascend the Cross, fear and trembling fell upon creation..."** (*Κύριε, ἀναβαίνοντός σου ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 8: **"The reed of denial has already been dipped by the unjust judges..."** (*Ἤδη βάπτεται κάλαμος ἀποφάσεως*). The Twelfth Gospel [Matthew 27:62–66: The Guard Set at the Tomb] is read by the Deacon from the ambo. At the conclusion of the reading, the Archbishop blesses him, and the choir chants: **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*). The Priest: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to sing unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, Ps. 91:1 [LXX]). The Reader: the Trisagion Prayers. The Chanter: the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ransomed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood; having been nailed to the Cross and pierced with the spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality upon mankind. O our Savior, glory to Thee!"** (*Ἐξηγόρασας ἡμᾶς*) three times. The Deacon intones the Augmented Litany: **"Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee: hear and have mercy"**; **"Again we pray for all pious and Orthodox Christians"**; **"Again we pray for our Archbishop [N.]"**. The Priest gives the exclamation: **"For Thou art a merciful and loving God, and unto Thee we send up glory: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** The Deacon: **"Wisdom!"** The Priest: **"Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"** (*Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*). The Archbishop [or Superior / Proestos]: **"Confirm, O Lord God, the holy Orthodox faith of pious and Orthodox Christians unto ages of ages"** (*Στερεώσαι Κύριος ὁ Θεός*). The Priest: **"Glory to Thee, O God, our hope, glory to Thee. May Christ our true God, Who endured spittings, and scourgings, buffetings, and the Cross and Death for the salvation of the world, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν δόξα σοι· ὁ ἐμπτυσμοὺς καὶ μάστιγας...*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).[^447]

Περὶ τὴν α΄ πρωϊνὴν ὥραν τῆς ἡμέρας εὐλογήσαντος τοῦ Ἱερέως, ὁ Προεστὼς τὸ *Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*, ὁ Ἀναγνώστης *Κύριε ἐλέησον* ιβ΄, *Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν*, *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν* γ΄ καὶ ἀναγινώσκει τοὺς ψαλμοὺς τῆς α΄ Ὥρας, εἶτα *Δόξα, Σταυρωθέντος σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Τί σε καλέσωμεν* καὶ ἄρχεται ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλων τὸ α΄ Ἰδιόμελον, ὁ β΄ μετὰ τοῦ Στίχου *Ἵνα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη*, καὶ ψάλλει τὸ β΄, καὶ αὖθις ὁ α΄ *Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τοῖς συλλαβοῦσί σε παρανόμοις*· ἀκολούθως ἡ Προφητεία, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ εὐθὺς *Τὰ διαβήματά μου*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Κοντάκιον *Τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρωθέντα*, *Κύριε ἐλέησον* μ΄, *Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ* καὶ ὁ Προεστὼς τὴν Εὐχήν· *Χριστὲ τὸ φῶς*, καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ γ΄ Ὥρα ⁴⁵.

units.slavonic_text: GREAT FRIDAY
units.english_text: 81.    Around the First Hour of the morning [7:00 a.m.], the Priest having given the blessing, the Superior [Proestos] says: **"O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; the Reader: **"Lord, have mercy"** (12 times), **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**, **"O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..."** (3 times), and he reads the Psalms of the First Hour: Psalm 5 [LXX]: **"Give ear to my words, O Lord..."**; Psalm 2 [LXX]: **"Why do the nations rage..."**; and Psalm 21 [LXX]: **"O God, my God, attend to me; why hast Thou forsaken me?..."**. Then "Glory...": **"When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, the tyranny was destroyed, and the power of the enemy was trampled underfoot; for neither an angel nor a man, but the Lord Himself saved us. Glory to Thee!"** (*Σταυρωθέντος σου Χριστέ*); "Both now and ever...": **"What shall we call thee, O full of grace?..."** (*Τί σε καλέσωμεν*). The First Choir begins chanting the first Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"Today the veil of the temple is rent in twain for the rebuke of the lawless, and the sun hides its rays beholding the Master crucified"** (*Σήμερον τοῦ ναοῦ τὸ καταπέτασμα*); the Second Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"As a sheep led to the slaughter wast Thou brought, O Christ King, and as an innocent lamb nailed to the Cross by lawless men on account of our sins, O Lover of mankind"** (*Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν*), preceded by the verse: **"Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?"** (*Ἵνα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη*, Ps. 2:1 [LXX]); and again the First Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Unto the transgressors who seized Thee, O Christ, Thou didst cry aloud: What harm did I do unto you, or wherein did I provoke you?..."** (*Τοῖς συλλαβοῦσί σε παρανόμοις*). Next, the Prophecy: Zechariah 11:10–13 [LXX] (The Thirty Pieces of Silver Cast into the Furnace in the House of the Lord); the Epistle: Galatians 6:14–18 (Glorying only in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:1–56 (The Trial before Pilate, the Mocking, the Crucifixion, and the Death of Jesus). Directly the Reader says: **"Order my steps according to Thy word, and let no iniquity have dominion over me..."** (*Τὰ διαβήματά μου*, Ps. 118:133 [LXX]), the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us; for Mary beheld Him upon the Tree and said: Even though Thou dost endure the Cross, Thou art my Son and my God!"** (*Τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρωθέντα*), **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times), the Prayer of the Hours: **"Thou Who at all times and at every hour, in heaven and on earth, art worshipped and glorified, O Christ God..."** (*Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ*), and the Superior [Proestos] says the concluding prayer: **"O Christ, the True Light, Who enlightenest and sanctifiest every man that cometh into the world..."** (*Χριστὲ τὸ φῶς*), and the Third Hour begins.⁴⁵

units.slavonic_text: THE HOURS
units.english_text: At the Third Hour, the service begins as at the First Hour, then Psalms 34, 108, and 50 [LXX]. "Glory...": **"O Lord, the Jews condemned Thee to death, the Life of all..."** (*Κύριε, κατέκριναν σε Ἰουδαῖοι θανάτῳ*); "Both now and ever...": **"O Theotokos, thou art the true vine that blossomed for us the fruit of life..."** (*Θεοτόκε, σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος*). The Second Choir begins the first Idiomelon in Tone 6: **"Through fear of the Jews, Peter Thy friend and companion denied Thee, O Lord..."** (*Διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων*); then the First Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 6: **"Before Thy precious Cross, when the soldiers mocked Thee, O Lord, the angelic hosts were struck with dread..."** (*Πρὸ τοῦ τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ*), preceded by the verse: **"Give ear to my words, O Lord; understand my cry"** (*Τὰ ῥήματά μου ἐνώτισαι Κύριε*, Ps. 5:1 [LXX]). Then the Second Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Drawn upon the Cross, Thou didst cry aloud, O Lord: For which deed do the Jews wish to stone Me? Because I healed their paralytics?..."** (*Ἑλκόμενος ἐπὶ Σταυροῦ*). The Prophecy: Isaiah 50:4–11 [LXX] (The Obedient Servant Gives His Back to Scourges); the Epistle: Romans 5:6–10 (While We Were Still Sinners, Christ Died for Us); then the Gospel: Mark 15:16–41 (The Soldiers Mock Christ, the Crucifixion, and His Death on the Cross). The Reader: **"Blessed is the Lord God, blessed is the Lord day by day..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς Κύριος ὁ Θεός*), and the rest as above: the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."**, **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times), **"Thou Who at all times..."**, the Prayer of Saint Mardarios: **"O Master God, Father Almighty, Lord, Only-Begotten Son Jesus Christ, and Holy Spirit, one Divinity, one Power, have mercy on me a sinner..."** (*Δέσποτα Θεέ*), and the Sixth Hour begins.[^448]

units.slavonic_text: 81.    Around the First Hour of the morning (7 a.m.), the Priest blesses and the Proestos says “O Heavenly King, {Comforter, the Spirit of Truth}.” The Reader: the Trisagion. The Priest: “For Yours is [the kingdom and the power].” The Reader: “Lord, have mercy” (12 times). Glory, Now and ever, “O come let us worship” (3 times) and he reads the Psalms of the First Hour [Psalms 5, 2, 21]. Glory, “O Christ, by Your being crucified {the tyrant has been destroyed},” Now and ever, “What shall we call you, {O full of grace?}” The First Choir sings the first Idiomelon {“Today the curtain of the Temple is rent”}. The Second Choir sings the second Idiomelon {“As a sheep to the slaughter You were brought, O Christ”} preceded by the Verse “Why have the nations raged?” [Psalm 2:1]. Then the First Choir sings Glory, Now and ever, “To the transgressors who took You, {O Christ, have You come and cried out aloud}.” The Reader: the Prophecy [Zacharias 11:10-13] and the Apostolos [Galatians 6:14-18]. The Gospel [Matthew 27:1-56] is then read. The Reader: “[Order] my steps [according to Your word].” The Trisagion, [Glory, Now and ever, “All-Holy Trinity, have mercy on us]; Kontakion “[O come let us all sing the praises of Him] Who was crucified for us,” “Lord, have mercy” (40 times). “You Who at every season [and every hour].” And the Proestos says the prayer “O Christ, the [True] Light [do enlighten and sanctify every man who comes into the world],” and the Third Hour begins.⁴⁵
units.english_text: 45. At this Hour, as also at the two following Hours, one Deacon in turn according to the order of seniority, vested in the customary mandya, censes with the hand-censer [*katzion*].

units.english_text: 83. units.english_text: 82.    The Sixth Hour begins as the previous two Hours, with Psalms 53, 139, and 90 [LXX]. "Glory...": **"Thou hast worked salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; Thou didst stretch out Thy most pure hands upon the Cross; Thou didst gather all the nations that cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, glory to Thee!"** (*Εἰργάσω σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς*); "Both now and ever...": **"Seeing that we have no boldness because of our manifold sins, do thou entreat Him Who was born of thee, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν παρρησίαν*). The First Choir chants the first Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"Thus saith the Lord unto the Jews: My people, what have I done unto you, or wherein have I grieved you? Your blind have I given sight, your lepers have I cleansed, the man lying on his pallet have I restored. My people, what have I done unto you, and wherewith have you repaid Me? Instead of manna, gall; instead of water, vinegar; instead of loving Me, you have nailed Me to the Cross!..."** (*Τάδε λέγει Κύριος πρὸς Ἰουδαίους*); the Second Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 8: **"O lawgivers of Israel, Jews and Pharisees, the choir of the Apostles cries aloud unto you: Behold the Temple which you destroyed; behold the Lamb Whom you crucified and delivered unto the tomb!..."** (*Οἱ νομοθέται Ἰσραήλ*), preceded by the verse: **"They gave Me gall for My food, and for My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink"** (*Ἔδωκαν εἰς τὸ βρῶμά μου χολὴν*, Ps. 68:21 [LXX]). Then the First Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Come, O Christ-bearing peoples, let us behold what counsel Judas the traitor took with the lawless priests against our Savior..."** (*Δεῦτε χριστοφόροι λαοί*). Next, the Prophecy: Isaiah 52:13–54:1 [LXX] (The Suffering Servant: He Was Wounded for Our Transgressions); the Epistle: Hebrews 2:11–18 (He Who Sanctifies and Those Who Are Sanctified Are All from One); and the Gospel: Luke 23:32–49 (The Crucifixion, the Penitent Thief, the Veil Rent, and the Death of Jesus). The Reader: **"Let Thy tender mercies speedily prevent us, O Lord, for we are brought very low..."** (*Ταχὺ προκαταλαβέτωσαν ἡμᾶς οἱ οἰκτιρμοί σου*, Ps. 78:8 [LXX]), the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."**, **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times), **"Thou Who at all times..."**, the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great: **"O God and Lord of powers, and Maker of all creation, Who through the compassion of Thine inscrutable mercy didst send down Thine Only-Begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of our race..."** (*Θεὲ καὶ Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*), and the Ninth Hour begins.

units.english_text: 83.    The Ninth Hour begins as the previous three Hours, with Psalms 68, 69, and 85 [LXX]. "Glory...": **"When the thief beheld the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, he said: If Thou wert not God incarnate Who art crucified with us, the sun would not have hidden its rays, nor would the earth have shaken with trembling. But O Thou Who endurest all things, remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!"** (*Ὁρῶν ὁ λῃστὴς τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς*); "Both now and ever...": **"O Good One, Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin and didst endure crucifixion, Who by death didst despoil death and didst manifest the Resurrection as God, despise not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine own hand..."** (*Ὁ δι' ἡμᾶς γεννηθεὶς ἐκ Παρθένου*). The Second Choir begins the first Idiomelon in Tone 7: **"A marvelous and fearful wonder it was to behold today: the Creator of heaven and earth hangs upon the Tree; He Who suspended the earth upon the waters is transfixed with nails; the sun hides its rays at the sight of the Master dishonored..."** (*Θάμβος ἦν κατιδεῖν τὸν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς Ποιητήν*); then the First Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 2: **"When the transgressors nailed the Lord of glory upon the Cross, they mocked Him and said: If Thou art the Son of God, save Thyself and come down from the Cross!..."** (*Ὅτε σε σταυρῷ προσήλωσαν παράνομοι*), preceded by the verse: **"They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"** (*Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς*, Ps. 21:18 [LXX]). The Second Choir takes up the conclusion to this Idiomelon: **"...Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit!"** (*Σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι*). The First Choir chants: **"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit"**; the Second Choir: **"Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** At this point the Canonarch, coming into the middle of the temple [before the Holy Cross], intones in the recitative manner of the Epistle the solemn Sticheron:

units.slavonic_text: 82.    The Sixth Hour begins as the previous two Hours [Psalms 54, 140, and 91]; {Glory, “You, O Christ God, worked out salvation.” Now and ever, “As there is no boldness in us because of the multitude of our sins.” The First Choir sings the first Idiomelon {“This is what the Lord said to the Jews.” The Second Choir sings the Second Idiomelon “You, the lawmakers of Israel,”} preceded by the Verse “They gave me poison for food, {and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink}.” {Psalm 69:21}. Then the First Choir sings Glory, Now and ever, “Come, you people, bearers of Christ {and see what Judas}.” The Prophecy {Isaiah 52:13-54:1}. The Apostolos {Hebrews 2:11-18} and the Gospel {Luke 23:32-49}. {The Reader: “Let Your tender mercies, O Lord, speedily go before us.”} Then the rest as before with the prayer “O God and Lord {of the angelic hosts},” and the Ninth Hour begins.

units.slavonic_text: 83.    We begin the Ninth Hour as we did the previous three Hours {but with Psalms 69, 70, and 86; Glory, “The thief said, as he beheld the Author of life, hanging upon the Cross.” Now and ever, “O good Lord, for our sakes You were born of a Virgin and have endured crucifixion.”} The Second Choir sings the first Idiomelon {“A dazzling wonder it was to see the Maker of heaven and earth.”} Then the First Choir sings the second Idiomelon “When the transgressors nailed the Lord of glory upon the Cross,” preceded by the Verse “They divided my garments among them.” The Second Choir sings the conclusion to the above Idiomelon: “...with the Father and the Spirit.” The First Choir sings “Glory to the Father {and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit}.” The Second Choir, “Now and ever {and to the ages of ages. Amen.}” At this point the Canonarch, coming to the middle of the Church, {stands facing the Crucifix and} intones in the manner of the Apostolos the Stichiron: Today is hung upon the Tree, He Who suspended the Land in the midst of the waters... (3 times) {A Crown of thorns crowns Him, Who is the King of Angels. He is wrapped about with the purple of mockery, Who wrapped the Heavens with clouds. He received buffetings, Who freed Adam in Jordan. He was transfixed with nails, Who is the Bridegroom of the Church. He was pierced with a spear Who is the son of the Virgin.} We worship Your Passion, O Christ. (3 times)

units.english_text: Then this same Sticheron is chanted by both choirs verse by verse. The Prophecy: Jeremiah 11:18–12:5, 9–11, 14–15 [LXX] (The Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter); the Epistle: Hebrews 10:19–31 (A New and Living Way Opened through the Veil of His Flesh); the Gospel: John 19:23–37 (The Crucifixion, the Parting of the Garments, "It Is Finished", and the Piercing of His Side). The Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Kontakion: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."**; **"Lord, have mercy"** (40 times); **"Thou Who at all times..."**; the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great: **"O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast patiently endured our transgressions, and hast brought us even unto this present hour, in which, hanging upon the life-creating Tree, Thou didst open the way into Paradise unto the penitent thief, and by death didst destroy death..."** (*Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ*); the Dismissal, and begins...[^449]

units.english_text: 84.    Ἐν τῷ Μ. Ἑσπερινῷ, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακόν, εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα* ψάλλομεν τὰ τῶν Ἀποστίχων ε΄ Ἰδιόμελα *Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις* [Δὶς] κτλ. εἰς ϛ΄. *Δόξα, Ὢ πῶς ἡ παράνομος συναγωγή, Καὶ νῦν, Φοβερὸν καὶ παράδοξον μυστήριον*, Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, τὸ *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* καὶ εὐθὺς τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα, ὁ Ἀπόστολος καὶ ἀπ' ἄμβωνος τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· τὸ *Εἴπωμεν πάντες*, τὸ *Καταξίωσον*, *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*, καὶ μετὰ τὸ *Εἴη τὸ κράτος*, οἱ Χοροὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὴν βορείαν Πύλην τοῦ ἁγίου Βήματος καὶ ἄρχονται ψάλλοντες τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, ἓξ δὲ Ἱερεῖς ἀσκεπεῖς ἐνδεδυμένοι φελώνια καὶ αἴροντες μετ' εὐλαβείας ἐπὶ κεφαλῆς τὸν ἐπιτάφιον, ἐξ ὧν ὁ Μέγας Ἀρχιμανδρίτης φέρει ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον, ἐξέρχονται τοῦ ἱεροῦ Βήματος προπορευομένων τῶν λαμπάδων, τῶν ἑξαπτερύγων, τῶν Ψαλτῶν, τοῦ Πριμικηρίου μετὰ τοῦ Διβαμβούλου καὶ τῶν Διακόνων θυμιώντων ἔρχονται εἰς τὸ μέσον τοῦ Ναοῦ ὅπου ἵσταται ηὐτρεπισμένον τὸ Κουβούκλιον, καὶ οἱ μὲν Χοροὶ τῶν Ψαλτῶν ἵστανται κατὰ σειρὰν ψάλλοντες τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν Ἀποστίχων, οἱ δὲ Ἱερεῖς φέροντες ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον, ποιοῦσι τρεῖς κύκλους περὶ τὸ Κουβούκλιον, εἶτα τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ἐντὸς τοῦ Κουβουκλίου, καὶ ὁ Μ. Ἐκκλησιάρχης ῥαίνει μὲ εὔοσμα ἄνθη αὐτό, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης κατερχόμενος τοῦ Θρόνου προσέρχεται, ἀσπάζεται τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον καὶ τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον καὶ εὐλογήσας τὸν λαόν, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*, ἀνέρχεται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον, οἱ δὲ ἅγιοι Ἀρχιερεῖς προσερχόμενοι ἀνὰ δύο ἀσπάζονται ἐπίσης καὶ ἔπειτα λαμβάνουσι παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἄνθη, ὡσαύτως καὶ πάντες

units.english_text: This is repeated antiphonally by both choirs verse by verse. Then the Prophecy (Jeremiah 11:18–12:4, 9–10, and 14–15 [LXX]: The Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter); the Epistle (Hebrews 10:19–31: A New and Living Way Opened through the Veil of His Flesh); and the Gospel (John 19:23–37: The Parting of the Garments, "It Is Finished", and the Piercing of His Side). Then the Reader: **"Deliver us not up utterly, for Thy holy Name's sake, and make not Thy covenant void..."** (*Μὴ δὴ παραδῴης ἡμᾶς εἰς τέλος*). Then the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us..."** (*Τὸν δι' ἡμᾶς σταυρωθέντα*), etc., as at the First Hour; the prayer: **"O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God..."** (*Δέσποτα Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ*); and the Dismissal. Then Vespers begins.

units.slavonic_text: VESPERS [OF GREAT FRIDAY] [TAKING DOWN THE BODY OF CHRIST FROM THE CROSS]
units.english_text: 84.    At Great Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the five Idiomela of the Aposticha for six verses: 1. **"All creation was altered with fear when it beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ..."** (*Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις ἠλλοιοῦτο φόβῳ*) (twice); 2. **"Why does the impious and lawless people imagine vain things?..."** (*Λαὸς δυσσεβὴς καὶ παράνομος*); 3. **"Today, seeing Thee, O Word, hanging upon the Cross, the blameless Virgin wept..."** (*Σήμερον σὲ θεωροῦσα ἡ ἄμεμπτος Παρθένος*); 4. **"Beholding Thee, the Creator and God of all, lifted up upon the Tree..."** (*Ἐπὶ ξύλου βλέπουσα κρεμάμενον*); 5. **"Today the Master of creation stands before Pilate..."** (*Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης τῆς κτίσεως*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"O how did the lawless assembly condemn the King of creation to death!..."** (*Ὢ πῶς ἡ παράνομος συναγωγή*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"A fearful and marvelous mystery is seen accomplished today: He Who is untouchable is held fast..."** (*Φοβερὸν καὶ παράδοξον μυστήριον*). The Entrance is made with the Gospel Book; **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*); and immediately the Readings: Exodus 33:11–23 [LXX] (The Lord Speaks with Moses Face to Face, and Moses Beholds the Glory of God from the Cleft of the Rock); Job 42:12–17 [LXX] (The Lord Blesses the Latter End of Job More than His Beginning); and Isaiah 52:13–54:1 [LXX] (The Fourth Servant Song: "Behold, My Servant Shall Prosper"). The Epistle: 1 Corinthians 1:18–31; 2:1–2 (The Word of the Cross is Foolishness to Those Who Perish, but to Us Who Are Saved It Is the Power of God); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:1–38; Luke 23:39–43; Matthew 27:39–54; John 19:31–37; Matthew 27:55–61 (The Composite Passion Gospel of the Crucifixion, the Death, and the Deposition of the Lord) read from the ambo. [At this point, while the words are read: "Now when evening was come, there came a rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph...", the body of the Lord is taken down from the Cross and wrapped in a clean linen sheet. When the Gospel reading is completed, the Priest receives the Sacred Body and carries It into the Sanctuary]. Then the litanies: **"Let us all say with our whole soul..."** (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*); **"Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin..."** (*Καταξίωσον*); **"Let us complete our evening supplication unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*). After the exclamation: **"Blessed and glorified be the might of Thy kingdom: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος*), the choirs assemble by the northern door of the Sanctuary and begin chanting the Aposticha. Six Priests with heads uncovered (not wearing the kamilavkion), vested in phelonia [and epitrachilia], bearing the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] upon their heads with reverence, among whom the Great Archimandrite carries also the Holy Gospel Book in his right hand, exit from the Sanctuary preceded by candles, processional fans [hexapteryga], the chanters, the Dean of the church [Primikirios] with the two-branched candlestick [divamvoulon], and the deacons censing; they advance to the middle of the temple, where the Tomb [Sepulchre / Kuvuklion] stands prepared...[^450]

units.english_text:
1. **"The noble Joseph, taking down Thine undefiled Body from the Tree, wrapped It in a clean linen shroud and with sweet spices, and laid It for burial in a new tomb"** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ, ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου καθελὼν τὸ ἄχραντόν σου Σῶμα, σινδόνι καθαρᾷ εἱλήσας καὶ ἀρώμασιν, ἐν μνήματι καινῷ κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*), chanted until **"and laid It for burial"** (*κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*);
2. **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women the angel stood by the tomb and cried aloud: Myrrh is fitting for the dead, but Christ has shown Himself foreign to corruption"** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί, παρὰ τὸ μνῆμα ἐπιστάς, ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα· Τὰ μύρα τοῖς θνητοῖς ὑπάρχει ἁρμόδια, Χριστὸς δὲ διαφθορᾶς ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*), chanted until **"foreign to corruption"** (*διαφθορᾶς ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*).

units.slavonic_incipit: carrying a Divamvulon, and the Deacons
units.slavonic_text: carrying a Divamvulon, and the Deacons censing; when they arrive in the center of the Church where the Sepulchre [Kuvuklion] stands ornamented, the choirs of chanters stand in their accustomed place and continue the rest of the Aposticha. The Priests, who are bearing the Epitaphios [a cloth depicting Christ's burial] upon their heads, circle the Sepulchre three times, then they place the Epitaphios inside the Sepulchre and the Great Ecclesiarch sprinkles it with sweet-smelling flowers. The Patriarch descends from the Throne and venerates the Gospel and the Epitaphios. He blesses the people while the choirs sing “For many years, [Master]” after which he returns to the Throne. The rest of the Bishops approach two by two, venerate and then receive flowers from the Patriarch, as do all the other Ecclesiastical officials. Meanwhile, the Second Choir slowly and with melody chants Glory, Now and ever, “You Who have been wrapped in light as in a garment.” Then, “Lord, now let Your servant {depart in peace}.” The Trisagion; then the Apolytikia in Mode II: 1. Noble Joseph [taking down Your undefiled body from the Tree after wrapping it in fair linen with sweet spices, until he laid it for burial in a new tomb. 2. The angel stood by the tomb and to the women bearing myrrh [he cried aloud: “Myrrh is fitting for the dead, until while Christ has shown Himself foreign to corruption].”
units.english_text: The Dismissal: **"Wisdom!"**; **"Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**; **"Glory to Thee, O God, our hope, glory to Thee. May Christ our true God, Who for us men and for our salvation condescended to the terrible Passions and the life-giving Cross and voluntary entombment in the flesh, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς . . . ὁ δι' ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν τὰ φρικτὰ Πάθη καὶ τὸν ζωοποιὸν Σταυρὸν καὶ τὴν ἑκούσιον ταφὴν σαρκὶ καταδεξάμενος Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς...*), and: **"Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."** (*Δι' εὐχῶν*).

units.slavonic_text: --- 46. For the reason that many in the cities have difficulty in leaving their homes around midnight [in order to attend the Matins Service at the Seventh Hour, that is, at 1 a.m.], for the sake of “ikonomia” and for the ease of all, the custom arose of celebrating this Matins Service at the same hour as that of the Matins of the Bridegroom, that is, at the First Hour of the night (7 p.m.). The Liturgy itself was put off until the next morning. As a result, the great length of one single liturgical event presenting both Matins and the Liturgy was alleviated by celebrating these services as two separate events done at different times.

units.english_text: 85.    Περὶ τὴν ζ΄ ὥραν τῆς νυκτὸς⁴⁶ ἀναγινώσκεται συνήθως ὁ Ἄμωμος, καὶ τὰ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ τοῦ Μ. Σαββάτου παραλειπόμενα Ἀναγνώσματα⁴⁷. Μετὰ τὸ *Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, *Σῶσον Κύριε* κτλ. καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ *Θεὸς Κύριος* τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια *Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ* μέχρι τοῦ *κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο, Δόξα, Ὅτε κατῆλθες* ὁλόκληρον, *Καὶ νῦν, Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξὶ* μέχρι τοῦ *ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*· εἶτα Συναπτὴ μικρὰ καὶ ψάλλεται τὸ Κάθισμα *Σινδόνι καθαρᾷ* ἅπαξ, ἀργῶς, *Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἐξέστησαν χοροὶ* ὡσαύτως,⁴⁸ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ ὁ Κανὼν *Κύματι θαλάσσης* εἰς ϛ΄, ἐν ἑκάστῃ δὲ Ὠδῇ ἐπιλέγεται καὶ ὁ Εἱρμός. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα *Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ* ἅπαξ καὶ τοῦτο ἀργῶς·⁴⁹ ἀφ' ϛ΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἡμέρας, καὶ ἀκολούθως ἡ ζ΄ καὶ ἡ η΄ Ὠδὴ τοῦ Κανόνος· εἶτα *Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Κανόνος Ὠδή, εἰς τὸ τέλος τῆς θ΄ ἐξέρχεται ὁ Πατριάρχης ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἱεροῦ Βήματος ἐνδεδυμένος ἅπασαν τὴν ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν, προπορευομένων τῶν Ἁγίων Ἀρχιερέων, καὶ ψάλλων τὸ *Ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τάφῳ*, προχωρεῖ πρὸς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον καὶ θυμιᾷ αὐτὸν σταυροειδῶς, ἀκολούθως δὲ πάντα τὸν λαόν· οἱ δὲ Ἀρχιερεῖς ἱστάμενοι ἐν χοροστασίᾳ ψάλλουσι τὰ ἐγκώμια τῆς α΄ Στάσεως, ἕως οὗ ἐπιστρέψῃ ὁ Πατριάρχης εἰς τὸν Θρόνον, εἶτα αὖθις τὸ πρῶτον τροπάριον,
