units.english_text: 85.    Around the Seventh Hour of the night [1:00 a.m.]⁴⁶ the Amomos [Psalm 118 LXX: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way..."] and the Old Testament readings omitted from the Vespers of Great Saturday are customarily read here.⁴⁷ Then the Priest says: **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"**; the Superior [Proestos]: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers; the Priest: **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**; the Reader: the Troparia: **"Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance..."** (*Σῶσον Κύριε*); **"Glory..."**: **"Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God..."**; **"Both now and ever..."**: **"O awesome and unashamed protection, all-lauded Theotokos..."**; and the Six Psalms [Ps. 3, 37, 62, 87, 102, and 142 LXX]. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*), the Dismissal Troparia in Tone 2: **"The noble Joseph..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ*) until **"and laid It for burial"** (*κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*); **"Glory..."**: Tone 2: **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Divinity..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*) in its entirety; **"Both now and ever..."**: Tone 2: **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women..."** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί*) until **"foreign to corruption"** (*ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*). Then the Small Litany, and the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1 is chanted: **"In a clean shroud and with spices, the noble Joseph, taking down Thine all-pure Body from the Tree, wrapped It and laid It in a new tomb; and so early in the morning the myrrh-bearing women cried aloud: Show us, O Christ, Thy Resurrection!"** (*Σινδόνι καθαρᾷ*) once, slowly; **"Glory... Both now and ever..."**: Tone 1: **"The angelic choirs were astounded at the sight of Him Who rests in the bosom of the Father being laid in a tomb as a mortal..."** (*Ἐξέστησαν χοροί*) likewise slowly.⁴⁸ Then Psalm 50 [LXX], and the Canon in Tone 6: **"Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves; but the children of those who were saved bury beneath the earth Him Who was hidden..."** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*) for six Troparia, the Heirmos being repeated slowly at the end of each Ode as Katavasia. After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1: **"Thy tomb, O Savior, the soldiers guarding became as dead men; and the angel sat upon the stone proclaiming the Resurrection unto the women..."** (*Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτήρ*) once, and this also slowly.⁴⁹ After Ode 6, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 2: **"He Who closed the abyss is beheld dead, and wrapped in fine linen and myrrh, the Immortal One is laid in a tomb as a mortal; and the women came to anoint Him with myrrh, weeping bitterly and crying aloud: This Sabbath is most blessed, in which Christ, having fallen asleep, shall rise again on the third day!"** (*Τὴν ἄβυσσον ὁ κλείσας*); the Ikos; the Menologion; and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the day from the Triodion; then follow Odes 7 and 8 of the Canon. The Deacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the Ninth Ode of the Canon is chanted. At the conclusion of Ode 9, the Patriarch, fully vested in all his hierarchical vestments, exits from the Sanctuary preceded by the holy Hierarchs; chanting the opening verse of the Lamentations [Enkomia]: **"Life in the tomb art Thou laid, O Christ, and the angelic hosts were astounded, glorifying Thy condescension"** (*Ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τάφῳ κατετέθης Χριστέ*), he advances toward the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] and censes it cross-wise, and afterward censes all the people. The Hierarchs, standing in choir formation, chant the Lamentations of the First Stasis until the Patriarch returns to the throne; then the first Troparion is chanted again.

units.slavonic_text: 85.    Around the Seventh Hour of the night (1 a.m.)⁴⁶ the Amomos [Psalm 118] and the omitted readings of the Vespers of Great Saturday are customarily read here.⁴⁷ [Then, the] Priest: “Blessed be our God {always, now and ever, Glory to You, our God, glory to You. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of Truth.”} The Trisagion; “Lord, save {Your people.” Glory, “O Christ our God, Who was of Your own will.” Now and ever, “O awful and ever-present protection all-lauded Theotokos”} and the Exapsalmos [the six Psalms 3,37,62,87,102 and 142]. At “God the Lord,” the Apolytikia: “Noble Joseph {taking down Your undefiled body}” until “laid it for burial {in a new tomb}.” Glory, “When You had gone down {to death}” (the entire hymn), Now and ever, “{The angel stood by the tomb} and to the women bearing spices,” until “Christ has shown Himself foreign {to corruption}.” Then the Small Litany and the Kathisma “In a clean shroud,” (once, slowly) is chanted. Glory, Now and ever, “The angelic choirs were filled with dread {as they beheld Him}.”⁴⁸ Then Psalm 50 and the Canon “In the waves of the sea,” in six with the Irmos being repeated at the end of each Ode. After the Third Ode, the Kathisma {“The soldiers keeping watch over Your tomb, O Savior,” (once, and this also slowly).⁴⁹ After the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion, Ikos, Minologion and the Postscript of the Day from the Triodion; then follow the Seventh and Eighth Odes of the Canon. Deacon: “The Theotokos and Mother of the Light.” Then the Ninth Ode of the Canon is chanted, at the end of which the Patriarch vested in his complete hierarchical vestments exits from the Holy Sanctuary {Vima}, preceded by the rest of the Hierarchs, singing “O Christ, the Life, You have been laid in a tomb.” He proceeds toward the Epitaphios, censes it cross-wise, then censes all the people; the Hierarchs, standing in formation, sing the First Stasis of the Lamentations until the Patriarch returns to the Throne; then the first verse of the First Stasis is repeated.

units.slavonic_text: --- 47. If, however, Matins is sung at the First Hour of the night (7 p.m.), then Psalm 119 and the Readings are read in the morning before Vespers. 48. At this point, the Great Archdeacon and the rest of the Deacons receive Keron [the blessing from the Patriarch to participate in the Service], enter into the Holy Sanctuary [Vima], put on their vestments, and, coming out, stand before the Patriarch with Dikirotrikira. 49. At the Fourth Ode of the Canon the Patriarch (or the Archbishop) enters the Holy Sanctuary [Vima] and vests along with the rest of the Bishops.

units.slavonic_incipit: The Patriarch along with the other
units.slavonic_text: The Patriarch along with the other Bishops begins the Second Stasis “It is right and meet {to magnify You, the Giver of life}”; at the end [of the Second Stasis], the first verse of this Stasis is repeated. Then the Small Litany with the Exclamation by the Patriarch: For holy are You, O our God, {Who sits upon the Throne of glory of the Cherubim and unto You we ascribe glory together with Your Father Who is without beginning and Your most holy, good and life-giving Spirit, now and ever and unto the ages of ages. Amen.}
units.english_text: They then begin the Third Stasis: **"All generations offer a hymn unto Thy burial, O my Christ"** (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι ὕμνον τῇ ταφῇ σου προσφέρουσι Χριστέ μου*). At the verse: **"The myrrh-bearing women came early in the morning and sprinkled myrrh upon Thy tomb"** (*Ἔρραναν τὸν τάφον αἱ Μυροφόροι μύρα, λίαν πρωῒ ἐλθοῦσαι*), the Patriarch descends from the throne, receives a sprinkler [*kanion*] from the Ecclesiarch, and singing this same verse (which is repeated three times), sprinkles the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] with rose-water. The Third Stasis having been completed, its first verse is repeated again. Then the Small Litany, with the exclamation by the Patriarch:

units.slavonic_incipit: The Patriarch along with the rest
units.slavonic_text: The Patriarch along with the rest of the Hierarchs begins to sing the Evlogitária. units.slavonic_text: [Original Greek Text: Holy Week: Great and Holy Saturday (Matins Concluded: Praises, Epitaphios Procession, and Dismissal) (§ 85 Concluded) (p. 774)]
units.english_text: ἡμῶν ἐκ γ΄ (τοῦτο καὶ μόνον), εἶτα τὸ *Πᾶσα πνοὴ* καὶ οἱ Αἶνοι⁵⁰ εἰς δ΄· *Δόξα, Τὴν σήμερον μυστικῶς, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Δοξολογία Μ. εἰς τὸ τέλος ψάλλεται τὸ Ἀσματικὸν *Ἅγιος ὁ Θεὸς* ὑπὸ τῶν χορῶν προπορευομένων τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου κατὰ τὴν ἑξῆς τάξιν· πρῶτοι ἡγοῦνται οἱ ἱερεῖς, εἶτα ἕπονται οἱ ψάλται. μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς αἴροντες τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον· οὕτω γίνεται ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ ναοῦ ἔξοδος καὶ ἡ ἐπάνοδος ἐπίσης. Ἐπανελθὼν ἐν τῷ Ναῷ ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ Ἱερὸν καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκφωνεῖ *Πρόσχωμεν, Εἰρήνη πᾶσι· Σοφία*· ψάλλει τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια *Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον* καὶ θυμιᾷ κύκλῳ τὴν Ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν προπορευόμενος ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου, εἶτα⁵¹ τὸ *Ταῖς Μυροφόροις γυναιξὶ* μέχρι τοῦ *ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*, ἑπομένως τὸ *Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ* μέχρι τοῦ *κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*, καὶ τιθέασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὸν Ἐπιτάφιον ἐπὶ τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης, ὁ δὲ Ἀναγνώστης ἔξωθεν ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Τροπάριον τῆς Προφητείας *Ὁ συνέχων τὰ πέρατα*, τὸ Προκείμενον, τὴν Προφητείαν καὶ ἀκολούθως τὸν Ἀπόστολον, καὶ ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, ἔμπροσθεν τῆς ὡραίας Πύλης. Μετὰ τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη* ἐκδύεται τὴν Ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν,⁵² ἐνδύεται τὸν Μανδύαν καὶ κρατῶν τὴν ποιμαντορικὴν ῥάβδον ἐξέρχεται τοῦ Βήματος καὶ ἵσταται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον. Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ τούτῳ ὁ Ἀρχιδιάκονος λέγει τὴν Ἐκτενῆ *Εἴπωμεν πάντες*, *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν Ἑωθινήν*, ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Σὸν γάρ ἐστι* καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Ἱερέως (ἡ χθὲς σημειωθεῖσα ἤτοι *Ὁ δι' ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν σωτηρίαν τὰ φρικτὰ Πάθη*) καὶ ἄρχεται

units.english_text: ... **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (*Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*) three times (this text only); then **"Let every breath"** and the Praises for four verses: 1. **"Today the tomb holds Him Who holds creation in the palm of His hand..."** (*Σήμερον συνέχει τάφος*); 2. **"What is this sight that we behold? What is this present rest?..."** (*Τί τὸ ὁρώμενον θέαμα;*); 3. **"Come, let us behold our Life lying in the tomb..."** (*Δεῦτε ἴδωμεν τὴν ζωὴν ἡμῶν*); 4. **"Joseph asked for the Body of Jesus, and laid It in his own new tomb..."** (*ᾐτήσατο Ἰωσὴφ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ*). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 2: **"This present day Moses mystically prefigured, saying: And God blessed the seventh day..."** (*Τὴν σήμερον μυστικῶς ὁ μέγας Μωϋσῆς προδιετυποῦτο λέγων*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 2: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις, Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*). The Great Doxology is chanted; at its conclusion, the Asmatikon: **"Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us"** (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*) is chanted slowly by the choirs, who precede the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] in solemn procession, exiting from and circling back into the church. The order of the procession is as follows: first the priests lead the way, then follow the chanters, and after them the Patriarch with the Hierarchs bearing the Epitaphios upon their heads; thus is conducted the exit from the temple and likewise the return. Having returned into the church, the Patriarch with the rest of the procession enters the Sanctuary, and immediately exclaims: **"Let us attend! Peace be unto all! Wisdom!"** (*Πρόσχωμεν. Εἰρήνη πᾶσι. Σοφία*). Then he chants the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 2: **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*), and censes around the Holy Altar Table, processing in front of the Epitaphios; then the Troparion:⁵¹* **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women..."** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί*) until **"foreign to corruption"** (*ἐδείχθη ἀλλότριος*); next the Troparion: **"The noble Joseph..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ*) until **"and laid It for burial"** (*κηδεύσας ἀπέθετο*); and the priests place the Epitaphios upon the Holy Altar Table. The Reader outside the iconostasis reads the Troparion of the Prophecy in Tone 2: **"O Christ, Who holdest fast the ends of the earth, Thou didst deign to be held fast in a narrow tomb..."** (*Ὁ συνέχων τὰ πέρατα*); the Prokimenon in Tone 4: **"Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for Thy Name's sake!"** (*Ἀνάστα, Κύριε, βοήθησον ἡμῖν*, Ps. 43:26 [LXX]); the Prophecy: Ezekiel 37:1–14 [LXX] (The Vision of the Dry Bones in the Valley Brought to Life: "Behold, I Will Open Your Graves, and Cause You to Come Up out of Your Graves, O My People"); the Epistle: 1 Corinthians 5:6–8 and Galatians 3:13–14 (Christ Our Passover is Sacrificed for Us, and Has Redeemed Us from the Curse of the Law); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:62–66 (The Chief Priests and the Pharisees Seal the Tomb and Post the Roman Guard) read by the Patriarch before the Royal Doors [Beautiful Gate]. After **"Many years to you, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he unvests from his hierarchical vestments,⁵²* puts on his monastic mandya, and holding his pastoral staff exits from the Sanctuary and takes his place upon the throne. In the meantime, the Archdeacon recites the Augmented Litany: **"Let us all say with our whole soul..."** (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*), and **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν*). The Priest gives the exclamation: **"For Thine it is to show mercy and to save us, O Christ our God..."** (*Σὸν γάρ ἐστι τὸ ἐλεεῖν καὶ σῴζειν ἡμᾶς*), and the Dismissal is given by the Priest (as noted yesterday): **"May Christ, our true God, Who for us men and for our salvation voluntarily endured His terrible Passions, the Cross, and voluntary entombment in the flesh, have mercy on us and save us..."**; and then begins...[^454]

units.slavonic_text: {“Today the tomb holds Him Who holds,” “What is this sight we behold? What is the present rest? “Come you and behold our Life lying in the tomb,” “Joseph asked for the Body of Christ and he laid it in a new tomb,”} Glory, “{Moses the Great} secretly forefigured this present day {saying}.” Now and ever, “Most blessed.” The Great Doxology and at the end the Melismatic [Asmatikon] “Holy God” is sung by the choirs which precede the Epitaphios in a procession, exiting from and returning to the church. The order of procession is as follows: first the Priests, then the chanters, and after them the Patriarch with the Hierarchs carrying the Epitaphios. Returning to the Church with the rest of the procession, the Patriarch enters the Holy Sanctuary [Vima] and immediately exclaims “Let us attend. Peace be with you. Wisdom.” Then he chants “When You had gone down to death,” while he proceeds to cense the Epitaphios which is being carried around the Holy Altar Table by the Hierarchs, then the hymn⁵¹* “The angel stood by the tomb” is chanted until “Christ has shown Himself foreign {to corruption}” and then the hymn “Noble Joseph taking down Your undefiled body” until “laid it in a tomb.” Then the Priests place the Epitaphios upon the Altar Table. Then the Reader reads the Troparion of the Prophecy “O Christ, Who holds fast the ends of the earth”; the Prophecy {Ezekiel 37:1-14}. The Apostolos {1 Corinthians 5:6-8 and Galatians 3:13-14}. The Gospel {Matthew 27:62-66} is read by the Patriarch in front of the Beautiful Gate. After “For many years, [Master],” he unvests from his Hierarchical vestments,⁵²* puts on the Mantle [Mandya], and holding the pastoral staff exits from the Sanctuary and stands at the Throne. In the meantime the Archdeacon says the Litany “Let us say with all our soul,” “Let us complete our morning supplication.” The Priest: “For to You belong {mercy and salvation}” and the Dismissal by the Priest (as yesterday): “May Christ, our True God, Who for us men and for our salvation voluntarily endured His terrible Passion, the Cross, and the entombment in the flesh, have mercy upon us.”
units.english_text: 52.* If the Matins of the Epitaphios is chanted at the First Hour of the night (7:00 p.m.), in which case Vespers and the Divine Liturgy do not immediately follow Matins, the Patriarch [or presiding Hierarch] does not unvest from his hierarchical vestments, but remains in the Sanctuary until the end, where he himself pronounces the Dismissal of the section.

units.slavonic_text: 86.    The Archdeacon: "Bless, Master!" The Priest: "Blessed is the Kingdom of the Father." The Patriarch: the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103). At "Lord, I have cried," the following eight Stichira are chanted: four of the Resurrection and four [Stichira Idiomela] of the day as follows: {1. "Accept our evening prayers, O Holy Lord." 2. "Walk about Zion, you people and encompass her...." 3. "Come, you people, praise and worship Christ...." 4. "We were set free by Your passion, O Christ...." 5&6. "Today Hell groaning cries aloud: Woe is me if only I had not accepted Him that was born of Mary...." (twice), 7. "Today hell groaning cries aloud: my power has been destroyed: I have accepted this dead man as one of the dead...." 8. "Today hell groaning cries aloud: my dominion has been offered in sacrifice; the Shepherd has been crucified and He has raised Adam...."}. Glory, "{Moses the Great} secretly forefigured this present day {saying...}" Now and ever, "{Let us praise the Virgin Mary,} glory of all the world and {doorway to heaven.}" Entrance with the Gospel, "O Gladsome Light." {There is no Prokimenon} then immediately the Readings: 1. "In the beginning, God created [heaven and earth...] (Genesis 1:1-13. 2. "Now the word of the Lord came to Jonas [the son of Amathi...] (Jonah, the entire book). 3. "In his eighteenth year, King Nabuchodonosor made a statue of gold..." (Daniel 3:1-23). 4. Then the Prayer of Azariah: "Blessed are You, O Lord, the God of our fathers..." and, 5. The Hymn of the Three Youths [through verse 34]: "Blessed are You in the firmament of heaven and to be sung and glorified for ever." [Found in the Apocrypha of the Septuagint Old Testament.] At this point all stand and we begin chanting in Mode I the rest of the Hymn of the Three Youths [from Verse 35]: {"Bless the Lord, all works of the Lord, sing praise you the Lord and exalt Him forever." Then the rest of the verses through verse 66: "Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, sing praise to Him and highly exalt Him forever."} [After each of the intermittent verses, which are intoned by the Canonarch, the following is sung as a refrain: "Praise you, the Lord, and exalt Him forever."] The ending from verse 66 and the following as below: "O you Apostles, Prophets and Witnesses of the Lord, bless you the Lord," with the Refrain: "We bless the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, the Lord."

units.english_text: "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"Moses the great mystically prefigured this present day, saying: And God blessed the seventh day; for this is the blessed Sabbath, this is the day of rest, whereon the Only-Begotten Son of God rested from all His works..."** (*Τὴν σήμερον μυστικῶς ὁ μέγας Μωϋσῆς*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 1: **"Let us praise the Virgin Mary, the glory of the whole world, who sprang forth from mankind and gave birth to the Master, the gate of heaven..."** (*Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν*).

units.slavonic_text: "We praise, and exalt the Lord in all the Ages." "We praise, we bless, and worship the Lord." "We praise and glorify the Lord in all the Ages."} The Liturgy of Saint Basil follows. [Deacon: "Let us pray to the Lord." Priest: "For You our God are Holy...."] {Instead of the Trisagios Hymn, we sing "As many of you as were baptized into Christ, {have put on Christ. Alleluia.}" Apostolos of the day {Romans 6:3-11}; at the end, the Alleluia is not sung. Instead of it, immediately the Priest from within the Sanctuary chants the following Verses in Mode III Plagal [Varys], while at the same time he proceeds from the Sanctuary down the middle aisle, scattering bay leaves around the entire Church [as a sign of triumph and victory over death]: "Arise, O God, and judge You the earth; for You shall keep all nations in Your inheritance." {Psalm 81:8}. This verse is repeated after each of the following verses of Psalm 81, which are intoned by the Canonarch; {and after the final verse the "Arise, O God" is chanted in a slower and more majestic manner: "God stands in the congregation of the Gods; He is a Judge among Gods. {81:1} How long will you give wrong judgement and accept the persons of the ungodly? {81:2} Judge the weak and the fatherless; do justice to the humble and the poor. {81:3} Rescue the poor; and deliver the needy out of the hand of the sinner. {81:4} They have not known nor understood, but walk on in darkness; all the foundations of the earth shall be shaken. {81:5} "I have said, You are gods, and you are all children of the Most High, but you shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes." {81:6-7}. Then the Gospel "Now late in the night of the Sabbath" until "the completion of time" {Matthew 28:1-20} is read from the Pulpit. And then continues the Liturgy of St. Basil. Instead of the usual Cherubic Hymn the following [hymn] in Mode I Plagal is sung: "Let all mortal flesh be silent, and let it stand in fear and trembling. And let it take no thought for any earthly thing. For the King who reigns and the Lord who rules comes to the slaughter to give Himself as food to the faithful. Before Him go the choirs of angels with all the Principalities and Powers, [Great Entrance] the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim covering their faces and singing the hymn: Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia."
units.english_text: The Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great continues. The Deacon: **"Let us pray to the Lord"**; the Priest: **"For Holy art Thou, our God, and unto Thee we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**

units.english_text: **"Let all mortal flesh keep silence, and stand with fear and trembling, and ponder nothing earthly within itself; for the King of kings and Lord of lords cometh forth to be slain, and to be given as food to the faithful. units.english_text: Τὸ Κοινωνικόν· *Ἐξηγέρθη ὡς ὁ ὑπνῶν Κύριος, καὶ ἀνέστη σῴζων ἡμᾶς, Ἀλληλούϊα*. Ἀντὶ τοῦ *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* ψάλλεται τὸ παρὸν εἰς ἦχον β΄ εἱρμολογικῶς· *Μνήσθητι εὔσπλαγχνε καὶ ἡμῶν, καθὼς ἐμνημόνευσας τοῦ Λῃστοῦ ἐν τῇ Βασιλείᾳ τῶν Οὐρανῶν*, τὸ *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις μετὰ τοῦ *Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*, διότι προηγήθη ὁ Ἑσπερινὸς τῆς Μ. Κυριακῆς. (῎Ιδε Προθεωρίας § 16 καὶ ἔκθεσιν τῆς ἐπιτροπῆς).

units.slavonic_text: The Communion Hymn [Kinonikon] "The Lord awoke as if from sleep and rose, saving us. Alleluia." Instead of "We have seen the [True] Light," the following is then sung in Mode II Irmologic: "Remember us, O merciful One, as You did remember the thief in the Kingdom of Heaven." Then is sung "Blessed be the Name of the Lord," and the Dismissal: "[May Christ, our True God,] Who rose from the dead [have mercy upon us]" because the Vespers of Great Sunday has already been done. (See The Provisions [Protheoria], Paragraph 16, and the Statement of the Typikon Committee [found in the Preface of this Typikon].)

units.slavonic_text: Περὶ ὥραν ε΄ τῆς νυκτὸς (11 μ.μ.) εἰσερχόμεθα ἐν τῷ Ναῷ· ὁ Ἱερεὺς *Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*, ὁ Πατριάρχης *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι, Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*, τὸ Τρισάγιον, *Κύριε ἐλέησον ιβ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν γ΄* καὶ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, εἶτα ψάλλεται μετὰ Στίχου *Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι*, ὁ Κανὼν *Κύματι θαλάσσης* εἰς ϛ΄ καὶ μεθ’ ἑκάστην Ὠδὴν ὁ Εἱρμός, τὸ Κάθισμα οὐ ψάλλεται. Εἰς τὴν δ΄ Ὠδὴν ἐξέρχονται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ οἱ Διάκονοι ἐνδεδυμένοι, μετὰ δικηροτρικήρων, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης προσκυνήσας τὰς ἁγίας Εἰκόνας καὶ ἑτοιμασθείς, ὡς συνήθως, διὰ τὴν Λειτουργίαν, εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ Ἱερὸν Βῆμα καὶ ἐνδύεται ἅπασαν τὴν Ἀρχιερατικὴν στολήν, ὡς καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς. Μετὰ τὴν θ΄ Ὠδὴν τοῦ Κανόνος, λέγεται ἔνδον τοῦ Βήματος τὸ *Τρισάγιον*, τὸ Τροπάριον *Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*, ἡ Ἐκτενὴς καὶ Ἀπόλυσις. Τότε ὁ Πατριάρχης,¹ προπορευομένων τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, ἐξέρχεται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ Βήματος, ψάλλων ἀργῶς μετ’ αὐτῶν τὸ *Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*, ὅπερ ἐπαναλαμβάνεται καὶ ὑπὸ

Εἴθισται ἔν τισι μέρεσιν ἵνα κατὰ τὴν ὥραν ταύτην ὁ προεξάρχων Ἀρχιερεὺς ἱστάμενος πρὸ τῆς Ὡραίας Πύλης μετὰ δικηροτρικήρου ἀνημμένου ἐκ τῆς ἀκοιμήτου κανδήλας τῆς πρὸ τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης, προσκαλεῖ τὸν λαὸν ἵνα ἀνάψωσι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν, ψάλλων τὸ Δεῦτε λάβετε φῶς ἐκ τοῦ ἀνεσπέρου φωτός. units.slavonic_text: About the 5th hour of the night {11 PM} we enter the Church; the Priest: "Blessed is our God"; the Patriarch: "Glory to You our God, glory to You." "O heavenly King"; the Trisagion, "Lord, have mercy" (12 times), Glory, Now and ever, "O come let us worship" (3 times) and Psalm 50 is read. Then the Canon "With the wave of the sea" with the Verse "Glory to You our God, glory to You" in 6; and after each Ode, the Irmos; the Kathisma is not chanted. At the 4th Ode, the Deacons, vested, exit the Sanctuary with the Dikirotrikira. The Patriarch, having venerated the Holy Icons and having prepared as usual for the Liturgy, enters the Holy Sanctuary and vests with full Hierarchical Vesture, as do all the [participating] Hierarchs. After the 9th Ode of the Canon, the Trisagion is said from within the Sanctuary, then the Apolytikion "When You did descend unto death," the Ektenis and Dismissal. Then the Patriarch,¹ preceded by the Hierarchs, exits the Holy Sanctuary, chanting slowly with them "Your Resurrection, Christ Savior," which is repeated also by the Choirs until they [the procession of the clergy] reach the place [dais] from
units.english_text: Around the Fifth Hour of the night [11:00 p.m.], we enter into the church. The Priest: **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός*); the Patriarch: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*); the Reader: the Trisagion Prayers, **"Lord, have mercy"** [12 times], **"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God"** [three times], and Psalm 50 [LXX: "Have mercy on me, O God..."] is read plainly. Then the Canon in Tone 6: **"Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves..."** (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*) is chanted for six Troparia, with the refrain: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"**; and after each Ode, the Heirmos is chanted slowly as Katavasia; the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] is not chanted.

units.slavonic_text: --- 1. It is customary in some places, at this point, for the leading Hierarch to stand before the Beautiful Gate, holding the Dikirotrikiron lit from the sleepless lamp which rests upon the Holy Table. Singing the hymn Come, receive the light from the unwaning Light, he summons the people to light their candles. {Translator's Note: For an excellent study of various issues regarding the Services of Holy Week and Pascha, see Great Week and Pascha in the Greek Orthodox Church by Alkiviadis C. Calivas, especially pages 97 - 121.}
units.english_text: At the Fourth Ode, the deacons, vested in their sacred vestments, exit from the Sanctuary with the two-branched and three-branched candlesticks [dikirotrikira]. The Patriarch, having venerated the holy icons and having prepared himself according to custom for the Divine Liturgy, enters the Sanctuary and vests in all his hierarchical vestments, as do all the concelebrating Hierarchs.

units.english_text: After the Ninth Ode of the Canon, the Trisagion Prayers are recited from within the Sanctuary; then the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 2: **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Divinity..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*); the Augmented Litany and the Dismissal are given.

It is customary in some places, at this point, for the presiding Hierarch to stand before the Beautiful Gate, holding the two-branched and three-branched candlestick [dikirotrikiron] lit from the sleepless lamp which rests upon the Holy Table. units.english_text: τῶν Χορῶν ἕως οὗ φθάσωσιν εἰς προσδιωρισμένην ἐξέδραν· ὁ Ἀρχιδιάκονος τότε ἐκφωνεῖ *Καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς*, καὶ ὁ Πατριάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον *Ὀψὲ σαββάτων τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ*¹ (Αὐτὸ εἶναι τὸ ἴδιο Εὐαγγέλιον ὅπερ ἀναγινώσκεται εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν τῆς πρωΐας· ὅρα κάτωθεν σημ. 2.) καὶ οἱ Χοροὶ τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη [Δέσποτα]*, εἶτα λαβὼν τὸ θυμιατόν, θυμιᾷ τρὶς τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον καὶ ἐκφωνήσας *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ καὶ ἀδιαιρέτῳ Τριάδι*, ψάλλει τὸ Τροπάριον *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ νεκρῶν* τρίς, καὶ οἱ Χοροὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἑξάκις, τοῦ Πατριάρχου θυμιῶντος καὶ λέγοντος τοὺς τέσσαρας Στίχους *Ἀναστήτω ὁ Θεός*, καὶ μετ’ αὐτοὺς τὸ *Δόξα*, καὶ τὸ *Καὶ νῦν*· ἐπὶ τέλους ὁ Πατριάρχης ψάλλει τὸ αὐτὸ θυμιῶν τοὺς Ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ λαπούς, ὁ δὲ Ἀρχιδιάκονος λέγει τὴν Μ. Συναπτὴν *Ἐν εἰρήνῃ τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*, ὁ Πατριάρχης τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν *Ὅτι πρέπει σοι πᾶσα δόξα*, καὶ οὕτως εἰσερχόμεθα ἐν τῷ Ναῷ μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς παρατάξεως, τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἀρχομένου ψάλλειν τὸν Κανόνα *Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα λαμπρυνθῶμεν λαοί*, μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων Ἀρχιερέων, ἀνὰ ϛ΄ Τροπάρια ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ μετὰ Στίχου *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου Κύριε*· εἰς τὰ δύο δὲ τελευταῖα *Δόξα* καὶ τὸ *Καὶ νῦν*· μεθ’ ἑκάστην Ὠδὴν ἡ Καταβασία, ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ ἡ Ἐκφώνησις· εἰς μὲν τὴν α΄ Ὠδήν, *Ὅτι σὸν τὸ κράτος*, εἰς δὲ τὴν γ΄ *Ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*, εἰς τὴν δ΄ *Ὅτι ἀγαθὸς καὶ φιλάνθρωπος*, εἰς τὴν ε΄ *Ὅτι ἡγίασται καὶ δεδόξασται*, εἰς τὴν ϛ΄ *Σὺ γὰρ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεύς*, εἰς τὴν ζ΄ *Εἴη τὸ κράτος*, εἰς τὴν η΄ *Ὅτι ηὐλόγηται [Σου τὸ Ὄνομα] καὶ δεδόξασται*, εἰς τὴν θ΄ *Ὅτι σὲ αἰνοῦσι πᾶσαι αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν*· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ *Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον* χῦμα· ἀφ’ ϛ΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἡμέρας μετὰ τῶν Στίχων, εἶτα τὸ *Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ* τρίς, ἅπαξ ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατριάρχου καὶ δὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, μετὰ δὲ τὸ *Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς*, ψάλλεται ἡ ζ΄ καὶ ἡ η΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ μετ’ αὐτὴν ὁ Μ. Ἀρχιδιάκονος ἐκφωνεῖ *Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ φωτός*, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν ἑξῆς Μεγαλυναρίων·

This is the same Gospel that is read at Vespers in the morning; see note #2 below}, and the Choirs sing "Many years, [O Master]." Then, taking the censer, the Patriarch censes the Gospel 3 times and exclaims "Glory to the holy, and consubstantial, and life-creating, and indivisible Trinity," then he sings the Hymn "Christ is risen from the dead" (3 times), and the Choirs [repeat it] 6 times, the Patriarch censing and intoning the 4 verses of "Let God arise," and after these Verses the Glory and the Now and ever. At the conclusion, the Patriarch chants the same hymn ["Christ is risen"] censing the Hierarchs and the rest of the participants; then the Archdeacon says the Great Litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord," and the Patriarch sings the Exclamation "For unto You is due all glory." And thus we enter into the Church with this processional order. The Patriarch begins to sing the Canon "It is the day of Resurrection, let us be radiant, O you peoples" with the Holy Hierarchs, with six hymns in each Ode, each hymn preceeded with the Verse "Glory to Your Holy Resurrection, O Lord"; the last 2 hymns are, on the other hand, preceded by the Glory and the Now and ever respectively. After each Ode, we do the Katavasia, the Litany and the Exclamation — after the 1st Ode: "For Yours is the dominion"; after the 3rd Ode: "For You are our God"; after the 4th Ode: "For [You are] a good and man-loving"; after the 5th Ode: "For sanctified and glorified"; after the 6th Ode: "[For] You are the King [of Peace]"; after the 7th Ode: "May Your kingdon be"; after the 8th Ode: "For blessed is [Your name] and glorified"; after the 9th Ode: "For all the hosts of the Heavens praise You. After the 3rd Ode, we read the Ypakoi "Coming before the dawn"; after the 6th Ode, we recite the Kontakion, the Ikos and the Postscript of the day with its verses. Then is recited "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" (three times) — once by the Patriarch and twice by the Hierarchs. After "Jesus, having risen," the 7th and 8th Odes are sung, after which the Great Archdeacon exclaims "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light," and the 9th Ode is sung with the following Megalynaria:

units.english_text: After the 3rd Ode, we read the Ypakoe plainly: **"Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..."** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον*); after the 6th Ode, we recite the Kontakion, the Ikos, and the Memorial [*Hypomnema* / Synaxarion] of the day with its verses. Then is recited: **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the Holy Lord Jesus, the only sinless One..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) [three times] — once by the Patriarch and twice by the concelebrating Hierarchs. After **"Jesus having risen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given us eternal life and great mercy"** (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου*), the 7th and 8th Odes are sung, after which the Great Archdeacon exclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the 9th Ode is sung with the appointed Megalynaria...[^459]

units.slavonic_text: [Then we chant] the Katavasia "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for your Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem." The Petition, and the Exapostilarion "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal" (3 times). At the Praises: the 4 Resurrection Stichira "We praise, O Christ" and the Stichira "A sacred Pascha" with their verses. Then we chant Glory, Now and ever, "It is the day of Resurrection" ³ until "And thus let us cry," at which point the 2nd Choir sings the customary melody of "Christ is risen"; then the 1st Choir and again the 2nd Choir repeat the same hymn and the Liturgy begins.

units.english_text: At the Praises, we set eight stichoi and chant the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1: **"We hymn Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and glorify Thy Resurrection!"** (*Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστὲ τὸ σωτήριον Πάθος*)... and the four Stichera of Pascha in Tone 5 with their verses of Psalm 67 LXX: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*). Then we chant "Glory... Both now and ever...": Paschal Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another. Let us say, Brethren, even to those who hate us; let us forgive all things at the Resurrection, and thus let us cry:"** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*) ³ until the words **"and thus let us cry"**, at which point the Second Choir sings the customary melody of **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*); then the First Choir chants the same, and again the Second Choir repeats it, and the Divine Liturgy begins.[^460]

units.english_text: 2.    The Archdeacon exclaims: **"Bless, Master!"** (*Εὐλόγησον Δέσποτα*). The Priest intones: **"Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία*), and the choirs sing: **"Amen."** Directly from within the Sanctuary, the celebrant sings: **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) [three times]; then the choirs chant it six times with the Paschal Verses of Psalm 67 LXX, and the last repetition is intoned again from within the Sanctuary.

units.slavonic_text: [Original Greek Text: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (The Divine Liturgy Concluded) (§ 2 Concluded) and Paschal Vespers Opening (§ 3 Opening) (p. 790)]
units.english_text: Κύριον ἐκ πηγῶν Ἰσραήλ ⁴. *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*, τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ *Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον*, τὸ Κοντάκιον *Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*, τὸ *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε* ⁵, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ *Ἀλληλούϊα*, καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως *Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*, Κοινωνικὸν *Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε* Μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχὴν τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* τρὶς χῦμα ⁶, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ὁ Κατηχητικὸς λόγος τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου *Εἴ τις εὐσεβὴς καὶ φιλόθεος* ⁷, εἰς τὸ τέλος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου *Ἡ τοῦ στόματός σου καθάπερ*, εἶτα Εὐλογία Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἐκφωνοῦντος εἰς τὸ τέλος *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* τρίς, καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀποκρινομένου ὡσαύτως τρὶς *Ἀληθῶς ἀνέστη*, ὁ Πατριάρχης *Δόξα τῇ αὐτοῦ τριημέρῳ ἐγέρσει*, ὁ λαὸς *Προσκυνοῦμεν αὐτοῦ τὴν τριήμερον ἔγερσιν*· καὶ ἐπὶ τέλους ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* ὁλόκληρον. Μετὰ τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν, ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς οὕτως ἐνδεδυμένοι, προπορευομένων λαμπάδων καὶ Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, ἀνέρχονται εἰς τὸ Μέγα Συνοδικόν, ἔνθα ψάλλεται ὁ Πολυχρονισμὸς τοῦ Πατριάρχου κατὰ τὸ ἔθος ⁸.

Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον, τὸ Κοντάκιον Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ, τὸ Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε ⁵, ὁ Ἀπόστολος, τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα, καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε Μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχὴν τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρὶς χῦμα ⁶, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ὁ Κατηχητικὸς λόγος τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου Εἴ τις εὐσεβὴς καὶ φιλόθεος ⁷, εἰς τὸ τέλος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου Ἡ τοῦ στόματός σου καθάπερ, εἶτα Εὐλογία Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἐκφωνοῦντος εἰς τὸ τέλος Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρίς, καὶ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀποκρινομένου ὡσαύτως τρὶς Ἀληθῶς ἀνέστη, ὁ Πατριάρχης Δόξα τῇ αὐτοῦ τριημέρῳ ἐγέρσει, ὁ λαὸς Προσκυνοῦμεν αὐτοῦ τὴν τριήμερον ἔγερσιν· καὶ ἐπὶ τέλους ὁ Πατριάρχης τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ὁλόκληρον. Μετὰ τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν, ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς οὕτως ἐνδεδυμένοι, προπορευομένων λαμπάδων καὶ Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τῆς λοιπῆς παρατάξεως, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ἀνέρχονται εἰς τὸ Μέγα Συνοδικόν, ἔνθα ψάλλεται ὁ Πολυχρονισμὸς τοῦ Πατριάρχου κατὰ τὸ ἔθος ⁸.

Τὸ Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ψάλλεται [ἀντὶ τοῦ Τρισαγίου Ὕμνου] μέχρι τοῦ Σαββάτου τῆς Διακαινησίμου καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἀποδόσει. 6. Τὸ μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχὴν Χριστὸς ἀνέστη γ΄ λέγεται μέχρι τοῦ Σαββάτου τῆς Διακαινησίμου, ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Θωμᾶ τὸ Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα. 7. Ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐλέγετο κατὰ τὰ ἀρχαῖα Τυπικὰ μετὰ τοὺς Αἴνους πρὸ τῆς Λειτουργίας, διότι ἀφορᾷ εἰς τὴν προπαρασκευὴν διὰ τὴν Λειτουργίαν καὶ τὴν ἁγίαν Κοινωνίαν· ἤδη ὅμως καθιερώθη νὰ λέγηται μετὰ τὸ Κοινωνικόν. 8. Ἀπὸ τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης μέχρι τοῦ Σαββάτου τῆς Διακαινησίμου, ὡς καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς Ἀποδόσεως ἀντὶ Ὡρῶν, Ἀποδείπνου καὶ Μεσονυκτικοῦ, λέγεται ἡ ἑξῆς Ἀκολουθία· Μετὰ τὸ Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη γ΄, Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ γ΄, τὰ δὲ ἐφεξῆς ἅπαξ· Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον, Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ, Ἐν τάφῳ σωματικῶς, Δόξα, Ὡς ζωηφόρος, Καὶ νῦν, Τὸ τοῦ Ὑψίστου ἡγιασμένον, Κύριε ἐλέησον μ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, καὶ τὸ Δι' εὐχῶν· καὶ αὖθις τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ τρίτου κτλ. Τρισσεύεται δὲ ἡ τοιαύτη Ἀκολουθία ἀντὶ Ὡρῶν, Ἀποδείπνου καὶ Μεσονυκτικοῦ, ὡς προείπομεν.

units.english_text: ...is of Israel's fountain." ⁴ **"Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). [After the Entrance:] **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**, the Ypakoe: **"Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..."** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον*), and the Kontakion: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One, yet didst Thou destroy the power of Hades..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*). units.english_text: At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!"** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ μεταλάβετε*).

The "As many as have been baptized in Christ" [instead of the Trisagios Hymn], ⁵ the Apostolos, the Alleluia, and the Gospel. At "Especially," "The Angel cried out . . . Shine, shine," Communion Hymn "Receive the body of Christ." After the Prayer behind the Amvon, "Christ is risen" (three times intoned), ⁶ and the Catechetical Sermon of Chrysostom "If any be pious" ⁷ is read by the Patriarch. At the end is chanted the Apolytikion of Chrysostom "Grace shining forth from your mouth," then "The blessing of the Lord," and Dismissal by the Patriarch who exclaims at the end "Christ is risen" (3 times), the people responding three times "Truly He is risen!" The Patriarch exclaims "Glory to His holy third-day Resurrection"; the people respond with "We adore His third-day Resurrection"; at the end the Patriarch sings the entire "Christ is risen." After the Dismissal, the Patriarch and the other Hierarchs, thus vested, ascend to the Great Synodikon [Meeting Room of the Holy Synod, preceded by candles, the Exapteryga [Six-winged Fans], and the remaining members of the procession, while the chanters sing "Christ is risen." There, according to tradition, the Polychronismos [Acclamation] of the Patriarch is chanted. ⁸

units.slavonic_text: _____________________________ 4. The Entrance hymn "In the Churches" is sung every day until the Leave-taking of Pascha. 5. "As many as have been baptized" is sung [in place of the Trisagios Hymn] until Saturday of Renewal Week and on the Leave-taking. 6. The singing of "Christ is risen" 3 times, after the Prayer behind the Amvon, is done during Renewal Week; but from the Sunday of Thomas on we sing "Blessed be the name." 7. According to the ancient Typika, this sermon was read after the Praises before the Liturgy, since it concerns the preparation for the Liturgy and for Holy Communion; now, however, it has been established to be read after the Communion Hymn. 8. From this day until the Saturday of Renewal Week, as well as on the day of the Leave-taking, instead of the Hours, Compline and Midnight Office, the following Service is performed: After "Blessed is our God," we chant "Christ is risen" (3 times), then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" (3 times), and the following hymns once each: "Coming before the dawn," "Though You descended into the grave," "In the grave with the body," Glory, "As life-bearing," Now and ever, "That which is sanctified by the One on High"; then "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), Glory, Now and ever, "More honorable," and "Through the prayers," and once again "Christ is risen" (3 times) etc. This service is performed three times in place of the Hours, Compline and Midnight Service, as we have said before.

units.english_text: Διακόνων προενδεδυμένων τὰς οἰκείας στολάς· ἄρχονται δὲ οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλειν καθ' ὃν καιρὸν ἐνδύεται ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων τὸ *Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα* ἀργόν, ἀκολούθως, προπορευομένων τῶν Λαμπαδούχων, τῶν Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ τοῦ Πριμικηρίου, καὶ τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, ἕπονται οἱ Ἱερεῖς, οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς, οἱ Διάκονοι μετὰ Δικηροτρικήρων καὶ μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης φέρων τὴν ῥάβδον καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν Εὐαγγέλιον (καὶ περιστοιχίζομενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Μ. Λογοθέτου, τῶν Πρέσβεων τῶν Ὀρθοδόξων Κρατῶν καὶ τῶν Λογάδων τοῦ Γένους).* Ἐν τοιαύτῃ παρατάξει κατέρχονται εἰς τὸν Ναόν, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, τῶν Ἱερέων καὶ Διακόνων εἰσέρχεται κατ' εὐθεῖαν εἰς τὸ Ἱερόν, καὶ λαβὼν θυμιατὸν θυμιᾷ πρὸ τῆς ἁγίας Τραπέζης, εἶτα ἐκφωνεῖ *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ Ὁμοουσίῳ*, καὶ ψάλλει τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*, κατὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ ἐν § 1 διάταξιν· ἀκολούθως ὁ Ἀρχιδιάκονος λέγει τὴν Μ. Συναπτήν, ὁ Πατριάρχης τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν *Ὅτι πρέπει σοι*. Εἰς τὸ *Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ *Τὸν πρὸ αἰώνων ἐκ Πατρὸς* κατὰ σειρὰν ϛ΄· τούτων ψαλλομένων, ὁ Πατριάρχης προπορευομένου τοῦ Πριμικηρίου μετὰ τοῦ Διβαμβούλου, θυμιᾷ τὰς εἰκόνας καὶ ἅπαντα τὸν λαὸν καὶ ἐπανερχόμενος ἵσταται εἰς τὸν Θρόνον· ὁ α΄ Χορὸς *Δόξα, Τὸν σωτήριον ὕμνον, Καὶ νῦν*, ὁ β΄ τὸ *Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ νόμου*. Εἴσοδος μετὰ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, τὸ *Φῶς ἱλαρὸν* ἀργῶς ὁλόκληρον ἔξω, εἶτα εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ψάλλων τὸ Μ. Προκείμενον *Τίς Θεὸς Μέγας*, ὅπερ οἱ Χοροὶ ἐπαναλαμβάνουσι μετὰ τῶν Στίχων καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Πατριάρχης *Καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ καταξιωθῆναι ἡμᾶς*, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον *Οὔσης ὀψίας* μέχρι τοῦ *Οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω*, κατὰ περιόδους ἐπαναλαμβανομένας καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἀρχιερέων, τῶν Ἱερέων καὶ τῶν Διακόνων. Μετὰ τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*, ἡ Ἐκτενής, τὸ *Καταξίωσον Κύριε*, *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν*, ἡ ἐκφώνησις *Εἴη τὸ κράτος*, καὶ ψάλλεται ὑπὸ τοῦ α΄ Χοροῦ τὸ Ἀπόστιχον Στιχηρὸν *Ἡ Ἀνάστασίς σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*, καὶ ἀκολούθως τὰ Στιχηρὰ *Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*, καὶ τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* γ΄· τούτου ψαλλομένου, ὁ Πατριάρχης καὶ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς ἐξέρχονται τοῦ Ἱεροῦ καὶ ἀνέρχονται αὖθις εἰς τὸ Μ. Συνοδικὸν μετὰ τῆς αὐτῆς παρατάξεως καὶ ἐκεῖ ποιεῖ τὴν Ἀπόλυσιν, τῶν Χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸν Πολυχρονισμὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὕτω λαμβάνει πέρας ὁ Ἑσπερινός.

units.slavonic_incipit: vestments. The Choirs begin to chant
units.slavonic_text: vestments. The Choirs begin to chant "It is the day of Resurrection" (slowly) while the Patriarch and the Hierarchs vest. Then, preceded by Candles, Exapteryga [Six-winged Fans], the Primikirios [Director of Cer- emonies] and the Choirs, singing "Christ is risen," follow the Priests, the Hierarchs, the Deacons with the Hierarchical Candles and finally the Patriarch carrying the Staff and the Holy Gospel (and surrounded by the Great Logothetis [ ], the ambassadors of the Orthodox Countries and the Logades [appointed representatives] of the Nation.)* In such processional order they come down to the Church; the Patriarch, together with the Hierarchs, the Priests and the Deacons, enters directly into the Sanctuary. And receiving the censer, he censes three times before the Holy Altar Table; then he proclaims "Glory to the holy and consubstantial," and sings "Christ is risen," according to the order of Matins in Paragraph 1 above. Following this, the Archdeacon says the Great Litany and the Patriarch the Exclamation "For to You belongs." At "Lord, I have cried" the 6 Resurrection Stichira are chanted in sequence, beginning with "Come, let us worship God." While these are being chanted, the Patriarch preceded by the Primikirios with the Divamvulon [two-wicked candle], censes the Icons and all the people and returning stands on the Throne. The First Choir chants Glory, "The saving hymn," Now and ever, the Second [Choir] "The shadow of the law has passed away." Entrance is made with the Gospel, the "O Gladsome Light" is chanted slowly in its entirety outside [the Sanctuary]. Then the Patriarch enters the Sanctuary singing the Great Prokimenon "What God is as great"; this is repeated by the Choirs with its verses and then the Patriarch says "That we may be found worthy," and the Gospel "When it was evening" up to "I will not believe," is read in segments and in sequence by the Hierarchs, Priests and Deacons. After "Many years," the Ektenis, the "Vouchsafe, O Lord," then "Let us complete our evening prayer." After the Exclamation "May the might," the First Choir chants the Resurrection Apostichon "Your Resurrection, Christ Savior," then follow the Stichira of Pascha "A sacred Pascha," Glory, Now and ever, "It is the day of Resurrection, and the Christ is risen" (three times); while this is chanted, the Patriarch and the Hierarchs exit the Sanctuary and ascend to the Great Synodikon [Meeting room of the Holy Synod] with this processional entourage and there the Patriarch does the Dismissal while the Choirs sing his Polychronismos [Acclamation] and the Vespers is concluded in this manner.
units.english_text: Following this, the Archdeacon recites the Great Litany, and the Patriarch intones the Exclamation: **"For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship..."** (*Ὅτι πρέπει σοι*).

Both now and ever...": **"It is the day of Resurrection..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), and **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times).

units.english_text: 4.    Εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὴν ἀντὶ Μεσονυκτικοῦ ὡρισμένην Ἀκολουθίαν (βλ. § 2, σημ. 8), ὁ Ἱερεὺς ἐνδυθεὶς πᾶσαν τὴν ἱερατικὴν στολὴν ἵσταται μετὰ θυμιατοῦ ἐνώπιον τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης καὶ θυμιῶν ἐκφωνεῖ *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ*· ἀκολούθως ψάλλει τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* ἐκ γ΄ ὡς διετυπώθη χθὲς ἐν § 1, εἶτα Συναπτή, ἡ Ἐκφώνησις *Ὅτι πρέπει σοι πᾶσα δόξα* καὶ ψάλλεται ὁ τῆς Ἀναστάσεως Κανὼν ὡς χθὲς ἀπαραλλάκτως· ἀλλ' ἀφ' ϛ΄ μόνον τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ *Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ*· μετὰ τὴν η΄ Ὠδήν, ὁ Διάκονος λέγει *Τὴν Θεοτόκον* καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον *Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας* (δὶς, κατὰ τὸ ἀρχαῖον Τυπικόν). Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ δ΄ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ *Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ πᾶσα κτίσις*, καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ *Πάσχα ἱερὸν* μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτῶν, *Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*, τὸ *Χριστὸς ἀνέστη* ἐκ γ΄ καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ Λειτουργία.

units.english_text: 4.    At Matins, following the prescribed service which replaces the Midnight Office (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest, vested in all his priestly vestments, stands with the censer before the Holy Table and censing exclaims: **"Glory to the holy, and consubstantial, and life-creating, and undivided Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ*); then he sings **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times) as prescribed yesterday in Paragraph 1. Then follow the Litany and the Exclamation: **"For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship..."** (*Ὅτι πρέπει σοι πᾶσα δόξα*). Then the Paschal Canon of the Resurrection is chanted exactly as yesterday; except that, after the 6th Ode, only the Kontakion is said, and immediately after we recite **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) [once]; after the 8th Ode, the Deacon chants **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον*), and the 9th Ode is sung with the Megalynaria. The Exaposteilarion: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητὸς*) is chanted twice, according to the ancient Typikon. At the Praises: the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2: **"Let every breath and all creation glorify Thee, O Lord..."** (*Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ πᾶσα κτίσις*) and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses. "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"It is the day of Resurrection..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins.

units.slavonic_text: MONDAY OF RENEWAL WEEK
units.english_text: 5.    At the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons etc. are celebrated as yesterday. After **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*) [chanted in place of the Trisagion Hymn], the Epistle and Gospel of the day are proclaimed. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**. After the Prayer behind the Ambo, we intone **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** three times plainly, and the Dismissal is pronounced.

units.slavonic_text: 4.    In Matins, following the prescribed Service which replaces the Midnight Service (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest vested with all his priestly vestments stands with the censer before the Holy Altar Table and censing exclaims "Glory to the holy and consubstantial"; then he sings "Christ is risen" (three times) as prescribed yesterday in Paragraph 1. Then follow the Litany and the Exclamation "For to You belong all glory." Then the Resurrection Canon is chanted exactly as yesterday; except that, after the 6th Ode, only the Kontakion is said, and immediately after we recite "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; after the 8th Ode, the Deacon chants "The Theotokos," and the 9th Ode is sung with the Megalynaria. The Exapostilarion "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal" is chanted (twice, according to the ancient Typikon). At the Praises: the 4 Resurrection Stichira "Every breath and all creation" and the Stichira of Easter "A sacred Pascha" with their verses. Glory, Now and ever, "It is the day of Resurrection," "Christ is risen" (three times) and the Liturgy begins.
units.english_text: This order of service is to be strictly observed throughout the entirety of Bright Week at Vespers, Matins, and the Divine Liturgy, excepting only the Gospel reading proclaimed at the Vespers on the Great Sunday [Pascha].

units.slavonic_text: FRIDAY OF RENEWAL WEEK The Service of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos of the Life-containing Fountain is chanted
units.english_text: 6.    On Thursday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant six Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3: **"Holding the victory over Hades, O Christ, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross..."** (*Νίκην ἔχων Χριστέ*) and four of the Life-Giving Fountain, repeating the first: **"Who can declare thy mighty wonders, O Fountain?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Πηγή*). "Glory...": **"Who can tell of thy mighty acts, O undefiled Fountain?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Πηγή*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 3: **"Who would not admire, who would not praise thy childbirth without seed, O all-pure Virgin?..."** (*Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε*). The Entrance is made with the censer; **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*) and the Prokimenon: **"I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation, my refuge, and my deliverer!"** (*Ἀγαπήσω σε, Κύριε, ἡ ἰσχύς μου*, Ps. 17:2–3 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha, which are begun by the Second Choir: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior..."** (*Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*)...[^464]

units.english_text: ...Choir: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the angels hymn in heaven: and make us worthy here on earth to glorify Thee with a pure heart!"** (*Τὴν Ἀνάστασίν σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*), and the three Prosomia of the Theotokos; "Glory...": **"Let us sound the trumpet of hymns, O ye lovers of the feast, let us leap for joy in songs, and let us dance exultantly in the ever-flowing Fountain of the Queen of all!..."** (*Σαλπίσωμεν φιλέορτοι ἐν ὕμνοις*); "Both now and ever...": **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) (three times), and Dismissal.*

units.slavonic_text: Choir: Your Resurrection, Christ Savior," and the three Prosomia of the Theotokos, Glory, "O You feast-lovers, let us sound the trumpet of hymns," Now and ever, "It is the day of Resurrection," "Christ is risen" (3 times) * and Dismissal. * {Translator's Note: A later practice, as outlined in the Imerologia of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of North and South America [IGOANSA]: 1985, p. 85; 1990, p. 105; and 1992, p. 109 as well as in the Imerologia of the Ecumenical Patriarchate [IEP]: 1996, p. 1196; 1999, p. 298 indicates this order: "Christ is risen," "Your temple, O Theotokos" and again "Christ is risen"}. 7.    On Friday at Matins, we sing the Canon of Easter and of the Theotokos (4 hymns); the verse for the Canon of the Theotokos is "All-holy Theotokos"; at the end of each Ode, the Katavasia, and the "Christ is risen" (three times) etc. as in Paragraph 4. After the 3rd Ode, we read the Kontakion of Easter, and we chant the Kathisma "The ever-flowing and life-emanating fountain" (once); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Theotokos, the Synaxarion of the Mineon, and the Postscript of the Life-containing Spring with its verses. Then "Having beheld the resurrec- tion" (3 times) etc. and then follows the 7th and 8th Odes of the Canons; then the 9th Ode with the Megalynaria; at the Canon of the Theotokos "Most holy Theotokos." The Exapostilarion of Easter and that of the Theotokos. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 Stichira of the Theotokos and "A sacred Pascha." **
units.english_text: 7.    On Friday at Matins, we chant the Canon of Pascha and the Canon of the Theotokos, with four Troparia for each ode; the verse for the Canon of the Theotokos is **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us!"** (*Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε, σῶσον ἡμᾶς*); at the conclusion of each Ode, the Katavasia, and **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times) etc. as in Paragraph 4. After the 3rd Ode, we recite the Kontakion of Pascha plainly, and we chant the Kathisma: **"The ever-flowing and living fountain..."** (*Τὴν ἀέναον κρήνην καὶ ζωηρὰν*) (once); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Theotokos, the Synaxarion of the Menaion, and the Hypomnema of the Life-Giving Fountain with its verses. Then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) (three times) etc., and then follow the 7th and 8th Odes of the Canons; then the 9th Ode with the Megalynaria; at the Canon of the Theotokos the verse: **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us!"**. The Exaposteilarion of Pascha and that of the Theotokos. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera, three Stichera of the Theotokos, and the first Paschal Sticheron: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*).**

units.english_text: 8.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance: **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**, the Ypakoe **"Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..."** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν ὄρθρον*), the Troparion of the Theotokos: **"From Thy never-failing spring, O woman full of the grace of God, Thou dost bestow upon me the streams of grace..."** (*Ἐξ ἀκενώτου σου πηγῆς θεοχαρίτωτε*), and the Kontakion: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*).***

units.english_text: **"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*) [in place of the Trisagion Hymn], the Epistle and Gospel of the day. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!"** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). At the Diptychs we chant the Megalynarion: **"The life-**[^465]

units.english_text: 9.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, λέγεται ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα (ὡς προεσημειώθη ἐν § 2, σημ. 8). Μετὰ δὲ τὸ Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός, ψάλλεται τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἅπαξ ἐκ τοῦ Βήματος καὶ ἐκ τῶν Χορῶν ἀνὰ μίαν φορὰν καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Προοιμιακὸς καὶ τὸ α΄ Κάθισμα τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ ς΄ Ἰδιόμελα κατὰ σειράν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, τὸ Προκείμενον Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Φιλάνθρωπε μέγα καὶ ἀνείκαστον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος ἐκ γ΄ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_text: Τῌ ΚΥΡΙΑΚῌ ΤΟΥ ΑΝΤΙΠΑΣΧΑ
units.english_text: 10.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ψάλλεται ὁ Τριαδικὸς Κανὼν τοῦ α΄ ἤχου, εἶτα ἡ Λιτὴ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ γ΄ Καθίσματα ἐκ β΄ (Εὐλογητάρια οὐ λέγονται σήμερον χάριν τῆς Δεσποτικῆς ἑορτῆς, ὡς σημειοῦσι καὶ τὰ ἀρχαῖα Τυπικὰ) καὶ εὐθὺς οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον⁹ καὶ ὁ Κανὼν εἰς ς΄ ἄνευ Στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Ὡς ἐν μέσῳ τῶν Μαθητῶν σου, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἑορτῆς, αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ τοῦ Κανόνος, ἡ Καταβασία Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, τὸ Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν δίς, καὶ ὁ Στίχος Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν¹⁰ καὶ τὰ Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ α΄ δὶς καὶ τὸ ἕτερον ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ γ΄ Καθίσματα ἐκ β΄ (Εὐλογητάρια οὐ λέγονται σήμερον χάριν τῆς Δεσποτικῆς ἑορτῆς, ὡς σημειοῦσι καὶ τὰ ἀρχαῖα Τυπικὰ) καὶ εὐθὺς οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον⁹ καὶ ὁ Κανὼν εἰς ς΄ ἄνευ Στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Ὡς ἐν μέσῳ τῶν Μαθητῶν σου, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἑορτῆς, αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ τοῦ Κανόνος, ἡ Καταβασία Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, τὸ Ἅγιος Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν δίς, καὶ ὁ Στίχος Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν¹⁰ καὶ τὰ Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ α΄ δὶς καὶ τὸ ἕτερον ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

units.english_text: 9.    On Saturday evening, the Ninth Hour of Pascha is recited (as noted in Paragraph 2, Note 8). After **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** is sung once from the Sanctuary and once by each of the choirs, and immediately we recite the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the First Stasis of the First Kathisma of the Psalter (Pss. 1–3 LXX). At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the six Idiomela of the Feast in order; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"When the doors were closed, the disciples being assembled, Jesus entered..."** (*Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων*); and the Saturday Evening Great Prokimenon: **"The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty!"** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν*, Ps. 92:1 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"O Lover of mankind, great and unsearchable is the multitude of Thy compassions!..."** (*Φιλάνθρωπε μέγα καὶ ἀνείκαστον*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 7: **"While the tomb was sealed, Thou, O Life, didst shine forth from the grave, O Christ God..."** (*Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος*) three times, and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 10.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, we chant the Triadic Canon in Tone 1, then the Liti of the Feast, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right to glorify Thee, God the Word..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion three times; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos (Pss. 134–135 LXX). The three Kathismata twice each (Resurrectional Evlogitaria are not chanted today since it is a Master Feast of the Lord, as the ancient Typika note) and immediately the Anavathmoi of Tone 4 (First Antiphon: **"From my youth..."**) and the Prokimenon in Tone 4: **"Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem"** (*Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 147:1 LXX) [Note 9] and the Canon of the Feast with six Troparia without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoe in Tone 6: **"As Thou didst stand in the midst of Thy disciples, O Savior, giving them peace: come also unto us and save us!"** (*Ὡς ἐν μέσῳ τῶν Μαθητῶν σου*); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"With his inquisitive right hand, Thomas explored Thy life-giving side, O Christ God..."** (*Τῇ φιλοπράγμονι δεξιᾷ*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias of Pascha (**"It is the day of Resurrection..."**) and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (First Eothinon: Matthew 28:16–20); then the 9th Ode of the Canon is sung, the Katavasia: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Then **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (twice), and the Verse: **"Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy!"** (*Ὑψοῦτε Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν*, Ps. 98:5 LXX) [Note 10] and the Exaposteilaria: **"With my hand have I explored Thy side, O Compassionate One..."** (*Ἐμῇ χειρὶ ἠρεύνησα*) — the first one twice and the second one once. At the Praises: the three Prosomia to 4, "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"Eight days after Thy Resurrection, O Jesus our King..."** (*Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ*). Great Doxology and the Dismissal Troparion.

units.slavonic_text: 9.    On Saturday evening, the 9th Hour of Easter is said (as noted in Paragraph 2, note 8). After "Blessed is our God," "Christ is risen" is sung once from the Vima [Sanctuary] and once by each of the Choirs, and immediately we recite the Introductory Psalm and the First Stasis of the Kathisma of the Psalter. At "Lord, I have cried" we sing the six Idiomela in order, Glory, Now and ever, "The doors being closed," and the Prokimenon "The Lord has reigned as King." At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela, Glory, Now and ever, "O friend of man, great and unsearchable." The Apolytikion "The tomb being sealed" three times, and Dismissal. 10.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, we sing the Triadic Canon of Mode I, then the Liti of the Feast, and the Triadic "It is meet," then the Trisagion, the Apolytikion and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikion three times; then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The three Kathismata twice each (Evlogitaria are not chanted today since it is a Lord's Feast, as the ancient Typika note) and immediately the Anavathmi of Mode IV and the Prokimenon "Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem" 9 and the Canon with six hymns without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoi "As in the midst of Your disciples"; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion, the Ikos, the Minologion of the day and the Postscript of the Feast. The Katavasie of Pascha and the entire order of the Morning Gospel; then the 9th Ode of the Canon is sung, the Katavasia "The angel cried out... Shine, shine." Then "Holy is the Lord our God" (twice), and the Verse "Exalt the Lord our God" 10 and the Exapostilaria — the first one twice and the second one once. At the Praises: the three Prosomia in 4, Glory, Now and ever, "Eight days after." Great Doxology and the Apolytikion.
units.english_text: *Note 9:* [On the Sunday of Antipascha] the Gospel of Matins is read after the Katavasias, as on all other Sundays of the year, [and not after the Prokimenon].

units.english_text: ...the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (*Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος*), and the Kontakion: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*). The Trisagion Hymn, the Epistle (Acts 5:12–20) and Gospel (John 20:19–31) of the Feast. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos of the Feast: **"O Thou radiant lamp and Mother of God, unsetting torch of the divine Glory, thee do we magnify in hymns!"** (*Σὲ τὴν φαεινὴν λαμπάδα*). Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem"** (*Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 147:1 LXX), and then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**. After the Prayer behind the Ambo, **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 12.    On Sunday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the three Stichera of the Praises: **"After Thine awesome Resurrection from the tomb..."** (*Μετὰ τὴν ἐκ τάφου σου φρικτήν*) and the three Stichera of the Saint of the day from the Menaion; "Glory... Both now and ever..." in Tone 1: **"When the doors were closed..."** (*Τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων*). Entrance with the censer, **"O Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*), and the Great Prokimenon: **"What God is as great as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders!"** (*Τίς Θεὸς Μέγας ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν; Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια*, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Sticheron: **"Our evening prayers receive, O holy Lord..."** (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς*) and the two Penitential Stichera; "Glory... Both now and ever..." in Tone 1: **"Eight days after Thy Resurrection, O Jesus our King..."** (*Μεθ᾿ ἡμέρας ὀκτώ*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (once), and Dismissal.

On Sunday evening, at "Lord, I have cried" we chant the three Stichira of the Praises "After Your awesome Resurrection from the grave" and the three Stichira of the Saint of the day, Glory, Now and ever "The doors being closed" in Mode I. Entrance, "O Gladsome Light" and the Prokimenon "What God is as great" with its verses. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichiron "Accept our evening prayers" and the two Peniten- tial Stichira, Glory, Now and ever, "Eight days after" in Mode I. The Apolytikion "The tomb being sealed" (once) and Dismissal. On Monday morning, the Service is chanted as prescribed in the Pentikostarion.

units.slavonic_text: 16.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ζ΄ καὶ γ΄ τῶν Μυροφόρων, Δόξα, Αἱ Μυροφόροι Γυναῖκες, Καὶ νῦν, Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ νόμου. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Ἡ Ἀνάστασίς σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ, καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Σὲ τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον τὸ φῶς, τὰ γ΄ τῶν Μυροφόρων Ἀπολυτίκια καὶ Ἀπόλυσις. 17.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς Κανών, ἡ Λιτὴ τῶν Μυροφόρων καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον, ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων ¹¹. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, τὰ β΄ Καθίσματα, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῶν Μυροφόρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Μυροφόρων, αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τῶν Μυροφόρων. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, Ἀναστάσιμα τῆς Ὀκτωήχου δ΄ καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, τὸ Ἑωθινὸν Μετὰ μύρων προσελθούσαις, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία
units.english_text: *Σημείωσις 11:* Ὁ Κανὼν τῶν Μυροφόρων, ὡς ἀναγινωσκόμενος ἐν ταῖς ἄλλαις ἡμέραις τῆς ἑβδομάδος, καταλιμπάνεται συνήθως σήμερον· τὸ αὐτὸ συμβαίνει καὶ διὰ τὰς ἀκολούθους Κυριακάς, τοῦ Παραλύτου, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος καὶ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ.

units.english_text: 15.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"While the tomb was sealed..."** (*Ἐσφραγισμένου τοῦ μνήματος*) and the Kontakion: **"With his inquisitive right hand, Thomas explored Thy life-giving side, O Christ God..."** (*Τῇ φιλοπράγμονι δεξιᾷ*); the Epistle (Acts 5:21–33) and Gospel (John 3:22–33) of the day. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos of the Feast: **"O Thou radiant lamp and Mother of God, unsetting torch of the divine Glory, thee do we magnify in hymns!"** (*Σὲ τὴν φαεινὴν λαμπάδα*). Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem"** (*Ἐπαίνει Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 147:1 LXX), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."**, **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"**, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: the Oktoichos "We praise Your saving Passion" and three of the Feast "After Your awesome Resurrection from the grave," Glory, Now and ever, "Eight days after." Great Doxology and the Apolytikion of the Feast. 15.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Easter. After the Entrance [the Apolytikion] "The tomb being sealed" and the Kontakion "With his searching right hand"; the Epistle and Gospel of the day. At "Especially," "You, the shining lamp," Communion Hymn "Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem," "Christ is risen," "Blessed be the name of the Lord" and Dismissal.
units.english_text: 16.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant seven Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2 and three of the Myrrh-bearers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"The Myrrh-bearing Women, reaching Thy tomb at deep dawn, sought Thee to anoint Thine immaculate Body with myrrh!..."** (*Αἱ Μυροφόροι Γυναῖκες*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 2: **"The shadow of the law passed away when grace arrived..."** (*Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιὰ τοῦ νόμου*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 2: **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened the whole universe..."** (*Ἡ Ἀνάστασίς σου Χριστὲ Σωτήρ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Paschal Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, Joseph taking Thee down from the Tree with Nicodemus wept and lamented..."** (*Σὲ τὸν ἀναβαλλόμενον τὸ φῶς*). The three Dismissal Troparia of the Myrrh-bearers: 1. Tone 2: **"The noble Joseph, taking down Thine immaculate Body from the Tree..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσήφ*), 2. "Glory...": **"When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Godhead..."** (*Ὅτε κατῆλθες πρὸς τὸν θάνατον*), 3. "Both now and ever...": **"Unto the myrrh-bearing women, the Angel standing by the tomb cried aloud: Myrrh is fitting for the dead, but Christ is shown to be a stranger to corruption!..."** (*Ταῖς μυροφόροις γυναιξί*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: THE THIRD SUNDAY AFTER PASCHA
units.english_text: 17.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 2, the Liti of the Myrrh-bearers, and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, **"The noble Joseph..."** (*Ὁ εὐσχήμων Ἰωσήφ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 2, the Anavathmoi of Tone 2, and the Prokimenon in Tone 2: **"Arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which Thou hast commanded..."** (Ps. 7:7 LXX). The Canon of Pascha with the two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus [Note 11]. After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 2: **"Thou didst command the myrrh-bearing women to rejoice, O Christ God..."** and the Ikos of the Myrrh-bearers, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers. The Katavasias of Pascha and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Second Eothinon: Mark 16:1–8); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia. The Exaposteilarion of Pascha: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητὸς*) and that of the Myrrh-bearers: **"Listen, ye women, to the voice of joy: having trampled down tyrannical Hades..."** (*Γυναῖκες ἀκουτίσθητε*). At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2, and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": the Second Eothinon Doxastikon in Tone 2: **"Coming with myrrhs, Mary's companions were perplexed..."** (*Μετὰ μύρων προσελθούσαις*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). units.slavonic_text: 16.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we sing 7 Stichira of the Resurrection and 3 of the Myrrhbearers, Glory, "The myrrhbearing women," Now and ever "The shadow of the Law has passed away." At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichiron "Your Resurrection, O Christ Savior," then the Stichira of Pascha "A sacred Pascha," Glory, Now and ever "You Who puts on light." The three Apolytikia of the Myrrhbearers, and Dismissal. 17.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, the Liti of the Myrrhbearers and the "It is meet"; then the Trisagion, "The noble Joseph," and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos. The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi, the Anavathmi of the Mode and the Prokimenon. The Canon of Easter with the two Theotokia. 11 After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Myrrhbearers, the Minologion and the Postscript of the Sunday of the Myrrhbearers. The Katavasie of Pascha and the entire order of the Morning Gospel; then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia. The Exapostilaria of Pascha and those of the Myrrhbearers. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and the Stichira "A sacred Pascha," Glory the Eothinon "Having come with myrrhs," Now and ever, "It is the day of Resurrection." Great Doxology and "Today salvation."
units.english_text: *Note 11:* The Canon of the Myrrh-bearers, since it is read on the other days of the week, is usually omitted today. The same occurs also on the following Sundays: of the Paralytic, of the Samaritan Woman, and of the Blind Man.

Τῇ Παρασκευῇ τῆς αὐτῆς ἑβδομάδος ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ γ΄ τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Μυροφόρων πρῶτα Στιχηρὰ καὶ γ΄ ἐκ τοῦ Μηναίου, Δόξα, Αἱ Μυροφόροι γυναῖκες, Καὶ νῦν, Παρῆλθεν ἡ σκιά. units.english_text: 18.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the three Dismissal Troparia of the Myrrh-bearers in sequence, that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion of Pascha: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*); the Epistle (Acts 6:1–7) and Gospel (Mark 15:43–16:8) of the Sunday. At "Especially", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee!
