units.english_text: 20.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant seven Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3, and three of the Paralytic, repeating the first; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"Jesus went up to Jerusalem to the Sheep's Pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches..."** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 3: **"How can we not marvel at thy childbirth, wherein God and man are united, O all-honored Lady?..."** (*Πῶς μὴ θαυμάσωμεν*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 3: **"Thou Who by Thy Passion, O Christ, didst darken the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection didst enlighten all things: accept our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind!"** (*Ὁ τῷ πάθει σου Χριστέ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"In Solomon's porch lay a multitude of the sick, and at Mid-feast Christ found the Paralytic who had been lying there thirty and eight years..."** (*Ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦ Σολομῶντος*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3: **"Let the heavens rejoice, let earthly things be glad; for the Lord hath wrought might with His arm!..."** (*Εὐφραινέσθω τὰ Οὐράνια*); the Theotokion in Tone 3: **"Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin, and didst endure the Cross, O Good One, and didst despoil death by death, and as God didst reveal the Resurrection: overlook not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine own hand!..."** (*Σὲ τὴν μεσιτεύσασαν*), and Dismissal.

On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 3; at the Liti, "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"At the Sheep's Pool a man lay sick for thirty and eight years..."** (*Ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρᾳ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"A temple and gate art thou, a palace and throne of the King, O all-honored Virgin..."** (*Ναὸς καὶ πύλη*); and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3 (twice) and the Theotokion (once), the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 3, the Anavathmoi of Tone 3, and the Prokimenon in Tone 3: **"Chant unto our God, chant! Chant unto our King, chant!"** (*Ψάλατε τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν, ψάλατε*, Ps. 46:7 LXX). The Canon of Pascha with its two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma in Tone 3: **"A word alone paralyzed the limbs of the sick man..."** (*Ῥῆμα Παράλυτον*); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Kathisma in Tone 4: **"Awed by the beauty of thy virginity and the exceeding brilliance of thy purity, Gabriel cried aloud unto thee, O Theotokos: What praise worthy of thee shall I offer?..."** (*Τὴν ὡραιότητα*). After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 3: **"As of old Thou didst raise up the Paralytic, O Lord, by Thy divine presence: so raise up my soul, paralyzed by grievous sins and shameful deeds!..."** and the Ikos of the Paralytic, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Paralytic. units.slavonic_text: 23.    Τῇ Τρίτῃ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ὁ Προοιμιακός, εἰς δὲ τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα τὰ γ΄ Προσόμοια Πάρεστιν ἡ μεσότης ἡμερῶν εἰς ς΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης. Εἴσοδος, τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὰ Ἀναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα Πεντηκοστῆς ἐφέστηκεν, Στίχοι Μνήσθητι τῆς συναγωγῆς σου ἧς ἐκτήσω ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς, καὶ Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων εἰργάσατο σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄ καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_text: 24.    Τῇ Τετάρτῃ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικόν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἶτα τὰ δύο Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας ἐκ β΄, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ καὶ ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα. Οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὰ β΄ Καθίσματα, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἑορτῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Θάλασσαν ἔπηξας, εἶτα ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ καὶ τῶν δύο Κανόνων, ἡ Καταβασία Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον δίς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ Προσόμοια εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Φωτισθέντες ἀδελφοί, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Sunday of the Paralytic Concluded (§ 22) and The Wednesday of Mid-Pentecost Opening (§§ 23–24) (p. 807)]
units.english_text: ...the two Theotokia. The Exaposteilarion of Pascha: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*), and that of the Paralytic: **"The all-compassionate Lord..."** (*Ὁ παντοδύναμος Κύριος*). At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3, and the first Paschal Sticheron: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Lord, the Paralytic..."** (*Κύριε τὸν Παράλυτον*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another!..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world: let us sing unto Him Who arose from the tomb, the Author of our life!..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.english_text: 22.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Paschal Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3: **"Let the heavens rejoice, let earthly things be glad!..."** (*Εὐφραινέσθω τὰ Οὐράνια*), that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion of Pascha: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*). The Epistle (Acts 9:32–42) and Gospel (John 5:1–15) of the Sunday. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα*), with the Ninth Heirmos of the Canon: **"With one voice, O Virgin, we bless thee: Hail, gate of the Lord, through which none may pass!..."** (*Συμφώνως Παρθένε*) [Note 12]. Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: THE WEDNESDAY OF MID-PENTECOST
units.english_text: 23.    On Tuesday evening, after **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), we recite the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX). At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the three Prosomia: **"Now has come the midpoint of the days..."** (*Πάρεστιν ἡ μεσότης ἡμερῶν*) to six (i.e., twice each); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"As the Feast comes to its midpoint, O Christ God..."** (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης*). Entrance with censer, the Prokimenon of the day, and the Old Testament Readings (Micah 4:2–3, 5; 5:2–5, 8; Isaiah 55:1–3, 6–11; Proverbs 9:1–11 LXX). At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela: **"The midpoint of the days of Pentecost has arrived..."** (*Πεντηκοστῆς ἐφέστηκεν*), with the appointed Verses: **"Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning"** (*Μνήσθητι τῆς συναγωγῆς σου ἧς ἐκτήσω ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς*, Ps. 73:2 LXX), and **"God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth"** (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων εἰργάσατο σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς*, Ps. 73:12 LXX); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast, provide Thou my thirsty soul with the water of piety, as Thou didst cry unto all, O Savior: Whosoever thirsteth, let him come unto Me and drink! O Well-spring of our life, Christ God, glory to Thee!"** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*) three times, and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: 23.    On Tuesday evening, after "Christ is risen," the Introductory Psalm. At "Lord, I have cried" we chant the 3 Stichira "Now has come the midpoint of the days" in six (i.e., twice each), Glory, Now and ever, "As the Feast comes to its midpoint." Entrance, the Prokimenon of the day and the Readings. At the Aposticha: the 3 Idiomela "The midpoint of the days of Pentecost has arrived," with the Verses "Remember Your congrega- tion, which You have purchased from the beginning," and "God, our King from before the ages, has wrought salvation in the midst of the earth," Glory, Now and ever "At the midpoint of the Feast." The Apolytikion three times, and Dismissal. 24.    On Wednesday at Matins, after the Midnight Service, the Trisagion, the Apolytikion and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikion (three times), the Psalter; then the Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], twice each. Then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" and Psalm 50 (read). Both Canons without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion, the Ikos, the Minologion and the Postscript of the Feast. The Katavasie "You did make the sea a wall," then the 9th Ode of both Canons and the Katavasia "Virginity is alien to mothers"; the Exapostilarion twice. At the Praises: 3 Stichira, repeating the first, Glory, Now and ever, "Having been enlightened, brethren." Great Doxology and the Apolytikion.
units.english_text: 24.    On Wednesday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8 (three times); then the Psalter; then the two Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], twice each. Then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) and Psalm 50 recited plainly. Both Canons without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 4: **"As the Feast of the Law is at midpoint, O Creator and Master of all, Thou didst say unto those present, O Christ God: Come and draw forth the water of immortality!..."** (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς τῆς νομικῆς μεσαζούσης*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias: **"Thou didst make the sea a wall..."** (*Θάλασσαν ἔπηξας*); then the 9th Ode of both Canons, and the Katavasia: **"Virginity is alien to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished!..."** (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων*); the Exaposteilarion: **"Having arrived at the midpoint of the feasts..."** (*Ὁ τὸν κρατῆρα ἔχων*) twice. At the Praises: three Prosomia to four (repeating the first); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 4: **"Having been enlightened, brethren, by the Resurrection of Christ the Savior..."** (*Φωτισθέντες ἀδελφοί*). Great Doxology and the Dismissal Troparion.[^470]

units.english_text: 26.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, ὁ Προοιμιακὸς καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ τῆς Μεσοπεντηκοστῆς γ΄ καὶ γ΄ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος. units.slavonic_text: Τῌ Ε΄ ΚΥΡΙΑΚῌ ΑΠΟ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΣΧΑ
units.english_text: 27.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, τῆς Λιτῆς Ἀγαλλιάσθω σήμερον φαιδρῶς, καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος· τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν δύο Θεοτοκίων, Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ α΄ Κάθισμα τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ β΄ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, καὶ τὸ γ΄ αὖθις τῆς ἑορτῆς. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν δύο Θεοτοκίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Ἡ πηγὴ τῆς ζωαρχίας, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.slavonic_text: 27.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, τῆς Λιτῆς Ἀγαλλιάσθω σήμερον φαιδρῶς, καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος· τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν δύο Θεοτοκίων, Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ α΄ Κάθισμα τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ β΄ τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, καὶ τὸ γ΄ αὖθις τῆς ἑορτῆς. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν δύο Θεοτοκίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα, τῆς Σαμαρείτιδος καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Ἡ πηγὴ τῆς ζωαρχίας, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.english_text: 25.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Paschal Antiphons and Entrance Hymn. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast; the Epistle (Acts 14:6–18) and Gospel (John 7:14–30) of the day. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: the Ninth Heirmos of Mid-Pentecost: **"Virginity is alien to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished!..."** (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων ἡ παρθενία*). Communion Hymn: **"He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him. Alleluia!"** (*Ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα*, John 6:56), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 26.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 4, three of Mid-Pentecost, and three of the Samaritan Woman; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"By Jacob's well Jesus found the Samaritan woman: He Who covers the earth with clouds asks water of her..."** (*Παρὰ τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ Ἰακώβ*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 4: **"The grandparent of God for Thy sake, David the Prophet, melodiously sang concerning thee unto Him Who wrought great things in thee..."** (*Ὁ διὰ σὲ θεοπάτωρ*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 4: **"O Lord, when Thou didst ascend the Cross, Thou didst wipe away our ancestral curse..."** (*Κύριε ἀνελθὼν ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory...": of the Samaritan Woman, in Tone 8; "Both now and ever...": of the Feast, in Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Having learned the joyful proclamation of the Resurrection from the angel..."** (*Τὸ φαιδρὸν τῆς Ἀναστάσεως*), the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast in Tone 8: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: 25.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Easter. After the Entrance, the Apolytikion and Kontakion of the Feast; the Epistle and Gospel of the day. At "Especially," "Virginity is alien to mothers," Communion Hymn "He who eats My flesh," "Christ is risen," "Blessed be the name of the Lord," and Dismissal.
units.english_text: 27.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 4, the "Glory... Both now and ever..." of the Liti: **"Let heaven and earth exult today in joy, for Christ hath appeared in the flesh as man!..."** (*Ἀγαλλιάσθω σήμερον φαιδρῶς*), and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"At the midpoint of the Feast..."** (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4 (twice) and that of the Feast (once); the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 4, the Anavathmoi of Tone 4, and the Prokimenon in Tone 4. The Canon of Pascha with the two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus. After the 3rd Ode, the first Kathisma of the Feast, the second of the Samaritan Woman, and the third again of the Feast. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"Having come to the well in faith, the Samaritan woman beheld Thee, the Water of Wisdom; and having drunk abundantly, she inherited the heavenly kingdom, ever praised in songs!"** (*Πίστει ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ φρέατι*) and the Ikos of the Samaritan Woman, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman. The Katavasias of Pascha (**"It is the day of Resurrection..."**) and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Fourth Eothinon: Luke 24:1–12); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia. The Exaposteilaria: of Pascha, of the Samaritan Woman, and of the Feast. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 4, and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"The well-spring of the beginning of life, Jesus our Savior, having come to the well of the Patriarch Jacob..."** (*Ἡ πηγὴ τῆς ζωαρχίας*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

The Epistle (Acts 11:19–30) and Gospel (John 4:5–42) of the Sunday. Τῇ δὲ Δευτέρᾳ καὶ Τρίτῃ παρατείνονται τὰ μεθέορτα τῆς Μεσοπεντηκοστῆς, καὶ τῇ Τετάρτῃ ἀποδίδονται, ψαλλομένης τῆς Ἀκολουθίας ὡς διετυπώθη ἐν § 23-25 πλὴν τῶν Ἀναγνωσμάτων. Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας.

Δόξα, Κύριε παράγων ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα σωτῆρα Χριστόν, καὶ τὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.
units.english_text: 30.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ Δόξα τῆς Λιτῆς, Καὶ νῦν, Νεῦσον παρακλήσεσι, καὶ τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δίς, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον ἅπαξ, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ Καθίσματα κατὰ σειρὰν τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Ὁ Κανὼν τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότης δίς, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τοῦ Τυφλοῦ, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα ἡ θ΄ τοῦ Πάσχα μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων καὶ τῶν β΄ Θεοτοκίων, ἡ Καταβασία Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ τὰ β΄ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τὰ Στιχηρὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

units.english_text: *Rubrical Note:* The Service of the Samaritan Woman is chanted only on Sunday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, on which day its Apodosis is celebrated. On Monday and Tuesday we chant the Afterfeast hymns of Mid-Pentecost. On Wednesday we celebrate the Apodosis of Mid-Pentecost, the Service being chanted as prescribed in Paragraphs 23–25, except for the Old Testament Readings. The Epistle and Gospel are of the day.

units.english_text: 29.    On Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant seven Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 5, and three of the Blind Man; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"Lord, passing by on the way, Thou didst find a man blind from his birth..."** (*Κύριε παράγων ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 5: **"In the Red Sea there was once depicted an image of the unwedded bride..."** (*Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ*). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 5: **"Thou Who didst take flesh, O Christ our Savior, and yet wast not parted from the heavens..."** (*Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα σωτῆρα Χριστόν*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"O Sun of Righteousness, Christ God, Who by Thy pure touch didst grant light to both eyes of him who from his mother's womb was deprived of light..."** (*Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, Who for our salvation was born of the Virgin, let us faithful praise and worship!..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), the Theotokion in Tone 5: **"Hail, impassable Gate of the Lord!..."** (*Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 30.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 5, the "Glory..." of the Liti, and "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"Incline to the entreaties of thy servants, O all-blameless one..."** (*Νεῦσον παρακλήσεσι*), and the Triadic hymn: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5 (twice) and the Theotokion (once); the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 5, the Anavathmoi of Tone 5, and the Prokimenon in Tone 5. The Canon of Pascha with the two Theotokia of Saint John of Damascus. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma in Tone 8: **"As the Master of all and the Fashioner, passing by on the way, Thou didst find a blind man seated and lamenting..."** (*Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Δεσπότης*) (twice); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 4: **"My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ, as the man blind from birth, crying unto Thee in repentance: Thou art the most radiant Light of those in darkness!"** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*) and the Ikos of the Blind Man, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Blind Man. The Katavasias: **"Let us sing unto the Savior God, Who led the people through the sea with dry feet..."** (*Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ*) and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Fifth Eothinon: Luke 24:12–35); then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia, and the Katavasia: **"Thee who art beyond human mind and word, who hast given birth in time unto the Timeless One, the faithful with one accord do magnify!"** (*Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν*). The Exaposteilarion of Pascha: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*) and the two Exaposteilaria of the Blind Man: **"Passing by, our Savior found the blind man..."** (*Παράγων ὁ Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν*). At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 5, and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"Who can tell of Thy mighty acts, O Christ, or who can recount the multitudes of Thy wonders?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

units.slavonic_text: 29.    On Saturday evening following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we sing 7 Stichira of the Resurrection, and 3 of the Blind Man, Glory, "Lord, passing by on the way," Now and ever, "In the Red Sea." At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichiron "You, the savior Christ who took on flesh," then the Stichira of Pascha "A sacred Pascha," Glory, "O Sun of Righteousness," Now and ever "It is the day of Resurrection." The Resurrection Apolytikion "The co-eternal Word," the Theotokion "Hail, impassable Gate of the Lord," and Dismissal. 30.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, the Glory of the Liti, Now and ever "Incline to the entreaties" and the "It is meet"; then the Trisagion, the Apolytikion and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikion (twice) and the Theotokion (once), the Psalter and the Amomos. The Kathismata, in order, of the First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi of the Mode, the Anavathmi and the Prokimenon. The Canon of Easter with the two Theotokia. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma "As the Master of all" (twice); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Blind Man, the Minologion and the Postscript of the Sunday. The Katavasie "Let us sing unto the Savior God" and the entire order of the Morning Gospel; then the Ninth Ode of Pascha with the Megalynaria together with the two Theotokia and the Katavasia "You, who are beyond the human mind." The Exapostilarion of Pascha and the two Exapostilaria of the Blind Man. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and the Stichira "A sacred Pascha," Glory, "Who can tell of Your mighty acts, O Christ," Now and ever, "It is the day of Resurrection," Great Doxology and "Today salvation." 31.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Easter. After the Entrance, the Apolytikion of the Resurrection, that of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion of Pascha. units.english_text: 32.    Τῇ Δευτέρᾳ ἑσπέρας ἀποδίδοται ἡ Ἀκολουθία τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ τῇ Τρίτῃ ἑσπέρας σημειούμενα κατὰ σειρὰν ς΄ Ἰδιόμελα. Δόξα, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ τοῦ Σαββάτου ἑσπέρας τῆς Ὀκτωήχου δ΄ Στιχηρὰ Διὰ τοῦ Τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ, Ὁ τὴν Ἀνάστασιν διδούς, Μέγα θαῦμα καὶ τὸ Ἀπόστιχον Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα, μετὰ τῶν στίχων Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσε κτλ. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον, τὸ Θεοτοκίον Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.slavonic_text: Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα, Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν Σῶμα Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις. 32.    Τῇ Δευτέρᾳ ἑσπέρας ἀποδίδοται ἡ Ἀκολουθία τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ ἐν τῷ Πεντηκοσταρίῳ τῇ Τρίτῃ ἑσπέρας σημειούμενα κατὰ σειρὰν ς΄ Ἰδιόμελα. Δόξα, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Καὶ νῦν, Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὰ τοῦ Σαββάτου ἑσπέρας τῆς Ὀκτωήχου δ΄ Στιχηρὰ Διὰ τοῦ Τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ, Ὁ τὴν Ἀνάστασιν διδούς, Μέγα θαῦμα καὶ τὸ Ἀπόστιχον Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα, μετὰ τῶν στίχων Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσε κτλ. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον, τὸ Θεοτοκίον Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις. 33.    Τῇ Τρίτῃ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικόν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ ἅπαξ τὸ Θεοτοκίον, τὸ Ψαλτήριον, τὰ Καθίσματα τῆς α΄ καὶ β΄ Στιχολογίας τὰ ἐν τῇ Τετάρτῃ σημειούμενα, τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ, ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ ὁ Κανὼν τῆς Κυριακῆς Σταύρωσιν ἑκούσιον, οὗ ὁ Στίχος Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Δόξα σοι, καὶ ὁ Προεόρτιος Ἄνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μετὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ Στίχου. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα Ὠμμάτωσας Χριστέ, καὶ τὸ ἕτερον Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτός. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ τῆς Κυριακῆς, καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῶν Ἁγίων τῆς ἡμέρας. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ, καὶ στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, ἡ Καταβασία Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν, τὰ β΄ τοῦ Τυφλοῦ Ἐξαποστειλάρια. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ γ΄, τὰ τῶν Αἴνων τῆς Κυριακῆς, καὶ τὰ γ΄ πρῶτα ἑσπέρια τοῦ Τυφλοῦ. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ, Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον. 34.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικόν. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, καὶ Κοντάκιον Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν τῆς ἡμέρας, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_text: 32.    On Monday evening, the Apodosis of the Service of the Blind Man takes place. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the six Idiomela from the Pentekostarion which are indicated in the Vespers of Tuesday evening, in order; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"Who can tell of Thy mighty acts, O Christ?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 5: **"In the Red Sea there was once depicted an image of the unwedded bride..."** (*Ἐν τῇ Ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ*). At the Aposticha: the four Saturday evening Stichera of the Octoechos in Tone 5: **"By Thy precious Cross hast Thou put the devil to shame, O Christ..."** (*Διὰ τοῦ Τιμίου σου Σταυροῦ*), **"He Who has granted resurrection unto the human race..."** (*Ὁ τὴν Ἀνάστασιν διδούς*), **"O great wonder! The Creator of invisible things..."** (*Μέγα θαῦμα*), and the Apostichon: **"Thou Who didst take flesh, O Christ our Savior..."** (*Σὲ τὸν σαρκωθέντα σωτῆρα Χριστόν*), with the verses: **"The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty!"** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν*, Ps. 92:1 LXX) etc.; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"O Sun of Righteousness, Christ God..."** (*Δικαιοσύνης Ἥλιε*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), the Theotokion in Tone 5: **"Hail, impassable Gate of the Lord!..."** (*Χαῖρε Πύλη Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: Sunday. At "Especially," "The Angel cried out . . . Shine, shine," Communion Hymn "[Receive] the body of Christ," [the Apolytikion] "Christ is risen," "Blessed be the name of the Lord," and Dismissal. 32.    On Monday evening, the Leave-taking of the Service of the Blind Man takes place. At "Lord, I have cried" we sing the six Idiomela from the Pentikostarion which are found in the Vespers of Tuesday evening. Glory, "Who can tell of Your mighty acts, O Christ," Now and ever, "In the Red Sea." At the Aposticha: the Saturday Stichira of the Oktoichos "By Your precious Cross," "He Who has granted the Resurrection, "O great wonder!" and the Apostichon "You, Who took on flesh" with the Verses "The Lord has reigned as King" etc. Glory, Now and ever, "The Sun of Righteousness." The Apolytikion "The co-eternal Word," the Theotokion "Hail! impassable Gate of the Lord," and Dismissal. 33.    On Tuesday at Matins, after Midnight Service, the Trisagion, the Apolytikion and the Exapsalmos. At "God is the Lord": the Apolytikion (twice) and the Theotokion (once), then the Psalter. The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis [Stichologia], which are indicated on Wednesday morning. Then we recite the "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," Psalm 50 and the Canon of Sunday "Having accepted a voluntary crucifix- ion," with the Verse "Glory to You, our God, glory to You" and of the Pre- feast "Up unto the Father" with its verse. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma "You gave eyes, O Christ" and the other one, i.e., "You were born as such." After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday and the Minologion of the Saints of the day. The Katavasie "Let us sing unto the Savior God," and we chant "More honorable" with the Katavasia "You, who are beyond the human mind." The two Exapostilaria of the Blind Man. At the Praises: 3 Resurrection Stichira of the Sunday, and the first 3 Vesper hymns of the Blind Man, Glory, Now and ever, "Who can tell of Your mighty acts, O Christ," Great Doxology and "The co-eternal Word." 34.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Easter. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, that of the Saint of the Church, the Kontakion "My soul's eyes," the Epistle and Gospel of the day. At "Especially," "It is meet," the Communion Hymn of the day, [the Apolytikion] "Christ is risen," "Blessed be the name of the Lord" and Dismissal.
units.english_text: 33.    On Tuesday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5 (twice) and the Theotokion (once), then the Psalter. The Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], which are indicated on Wednesday morning; then we recite **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), Psalm 50, and the Sunday Canon: **"Having accepted a voluntary crucifixion, O Master..."** (*Σταύρωσιν ἑκούσιον*), with the Verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι*), and the Forefeast Canon: **"Up unto the Father hast Thou ascended, O Christ God..."** (*Ἄνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα*) with the same Verse. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma in Tone 4: **"Thou didst give eyes to him who was blind from birth, O Christ..."** (*Ὠμμάτωσας Χριστέ*) and the other one: **"Thou wast born as such, O blind man..."** (*Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτός*). After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday of the Blind Man, and the Menologion of the Saints of the day. The Katavasias: **"Let us sing unto the Savior God..."** (*Τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ*); and we chant **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*) with the Katavasia: **"Thee who art beyond human mind and word..."** (*Σὲ τὴν ὑπὲρ νοῦν*). The two Exaposteilaria of the Blind Man. At the Praises: three Resurrectional Stichera of the Sunday in Tone 5, and the first three Vespers hymns of the Blind Man; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: **"Who can tell of Thy mighty acts, O Christ?..."** (*Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας σου Χριστέ*). Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*).

units.english_text: 34.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Paschal Antiphons and Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion in Tone 5, that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion in Tone 4: **"My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ..."** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*). The Epistle (Acts 16:20–34) and Gospel (John 9:39–10:9) of the day. At "Especially", **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God!..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the Communion Hymn of the day: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens, praise Him in the highest! Alleluia!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX), the Dismissal Troparion: **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.[^473]

units.english_text: 35.    Τῇ Τρίτῃ ἑσπέρας ἀναγινώσκεται ἡ θ΄ ὥρα τρίψαλμος, ἐν ᾗ λέγομεν Ἀπολυτίκιον Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον, καὶ Κοντάκιον Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα· εἶτα ἀντὶ τοῦ Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς λέγεται (ὡς εἴθισται νῦν) Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ ψάλλεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἱερέως ἔσωθεν τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη γ΄ καὶ ἀνὰ γ΄ ὑπὸ [ἑκάστου] τῶν Χορῶν, καὶ ἅπαξ αὖθις ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἱερέως. [Σημειωτέον ὅτι ἡ τάξις τοῦ Πεντηκοσταρίου ἁπλῶς λέγει· «Καὶ ψάλλομεν τὸ Χριστὸς Ἀνέστη, μετὰ τῶν στίχων αὐτοῦ ὅπως ἔγινε τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Πάσχα.» Ὡς φαίνεται, ἀπαιτεῖται ἐδῶ ἡ ἰδία τάξις, δηλαδή, ἐὰν ἕκαστος τῶν δύο Χορῶν ψάλλει τὸ Χριστὸς Ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄, τότε ἔχομεν τὸ σύνολον τῶν 10 ὅπως εἰς τὸ Πάσχα.]

units.slavonic_text: Τῌ ΤΕΤΑΡΤῌ ΤΗΣ ΣΤ΄ ΕΒΔΟΜΑΔΟΣ
units.english_text: 36.    Τῷ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον μετὰ τὸ μεσονυκτικὸν τοῦ Πάσχα (ὅρα ἐν § 2 ὑποσημ. 8) ὁ Ἱερεὺς θυμιῶν ἐνώπιον τῆς Ἁγίας Τραπέζης ἐκφωνεῖ Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ, καὶ ψάλλει τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ὡς χθές· εἶτα ἡ Συναπτὴ καὶ ψάλλεται ὁ Κανὼν εἰς δ΄, ἡ Καταβασία ὁμοῦ, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη γ΄, τὸ Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἡ Αἴτησις καὶ ἡ Ἐκφώνησις ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοὴ Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ γ΄, τὸ Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡ ζ΄ καὶ η΄ τοῦ Κανόνος Ὠδή· εἶτα Τὴν θεοτόκον, καὶ ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ἐκ γ΄. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ Στιχηρὰ Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστὲ εἰς δ΄ καὶ τὰ Πάσχα ἱερόν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη τρίς, καὶ ἄρχεται ἡ Λειτουργία.

units.english_text: 35.    On Tuesday evening the Ninth Hour is read as tri-psalmic (i.e., involving three psalms: Psalms 83, 84, 85 LXX), at which we say the Dismissal Troparion: **"The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit..."** (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), and the Kontakion: **"My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ..."** (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*); then, instead of the usual **"Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, the Priest exclaims (as is the custom now): **"Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and indivisible Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ*). Then the Priest inside the Sanctuary chants **"Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!"** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) three times; this hymn is chanted also three times by each of the two Choirs, and again immediately once by the Priest from the Sanctuary [Note: The rubrics of the Pentekostarion state simply: "And we chant Christ is risen with its verses, exactly as was done on the day of Pascha." Apparently, this exact order is what is actually being called for here: if each of the two Choirs chants "Christ is risen" three times, we have the sum total of 10 times, as on the day of Pascha].

units.english_text: Then the Litany follows. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the six Stichera of the Octoechos in Tone 5: **"Accept our evening prayers, O holy Lord, and grant unto us remission of sins; for Thou alone art He Who didst manifest the Resurrection unto the world!"** (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς*) in order; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: **"Him Who is co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, let us praise..."** (*Τὸν τῷ Πατρὶ συνάναρχον*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 1: **"The Joy of all the world, who sprang forth from mankind and gave birth unto the Master..."** (*Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν*). Entrance with censer, and the Prokimenon of the day: **"Thy mercy, O Lord, shall pursue me all the days of my life!"** (*Τὸ ἔλεός σου, Κύριε*, Ps. 22:6 LXX). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 5: **"By Thy Passion, O Christ, hast Thou darkened the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection hast Thou enlightened all things..."** (*Τῷ πάθει σου Χριστέ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another!..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 36.    In the morning at Matins, after the Midnight Office of Pascha (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest censing in front of the Holy Table exclaims: **"Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and indivisible Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."**, and chants **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) as yesterday; then the Litany, and the Paschal Canon is chanted with four Troparia for each ode including the Katavasia. Then we chant **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), the hymn: **"Jesus, having arisen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given unto us life eternal and great mercy!"** (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου*), the Litany, and the Exclamation at the end of each Ode. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoe: **"Coming before the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..."** (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον*) (recited plainly); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..."** and the Ikos of Pascha, then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the holy Lord Jesus..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) (three times), and **"Jesus, having arisen from the tomb..."** (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς*); then the 7th and 8th Odes of the Canon are chanted. Then the deacon or priest proclaims: **"The Theotokos and Mother of the Light, honoring her in hymns, let us magnify!"** (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the 9th Ode is chanted with the Megalynaria of Pascha. The Exaposteilarion: **"Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst arise..."** (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*) (three times). At the Praises: the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1: **"We praise Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and glorify Thy Resurrection!"** (*Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστέ*) and the Stichera of Pascha: **"A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..."** (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 5: **"It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..."** (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), then **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins.[^474]

units.english_text: 37.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τοῦ Πάσχα καὶ τὸ Εἰσοδικόν. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον, Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου, Κοινωνικὸν τοῦ Πάσχα, Χριστὸς ἀνέστη. Μετὰ τὴν Ὀπισθάμβωνον εὐχήν, τὸ Χριστὸς ἀνέστη ἐκ γ΄ χῦμα, Ἀπόλυσις καὶ Ἀπόδοσις.

units.english_text: 37.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance we chant **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), the Ypakoe, and the Kontakion. Instead of the Trisagion Hymn we chant **"As many as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia!"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*); the Epistle and the Gospel of the day. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: **"The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee!..."** (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα . . . Φωτίζου, φωτίζου*). Communion Hymn of Pascha: **"Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!"** (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*). After the Prayer behind the Amvon, **"Christ is risen from the dead..."** (three times) recited plainly, the Dismissal, and the Apodosis.

units.english_text: 38.    On Wednesday evening, after the Ninth Hour of Pascha, the Priest intones **"Blessed is our God..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς*), and the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) begins with **"Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ, our King and our God"** (three times). At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the five Idiomela: **"The Lord ascended into the heavens, that He might send the Paraclete unto the world..."** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἀνελήφθη*) to six, repeating the first hymn; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"Without parting from the Fatherly bosom, O sweetest Jesus..."** (*Τῶν κόλπων τῶν Πατρικῶν*). Entrance with censer, the Prokimenon of the day, and the Old Testament Readings (Isaiah 2:2–3; 62:10–63:3, 7–9; Zechariah 14:1, 4, 8–11 LXX). At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet..."** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ*). The Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God, having gladdened Thy disciples with the promise of the Holy Spirit, they having been assured by the blessing that Thou art the Son of God, the Redeemer of the world!"** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*) three times, and the Dismissal with the following appointed prologue: **"He Who ascended in glory from us into the heavens and sat at the right hand of God the Father, Christ our true God..."** (*Ὁ ἐν δόξῃ ἀναληφθεὶς ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς Οὐρανοὺς καὶ ἐν δεξιᾷ καθίσας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*).

units.slavonic_text: 37.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Easter. After the Entrance we chant "Christ is risen," the Ypakoi, and the Kontakion. [Instead of the Trisagios Hymn] we chant "As many as have been baptized in Christ"; the Apostolos and the Gospel of the day. At "Especially," "The Angel cried out . . . Shine, shine," Communion Hymn of Easter, "Christ is risen." After the Prayer behind the Amvon "Christ is risen" (three times) intoned plainly, the Dismissal, and the Leave-taking.
units.english_text: 39.    On Thursday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Liti, then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ascended in glory..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion (three times); then the Psalter and the Polyeleos. The Kathismata in order, twice each; the Anavathmoi: the first Antiphon of Tone 4 (**"From my youth many passions war against me..."**), and the Prokimenon: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet!"** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, Κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος*, Ps. 46:5 LXX), **"Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord!"** (*Πᾶσα πνοὴ*), and the Third Matins Gospel (Mark 16:9–20), **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), and Psalm 50 recited plainly. "Glory...": **"Through the intercessions of the Apostles..."** (*Ταῖς τῶν Ἀποστόλων*); "Both now and ever...": **"Through the intercessions of the Theotokos..."** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*); the Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy..."** (*Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεὸς*), and the Idiomelon: **"Today the heavenly powers in the heavens marvel seeing our nature ascend..."** (*Σήμερον ἐν Οὐρανοῖς αἱ ἄνω δυνάμεις*). Both Canons, the first to six and the second to four, without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma (once); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 6: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes, and united things on earth with the heavenly, Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias: **"Covered by a divine cloud, he that was slow of tongue proclaimed the Law written of God..."** (*Θείῳ καλυφθείς*); then the 9th Ode is chanted: the first Canon without verses, and the second Canon with its Megalynarion: **"Ye Angels, marveling at the ascension of the Master, how with glory He was taken up from earth unto the heights..."** (*Ἄγγελοι τὴν ἄνοδον τοῦ Δεσπότου . . . πῶς μετὰ δόξης ἐπήρθη ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς εἰς τὰ ἄνω*); the Katavasia: **"Rejoice, O Queen, boasting of virgins and mothers!..."** (*Χαίροις Ἄνασσα*), then the Exaposteilarion: **"While the disciples looked on, Thou wast taken up, O Christ, unto the Father, to sit beside Him..."** (*Τῶν Μαθητῶν ὁρώντων σε*) (three times). At the Praises: the three Prosomia to four (repeating the first); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 2: **"Thou wast born as Thou Thyself didst will; Thou didst appear as Thou Thyself didst wish; Thou didst suffer in the flesh, O our God..."** (*Ἐτέχθης ὡς αὐτὸς ἠθέλησας*)...[^475]

units.slavonic_incipit: Πάντα τὰ ἔθνη κροτήσατε χεῖρας, ἀλαλάξατε
units.slavonic_text: Πάντα τὰ ἔθνη κροτήσατε χεῖρας, ἀλαλάξατε τῷ Θεῷ τῷ Σωτῆρι ἡμῶν. Ὅτι Κύριος ὕψιστος, φοβερὸς βασιλεὺς Μέγας, ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν. Ὑπέταξε λαοὺς ἡμῖν καὶ ἔθνη ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν. | Ταῖς πρεσβείαις | τῆς Θεοτόκου... Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ταῖς πρεσβείαις τῆς Θεοτόκου . . .
units.english_text:

καὶ ἔθνη ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν.

Κλινῶ εἰς παραβολὴν τὸ οὖς μου, ἀνοίξω ἐν ψαλτηρίῳ τὸ πρόβλημά μου. | Ἀνελήφθης | ἐν δόξῃ. units.slavonic_text: Clap your hands, all you nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing. For the Lord Most high is terrible, a great King over all the earth. Amen.

units.slavonic_text: *(Printed Page 819)*
units.english_text: The Entrance Hymn: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet! Save us, O Son of God, Who didst ascend in glory from us into the heavens, save us who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, Κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος· Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν δόξῃ ἀναληφθείς...*). The Dismissal Troparion: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*), the Kontakion: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*)...[^476]

units.english_text: 42.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανών, τὸ τῆς Λιτῆς Δόξα, Ἀποστολικῶν παραδόσεων, Καὶ νῦν, Κύριε τῆς οἰκονομίας πληρώσας τὸ μυστήριον, τὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ὑπερδεδοξασμένος εἶ καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὰ Ἀπολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα κατὰ σειρὰν Καθίσματα, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοὴ τοῦ ἤχου, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον· οἱ Κανόνες, ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος, ὁ τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ τῶν Πατέρων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς {Σημ. Μεταφραστοῦ· Λέγομεν τὸ Κοντάκιον τῆς Ἀναλήψεως. Αὐτὸ ὑποδεικνύουν τὸ Πεντηκοστάριον καὶ τὰ 1998 καὶ 1999 Ἡμερολόγια [ΗΟΠ]. Παρότι τὸ Τυπικὸν δὲν εἶναι σαφὲς εἰς αὐτὸ τὸ σημεῖον, ἡ Προθεωρία, σελ. (Βιολάκης σελ. 22), §25, ὑποστηρίζει αὐτὴν τὴν πράξην}, τὸ Κάθισμα τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον, καὶ Οἶκος τὰ τῶν Πατέρων, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Πατέρων. Αἱ Καταβασίαι Θείῳ καλυφθείς, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἐξαποστειλάριον, τὸ τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῶν Πατέρων δ΄. Δόξα, Τῶν Ἁγίων Πατέρων ὁ χορός, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη. Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

Communion Hymn: **"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet. Alleluia!"** (*Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ*, Ps. 46:5 LXX). After the Communion Hymn, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*); **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and the Dismissal as in Vespers [Note 13].

units.english_text: 41.    In Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX) and the Psalter (First Kathisma: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX), at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant three Resurrectional Stichera of Tone 6, three of the Ascension, and four of the Fathers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"Let us extol today the mystical trumpets of the Spirit, the God-bearing Fathers..."** (*Τὰς μυστικὰς σήμερον*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion of Tone 6: **"Who would not call thee blessed, O all-holy Virgin?..."** (*Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε*). Entrance with censer, **"O Joyful Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokimenon of the day: **"The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty!"** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν*, Ps. 92:1 LXX), and the Old Testament Readings (Genesis 14:14–20; Deuteronomy 1:8–11, 15–17; 10:14–21 LXX). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Stichera; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 4: **"Let us faithfully celebrate today the yearly commemoration of the God-bearing Fathers..."** (*Τὴν ἐτήσιον μνήμην σήμερον*); "Both now and ever...": of the Feast, in Tone 4: **"O Lord, having fulfilled the mystery hidden from the ages..."** (*Κύριε τὸ μυστήριον*). The Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion of Tone 6, "Glory...": that of the Fathers in Tone 8: **"Most glorified art Thou, O Christ our God, Who hast established our Fathers as luminous stars upon the earth..."** (*Ὑπερδεδοξασμένος εἶ*); "Both now and ever...": that of the Ascension in Tone 4: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*), and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 42.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon in Tone 6, the "Glory..." of the Liti: **"Keeping the Apostolic traditions..."** (*Ἀποστολικῶν παραδόσεων*); "Both now and ever...": of the Feast: **"O Lord, having fulfilled the mystery of the dispensation..."** (*Κύριε τῆς οἰκονομίας πληρώσας τὸ μυστήριον*); then the Triadic hymns: **"It is truly right..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion of the Fathers: **"Most glorified art Thou, O Christ our God..."** (*Ὑπερδεδοξασμένος εἶ*), and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma). The Resurrectional Kathismata in order, the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (**"Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes"**), the Ypakoe of Tone 6, the Anavathmoi of Tone 6, and the Prokimenon of Tone 6. The Canons: the Resurrectional Canon, that of the Feast, and that of the Fathers. After the 3rd Ode [Translator's Note: We recite the Kontakion of the Ascension: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*). Note that this is indicated both in the Pentekostarion and in the Imerologia [IEP] 1998 and 1999; though the Typikon itself is not clear on this issue, it appears that a look at the Protheoria (Violakis, p. 22, § 25) supports this practice], then the Kathisma of the Fathers and that of the Feast. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"The preaching of the Apostles and the dogmas of the Fathers confirmed the one Faith for the Church..."** (*Τῶν Ἀποστόλων τὸ κήρυγμα*) and the Ikos of the Fathers, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Sunday of the Fathers. The Katavasias: **"Covered by a divine cloud..."** (*Θείῳ καλυφθείς*), and the entire order of the Matins Gospel (Tenth Eothinon: John 21:1–14); then we chant with verses: **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*). Exaposteilaria: the Resurrectional Exaposteilarion, that of the Fathers, and that of the Feast. At the Praises: four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 6 and four of the Fathers; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"The choir of the Holy Fathers, coming together from the ends of the earth..."** (*Τῶν Ἁγίων Πατέρων ὁ χορός*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 2: **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις*). Great Doxology and Dismissal Troparion: **"Today is salvation come into the world..."** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).[^477]

units.slavonic_text: 41.    In Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm and the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" we chant 3 Stichira of the Resurrection, 3 of the Ascension, and 4 of the Fathers. Glory, "Let us extol today those mystical trumpets," Now and ever, "Who would not call you blessed." Entrance, "O Gladsome Light," the Prokimenon and the Read- ings. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira, Glory, "The yearly commemoration today," Now and ever, "Lord, the mystery." The Apolytikion of the Resurrection, Glory that of the Fathers, Now and ever, "You have ascended in glory," and Dismissal. 42.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Triadic Canon, the Glory of the Liti "Of the Apostolic traditions," Now and ever of the Feast "Lord, when You did fulfill the mystery of the economy"; then the "It is meet," the Trisagion, the Apolytikion "Exceedingly glorified" and the Exapsalmos. At God is the Lord: the Apolytikia as in Vespers, then the Psalter and the Amomos. The Resurrection Kathismata in order, the Evlogitaria, the Ypakoi of the Mode, the Anavathmi, and the Prokimenon. The Canons of the Resurrection, of the Feast, and of the Fathers. After the 3rd Ode, {Translator's Note: We recite the Kontakion of the Ascension. Note that this is indicated both in the Pentikostarion and Imerologia [IEP] 1998 and 1999; though the Typikon itself is not clear on this issue, it appears that a look at the Protheoria [p. , (Violakis, p. 22), Para. 25] supports this usage} and then the Kathisma of the Fathers and that of the Feast. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Fathers, the Minologion and the Postscript of the Sunday of the Fathers. The Katavasie "Covered by a divine cloud," and the entire order of the Morning Gospel; then we sing, with verses, "More honorable." Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of the Fathers and of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Fathers, Glory, "The chorus of the Holy Fathers," Now and ever, "Most blessed." Great Doxology and "Today salvation."

units.english_text: 43.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Πατέρων. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς τῶν Πατέρων, καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ· Κοντάκιον Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας οἰκονομίαν· Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. units.slavonic_text: 44.    Τῇ Παρασκευῇ ἑσπέρας, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν ς΄ Στιχηρά, Μαρτυρικὰ δ΄ (ἐκ τῆς Ὀκτωήχου) Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε, καὶ γ΄ τῶν Κεκοιμημένων Τῶν ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος σήμερον νεκρῶν, Δόξα, Θρηνῶ καὶ ὀδύρομαι, Καὶ νῦν, Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε, ἀντὶ Προκειμένου ψάλλεται τρεῖς φορὰς τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα ἐκ γ΄ μετὰ τῶν ὡρισμένων στίχων εἰς τὰς δύο τελευταίας φοράς. Εἰς τὰ Ἀπόστιχα τὸ Μαρτυρικὸν Ὁ Σταυρός σου Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δύο Νεκρώσιμα μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτῶν. Δόξα, Ἀρχή μοι καὶ ὑπόστασις, Καὶ νῦν, Πρεσβείαις τῆς τεκούσης σε, τὸ Νῦν ἀπολύεις, καὶ εὐθὺς ψάλλεται ὁ Κανὼν Ἐν οὐρανίοις θαλάμοις μετὰ τῶν Στίχων Πρεσβείαις τῶν Μαρτύρων σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, ἀνάπαυσον τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν δούλων σου, καὶ τὸ Αἱ ψυχαὶ αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς αὐλισθήσονται, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, ἐν ἑκάστῃ Ὠδῇ. Ἀπ᾿ θ΄ ὁ Εἱρμός, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, Δόξα, τὸ τέλος Ἐν σοὶ γὰρ τὴν ἐλπίδα κτλ. Καὶ νῦν, Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν, εἶτα Μετὰ Πνευμάτων δικαίων κτλ. καὶ μνημονεύονται ἐπὶ τῶν κολλύβων τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν Κεκοιμημένων, ὡς ἐσημειώθη ἐν τῷ Τριῳ

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Seventh Sunday Liturgy (§ 43), Apodosis of Ascension Note, and Saturday of the Seventh Week: Memorial Saturday (§ 44 Opening) (p. 823)]
units.english_text: 43.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Typika and the Beatitudes of Tone 6 to four, and four hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Fathers. After the Entrance, the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion of Tone 6, that of the Feast (Ascension), that of the Fathers, and that of the Patron Saint of the Church; the Kontakion: **"When Thou hadst fulfilled the dispensation for our sakes..."** (*Τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πληρώσας*). The Epistle (Acts 20:16–18, 28–36) and Gospel (John 17:1–13) of the Sunday. At "Especially", **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*). Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens, praise Him in the highest! Alleluia!"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX). At "With the fear of God...", we chant the Dismissal Troparion of the Ascension: **"Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God..."** (*Ἀνελήφθης ἐν δόξῃ*). Then **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal.

units.slavonic_text: 43.    In the Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Mode and 4 hymns from the 6th Ode of the Canon of the Fathers. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Apolytikion, that of the Feast, that of the Fathers, that of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion "When You had fulfilled for us the economy." Apostolos and Gospel of the Sunday. At "Especially," "It is meet," Communion Hymn "Praise the Lord"; at "With the fear of God," we chant "You ascended in glory." Then "Blessed be the name of the Lord" and Dismissal. On Friday of this week the Leave-taking of the Feast of the Ascension takes place; the Service is sung exactly as prescribed in Paragraphs 38 - 40: in Vespers, with the exception of the Readings; and in Matins, with the exception of the Liti of the Polyeleos with its Kathisma of the Third Stasis, and also of the Gospel. In the Liturgy, we read the Apostolos and Gospel of the day.

units.slavonic_text: THE SATURDAY OF THIS [SEVENTH] WEEK [THAT IS, THE SATURDAY BEFORE PENTECOST]
units.english_text: 44.    On Friday evening, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant six Stichera: four Martyrika from the Octoechos: **"Thy Martyrs, O Lord..."** (*Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε*), and three for the Reposed: **"Today, those who have died from time immemorial..."** (*Τῶν ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος σήμερον νεκρῶν*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"I weep and I lament when I contemplate death..."** (*Θρηνῶ καὶ ὀδύρομαι*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 8: **"Who would not call thee blessed, O all-holy Virgin?..."** (*Τίς μὴ μακαρίσει σε*). In place of the Prokimenon, we chant **"Alleluia"** three times, with the appointed verses chanted for the last two times. At the Aposticha: the Martyrikon: **"Thy Cross, O Lord..."** (*Ὁ Σταυρός σου Κύριε*), and the two Stichera of the Reposed with their verses. "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"My beginning and foundation was Thy creative command..."** (*Ἀρχή μοι καὶ ὑπόστασις*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"By the intercessions of her who gave birth unto Thee, O Christ..."** (*Πρεσβείαις τῆς τεκούσης σε*). The prayer **"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..."** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*), and immediately we chant the Canon: **"In the heavenly bridal chambers..."** (*Ἐν οὐρανίοις θαλάμοις*) with the Verses: **"Through the intercessions of Thy Martyrs, O Christ God, give rest to the souls of Thy servants!"** (*Πρεσβείαις τῶν Μαρτύρων σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, ἀνάπαυσον τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν δούλων σου*) and **"Their souls shall dwell with good things"** (*Αἱ ψυχαὶ αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοῖς αὐλισθήσονται*, Ps. 24:13 LXX), chanting "Glory...", "Both now and ever..." in each Ode. After the 9th Ode, the Heirmos, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*); "Glory...": the ending: **"For in Thee have they placed their hope, our Maker and Creator and God"** (*Ἐν σοὶ γὰρ τὴν ἐλπίδα*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"Thee do we have as a rampart and haven..."** (*Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν*); then the Troparia: **"With the souls of the righteous departed, give rest to the soul of Thy servant, O Savior..."** (*Μετὰ πνευμάτων δικαίων*), and the names of the Reposed are commemorated over the Kolyvo [boiled wheat], as noted in the Triodion...[^478]

Τῷ Σαββάτῳ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικὸν τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος· εἶτα τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα μετὰ τῶν Στίχων αὐτοῦ καὶ τῶν Ἀπολυτικίων, ὡς ἐλέχθη ἐν τῷ Σαββάτῳ πρὸ τῆς Ἀπόκρεω· τὸ Ψαλτήριον, τὰ Καθίσματα, καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, καὶ μνημονεύονται τὰ ὀνόματα ὡς χθὲς ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ — τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, καὶ μετὰ τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν, {τὸ Κάθισμα} Ἀνάπαυσον Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν, {Δόξα,} Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου ἀνατείλας· εἶτα ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς καὶ ὁ Κανὼν Ψυχῶν πασῶν ὁ Δεσπότης μετὰ τῶν ὡρισμένων Στίχων. Ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα, καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τοῦ Τριῳδίου· εἶτα ψάλλεται ὁ Εἱρμὸς τῆς η΄ Ὠδῆς Ἔκστηθι φρίττων Οὐρανέ, καὶ στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, ὁ Εἱρμὸς Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα, τὰ β΄ Ἐξαποστειλάρια. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ δ΄ Στιχηρὰ Φοβερὸν τὸ τέλος τὸ τοῦ θανάτου, Δόξα, Ὡς ἄνθος μαραίνεται, Καὶ νῦν, Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, τὸ Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει χῦμα, ἡ Συναπτή, καὶ τὰ δ΄ Ἀπόστιχα Ἔχων ἀκατάληπτον, Δόξα, Ἄλγος τῷ Ἀδάμ, Καὶ νῦν, Ὤφθης ἐνδιαίτημα, τὸ Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὰ δύο Τροπάρια, Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, καὶ τὸ Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος.

Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Ἀντίφωνα, Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι, μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον Ὁ βάθει σοφίας, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, τὸ Κοντάκιον Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον Χριστέ (ὅρα ς΄ Ὠδὴν τοῦ ἑσπερινοῦ Κανόνος). Ἀπόστολος Νεκρώσιμος, καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω, ἀντὶ τοῦ Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς, Ὁ βάθει σοφίας φιλανθρώπως πάντα οἰκονομῶν 14· εἶτα ψάλλεται τὸ Μετὰ πνευμάτων δικαίων, καὶ μνημονεύονται τὰ ὀνόματα πάντων τῶν ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος κεκοιμημένων εὐσεβῶν καὶ Ὀρθοδόξων Χριστιανῶν κτλ. καὶ Ἀπόλυσις.

units.english_text: 45.    On Saturday at Matins, after the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*), and the Six Psalms; then **"Alleluia"** with its verses and the Dismissal Troparia, as prescribed on the Saturday before Meatfare Sunday; the Psalter, the Kathismata, and the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX / 17th Kathisma), and the names of the Reposed are commemorated as yesterday at Vespers; the Evlogitaria, and after the Exclamation, the Kathisma: **"Give rest with the righteous, O our Savior, unto Thy servants..."** (*Ἀνάπαυσον Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν*); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Theotokion: **"O Thou Who didst dawn from the Virgin..."** (*Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου ἀνατείλας*). Then Psalm 50, and the Canon: **"O Master of all souls..."** (*Ψυχῶν πασῶν ὁ Δεσπότης*) with the prescribed verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma and the Theotokion. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"With the Saints grant rest, O Christ, unto the souls of Thy servants, where there is neither pain, nor grief, nor sighing, but life everlasting!"** (*Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Triodion; then we chant the Heirmos of the 8th Ode: **"Be astonished and tremble, O heaven..."** (*Ἔκστηθι φρίττων Οὐρανέ*), we chant with verses: **"More honorable than the Cherubim..."** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν Χερουβίμ*), the Heirmos: **"Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee as is meet..."** (*Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα*), and the two Exaposteilaria. At the Praises: the four Stichera: **"Dreaded is the end, the coming of death..."** (*Φοβερὸν τὸ τέλος τὸ τοῦ θανάτου*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 8: **"As a flower fadeth, and as a shadow passeth away, so is every man dissolved..."** (*Ὡς ἄνθος μαραίνεται*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 8: **"Thou art our God, Who in wisdom hast fashioned all things..."** (*Σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*); the prayer **"To Thee belongeth glory..."** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*) recited plainly, the Litany, and the four Aposticha: **"Having an inconceivable depth of compassions, O Christ..."** (*Ἔχων ἀκατάληπτον*); "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: **"A pain unto Adam was the eating of the tree of old in Eden..."** (*Ἄλγος τῷ Ἀδάμ*); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 6: **"Thou hast been seen as a dwelling-place, O unwedded Virgin..."** (*Ὤφθης ἐνδιαίτημα*); then **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord, and to chant unto Thy name, O Most High"** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*, Ps. 91:1 LXX); the Trisagion, the two Dismissal Troparia: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*) and **"Thee do we have as a rampart and haven..."** (*Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν*).

units.slavonic_incipit: Saturday before Meatfare Sunday. The Dismissal
units.slavonic_text: Saturday before Meatfare Sunday. The Dismissal follows. 45.    On Saturday at Matins, after the Midnight service, the Trisagion, "With the depth of wisdom" and the Exapsalmos; then "Alleluia" with its verses and the Apolytikia, as prescribed on the Saturday before Meatfare Sunday; the Psalter, the Kathismata and the Amomos, and the names [of the Reposed] are commemorated as yesterday at Vespers; the Evlogitaria, and after the Exclamation, {the Kathisma} "Grant rest with the righteous, our Savior," {Glory,} Now and ever, "You Who have dawned from the Virgin." Then Psalm 50, and the Canon "The Master of all souls," with the prescribed verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma and the Theotokion. After the 6th Ode, the Kontakion, the Ikos, the Minologion, and the Postscript of the Triodion; then the Irmos of the 8th Ode "Be astonished and tremble, O Heaven," "More honorable," the Irmos "Every tongue is at a loss" and the 2 Exapostilaria. At the Praises: the 4 Stichira "Dreaded is the last moment before death's coming," Glory, "[Every man] withers like a flower," Now and ever, "You are our God," the "To You belongs glory" (read), the Synapti, and the 4 Aposticha "Since You have an inconceivable compassion," Glory, "A pain to Adam," Now and ever, "You have been seen as a dwelling place" then "It is good to confess"; the Trisagion, the two Hymns "With the depth of wisdom" and "You do we have as a rampart [and haven.]" 46.    In the Liturgy, the Antiphons, "It is good to confess." After the Entrance, the Apolytikion "With the depth of wisdom" and that of the Saint of the Church, the Kontakion "With the Saints grant rest" (see the 6th Ode of the Canon of Vespers). Apostolos of the Reposed and Gospel of the day. At "Especially," "It is meet," Communion Hymn "Blessed are they whom You have chosen." Instead of "We have seen the [true] light," we chant "With the depth of wisdom providing for all with Love of mankind" 14 then the "With the spirits of the righteous," and the names of all the deceased pious and Orthodox Christians from time immemorial are com- memorated etc., and Dismissal.
units.english_text: 46.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons: **"It is good to give praise unto the Lord..."** (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι*). After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας*), that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion: **"With the Saints grant rest, O Christ..."** (*Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον*) (see the 6th Ode of the Vespers Canon). The Epistle of the Reposed (1 Thessalonians 4:13–17) and Gospel of the day (John 21:15–25). At "Especially", **"It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*). Communion Hymn: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord; and their memorial is unto generation and generation. Alleluia!"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω*, Ps. 64:4 LXX). In place of **"We have seen the true Light..."** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), we chant the Dismissal Troparion: **"O Thou Who with the depth of wisdom providing for all with love of mankind..."** (*Ὁ βάθει σοφίας φιλανθρώπως πάντα οἰκονομῶν*) [Note 14]; then we chant **"With the spirits of the righteous departed..."** (*Μετὰ πνευμάτων δικαίων*), and the names of all the deceased pious and Orthodox Christians from time immemorial are commemorated, etc., and Dismissal.

units.english_text: 47.    In Great Vespers on Saturday evening, following the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX), we do not chant the Psalter [Translator's Note: The Pentekostarion prescribes the First Kathisma of the Psalter: "Blessed is the man", Pss. 1–3 LXX]. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we set ten verses and chant the three Idiomela of Tone 1: **"We celebrate Pentecost and the coming of the Spirit..."** (*Πεντηκοστὴν ἑορτάζομεν*) to five...[^479]

units.english_text: 48.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν ἡ Λιτή, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ γ΄ Καθίσματα ἐκ β΄, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τὸ α΄ Ἀντίφωνον τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Τὸ Πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν ὁδηγήσει με ἐν γῇ εὐθείᾳ, τὸ Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον Οὔσης ὀψίας μέχρι τοῦ Ἄν τινων κρατῆτε κεκράτηνται· Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ οὐ λέγομεν, ἀλλ᾽ εὐθὺς τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμὸν χῦμα, Δόξα, Ταῖς τῶν Ἀποστόλων, Καὶ νῦν, Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου, ὁ Στίχος Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός, καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι ἄνευ Στίχων· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, τὸ Κάθισμα ἅπαξ, ἀφ᾽ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον· ὁ Οἶκος, τὸ Μηνολόγιον, καὶ τὸ Ὑπόμνημα τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, αἱ Καταβασίαι διπλαῖ· εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδή, τὸ α΄ Ἐξαποστειλάριον δίς, καὶ τὸ β΄ ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα Παράδοξα σήμερον εἰς δ΄ (Τὸ Πεντηκοστάριον ὑποδεικνύει ὅτι ἕκαστον Ἰδιόμελον ἐπαναλαμβάνεται) Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε Δοξολογία Μ. καὶ τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον.

units.slavonic_text: Ἀντίφωνον Α΄ Οἱ οὐρανοὶ διηγοῦνται δόξαν Θεοῦ, ποίησιν δὲ χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ἀναγγέλλει τὸ στερέωμα. | Ταῖς | πρεσβείαις | τῆς | Θεοτόκου... units.english_text: 48.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50, the Liti, then the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..."**, and the Six Psalms. At **"God is the Lord"** (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion (three times); then the Psalter and the Polyeleos; the three Kathismata twice each; the Anavathmoi: the first Antiphon of Tone 4 (**"From my youth many passions war against me..."**), and the Prokimenon: **"Thy good Spirit shall lead me in the land of uprightness!"** (*Τὸ Πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν ὁδηγήσει με ἐν γῇ εὐθείᾳ*, Ps. 142:10 LXX), **"Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord!"** (*Πᾶσα πνοὴ*), and the Matins Gospel: **"When it was evening on that day..."** (*Οὔσης ὀψίας*) until **"whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained"** (John 20:19–23). We do not recite **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*), but read immediately Psalm 50 recited plainly. "Glory...": **"Through the intercessions of the Apostles..."** (*Ταῖς τῶν Ἀποστόλων*); "Both now and ever...": **"Through the intercessions of the Theotokos..."** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*); the Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy..."** (*Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός*), and the Idiomelon in Tone 6: **"O Heavenly King, Comforter, Spirit of truth, Who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and dwell in us, and cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One!"** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*). Both Canons without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the Kathisma (once); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"When the Most High came down and confused the tongues, He divided the nations; but when He distributed the tongues of fire, He called all to unity; and with one voice we glorify the All-holy Spirit!"** (*Ὅτε καταβὰς τὰς γλώσσας συνέχεε*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of Pentecost. The Katavasias of both Canons [double] (both the Iambic and Heirmologic Katavasias); then the 9th Ode is chanted. The first Exaposteilarion: **"O All-holy Spirit, Light proceeding from the Father, through the Son Thou didst come unto the unlettered Disciples..."** (*Φῶς ὁ Πατήρ, φῶς ὁ Λόγος, φῶς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα*) (twice), and the second: **"Our Light and Life is the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit..."** (*Τριαδικὸν*) (once). At the Praises: the three Idiomela: **"Marvelous things today have all the nations seen..."** (*Παράδοξα σήμερον*) to four, repeating the first hymn [Translator's Note: The Pentekostarion indicates that each Idiomelon is repeated]; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: **"O Heavenly King, Comforter..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε*). The Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..."**.

units.slavonic_text: ANTIPHON ONE The heavens are telling the glory of God; and the firmament proclaims his handiwork. Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night declares knowledge. There is no speech, nor are there words; their voice is not heard. Yet their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. | Through the | intercessions | of the | Theotokos...

units.slavonic_text: Ἀντίφωνον Γ΄ Κύριε ἐν τῇ δυνάμει σου εὐφρανθήσεται ὁ Βασιλεύς καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ σωτηρίῳ σου ἀγαλλιάσεται σφόδρα. | Εὐλογητὸς | εἶ, Χριστὲ | ὁ Θεὸς | ἡμῶν... Ὅτι προέφθασας αὐτὸν ἐν εὐλογίαις χρηστότητος, ἔθηκας ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ στέφανον ἐκ λίθου τιμίου. [Ζωὴν ᾐτήσατό σε, καὶ ἔδωκας αὐτῷ μακρότητα ἡμερῶν εἰς αἰῶνας αἰῶνος.]*

units.english_text: The Entrance Hymn: **"Be Thou exalted, O Lord, in Thy strength; we will sing and praise Thy mighty acts! Save us, O Good Paraclete, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Ὑψώθητι Κύριε ἐν τῇ δυνάμει σου, ᾄσομεν καὶ ψαλοῦμεν τὰς δυναστείας σου· Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Παράκλητε ἀγαθέ, τοὺς ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα*, Ps. 20:13 LXX). After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Kontakion in Tone 8: **"When the Most High came down and confused the tongues, He divided the nations; but when He distributed the tongues of fire, He called all to unity; and with one voice we glorify the All-holy Spirit!"** (*Ὅτε καταβὰς τὰς γλώσσας συνέχεε*). Instead of the Trisagion Hymn, we chant: **"As many as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia!"** (*Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε*). The Epistle (Acts 2:1–11) and the Gospel (John 7:37–52; 8:12) of the Feast. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: the Ninth Heirmos of the Iambic Canon in Tone 4: **"Without experiencing corruption didst thou conceive, and didst lend flesh unto the Word, the Artificer of all, O Mother unwedded, Virgin Theotokos, vessel of the Uncontainable, dwelling-place of thine Infinite Creator: thee do we magnify!"** (*Μὴ τῆς φθορᾶς διαπείρᾳ κυοφορήσασα*)...[^481]

units.english_text: 50.    Ἐν τῷ Μ. units.english_text: Communion Hymn: **"Thy good Spirit shall lead me in the land of uprightness. Alleluia!"** (*Τὸ Πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν ὁδηγήσει με ἐν γῇ εὐθείᾳ*, Ps. 142:10 LXX) [Note 15]. At "With the fear of God...", we chant the Dismissal Troparion: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*); then **"Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages"** (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and the Dismissal as indicated at Vespers [Note 16].
