units.english_text: When everything else needed is ready, the Bishop gives the blessing: **"Blessed is our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and at once Psalm 142 [LXX] is recited: **"O Lord, hear my prayer..."** (*Κύριε, εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου*), followed by the Small Litany intoned by the Deacon: **"Again and again in peace let us pray unto the Lord"** (*Ἔτι καὶ ἔτι ἐν εἰρήνῃ τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*). The Bishop then exclaims: **"For holy art Thou, our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Ὅτι Ἅγιος εἶ, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*). Then the Deacon: **"Let us pray to the Lord"** (*Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*); then the Bishop recites the Prayer and intones: **"Peace be unto all"** (*Εἰρήνη πᾶσι*). The Deacon: **"Let us bow our heads unto the Lord"** (*Τὰς κεφαλὰς ἡμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ κλίνωμεν*); the Bishop recites the Prayer in a low voice [*μυστικῶς*] and pronounces the Exclamation: **"Blessed and glorified be the majesty of Thy kingdom, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος τῆς βασιλείας σου...*).†

There are also 4 more columns supporting the Holy Table at each corner. They symbolize the Four Evangelists, while the central supporting column symbolizes Christ.] 2. If the Service is not conducted in the new Church, but in another already consecrated Church, at this time the Bishop vested in his Archieratical vestments (as well as all the Clergy in their vestments) carries upon his head the Holy Relics and transfers them in a procession to the new Church, where after the customary circling of the new Church, he enters it to celebrate the Consecration and following that the Liturgy; it is prescribed that the Liturgy be celebrated in that [the new] Church.
units.english_text: After this Exclamation, the Bishop lifts the Diskarion [Paten] on which are the Holy Relics onto his head and, preceded by the Priests with the Holy Gospel Books, the Cross, the Ripidia (*Exapteryga*, six-winged fans) and the Candles, with the Chanters chanting the Troparia: **"O Holy Martyrs, who have fought the good fight and received your crowns..."** (*Ἅγιοι Μάρτυρες οἱ καλῶς ἀθλήσαντες*), and **"Glory to Thee, O Christ God, the Apostles' boast, the Martyrs' joy..."** (*Δόξα σοι, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός*), he leaves the church (as do all the people) and goes in solemn procession around it, while the Idiomela are chanted: **"Be renewed, be renewed, O new Jerusalem..."** (*Ἐγκαινίζου, ἐγκαινίζου, ἡ νέα Ἱερουσαλήμ*), and **"Of old when renewing the temple of testimony..."** (*Πάλαι μὲν ἐγκαινίζων τὸν τῆς σκηνῆς ναόν*)...[^501]

units.english_text: Ἐγκαίνια τιμᾶσθαι· Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν κόλπων τῶν πατρικῶν. Φθάσας δὲ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν μεγάλων πυλῶν τοῦ Ναοῦ, τίθησι τὰ ἱερὰ Λείψανα ἐπὶ τετραποδίου, καὶ ὁ μὲν Διάκονος ἀναγινώσκει τὸν Ἀπόστολον, ὁ δὲ Ἀρχιερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ τοῦτο αὖθις λιτανεύει περὶ τὸν Ναὸν ψαλλομένης τῆς γ΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Ἐγκαινίων, καὶ ἀφοῦ φθάσῃ αὖθις πρὸ τῶν Πυλῶν, ἀναγινώσκεται Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον ὡς ἀνωτέρω· καὶ τρίτον λιτανεύει περὶ τὸν Ναὸν ψαλλομένης τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος· ἐλθὼν δὲ τελευταῖον πρὸ τῶν Πυλῶν τοῦ Ναοῦ ἐκφωνεῖ Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, Ἀμήν, καὶ ψάλλεται τὸ Τροπάριον Ὁ ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ τῆς πίστεως· τούτου ψαλλομένου, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς τίθησι τὰ ἱερὰ Λείψανα ἐπὶ τοῦ Τετραποδίου καὶ ἐπεύχεται τὴν Εὐχὴν Ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατήρ, εἶτα καὶ τὴν τῆς Εἰσόδου Εὐχήν.

units.english_text: Τῶν δὲ Πυλῶν τοῦ Ναοῦ κεκλεισμένων οὐσῶν, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς ἐκφωνεῖ, Ἄρατε πύλας οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν καὶ ἐπάρθητε πύλαι αἰώνιοι, καὶ εἰσελεύσεται ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης· ἔνδοθεν δὲ τοῦ Ναοῦ ἱστάμενός τις ἀντιφωνεῖ Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης; ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς Κύριος κραταιὸς καὶ δυνατός, Κύριος δυνατὸς ἐν πολέμῳ· καὶ ταῦτα λέγονται ἐκ τρίτου. Μετὰ ταῦτα σφραγίσας τρὶς τὰς πύλας μετὰ τῶν ἱερῶν Λειψάνων σταυροειδῶς, καὶ τούτων ἀνοιγομένων, εἰσέρχεται ἐν τῷ Ναῷ μετὰ τοῦ Κλήρου καὶ σὺν αὐτοῖς πᾶς ὁ λαός, ψαλλομένου τοῦ Ἀπολυτικίου τῶν Ἐγκαινίων Ὡς τοῦ ἄνω στερεώματος τὴν εὐπρέπειαν.

units.slavonic_incipit: Ἐγκαινία τιμᾶσθαι· Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ
units.slavonic_text: Ἐγκαινία τιμᾶσθαι· Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν κόλπων τῶν πατρικῶν. Φθάσας δὲ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν μεγάλων πυλῶν τοῦ Ναοῦ, τίθησι τὰ ἱερὰ Λείψανα ἐπὶ τετραποδίου, καὶ ὁ μὲν Διάκονος ἀναγινώσκει τὸν Ἀπόστολον, ὁ δὲ Ἀρχιερεὺς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον· μετὰ τοῦτο αὖθις λιτανεύει περὶ τὸν Ναὸν ψαλλομένης τῆς γ΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῶν Ἐγκαινίων, καὶ ἀφοῦ φθάσῃ αὖθις πρὸ τῶν Πυλῶν, ἀναγινώσκεται Ἀπόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον ὡς ἀνωτέρω· καὶ τρίτον λιτανεύει περὶ τὸν Ναὸν ψαλλομένης τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος· ἐλθὼν δὲ τελευταῖον πρὸ τῶν Πυλῶν τοῦ Ναοῦ ἐκφωνεῖ Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, Ἀμήν, καὶ ψάλλεται τὸ Τροπάριον Ὁ ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ τῆς πίστεως· τούτου ψαλλομένου, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς τίθησι τὰ ἱερὰ Λείψανα ἐπὶ τοῦ Τετραποδίου καὶ ἐπεύχεται τὴν Εὐχὴν Ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατήρ, εἶτα καὶ τὴν τῆς Εἰσόδου Εὐχήν. Τῶν δὲ Πυλῶν τοῦ Ναοῦ κεκλεισμένων οὐσῶν, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς ἐκφωνεῖ, Ἄρατε πύλας οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν καὶ ἐπάρθητε πύλαι αἰώνιοι, καὶ εἰσελεύσεται ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης· ἔνδοθεν δὲ τοῦ Ναοῦ ἱστάμενός τις ἀντιφωνεῖ Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης; ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς Κύριος κραταιὸς καὶ δυνατός, Κύριος δυνατὸς ἐν πολέμῳ· καὶ ταῦτα λέγονται ἐκ τρίτου. Μετὰ ταῦτα σφραγίσας τρὶς τὰς πύλας μετὰ τῶν ἱερῶν Λειψάνων σταυροειδῶς, καὶ τούτων ἀνοιγομένων, εἰσέρχεται ἐν τῷ Ναῷ μετὰ τοῦ Κλήρου καὶ σὺν αὐτοῖς πᾶς ὁ λαός, ψαλλομένου τοῦ Ἀπολυτικίου τῶν Ἐγκαινίων Ὡς τοῦ ἄνω στερεώματος τὴν εὐπρέπειαν. Εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν Βῆμα ἀποτίθησι τὰ ἅγια Λείψανα εἰς τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην αὐτοῖς ἀργυρᾶν θήκην, καὶ ἐπιχύσας τούτοις ἅγιον Μύρον, ἀσφαλίζει ταῦτα μετ’ ἐπιμελείας καὶ προσοχῆς μεγίστης, ἐκφωνῶν ἐκ γ΄ τὸ Αἰωνία ἡ μνήμη τῶν κτιτόρων τοῦ ἁγίου Ναοῦ τούτου, τοῦ λαοῦ ἀντιφωνοῦντος Αἰωνία ἡ μνήμη. Καὶ ἀκολούθως [ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς] ἐπισυνάπτει τὰς δύο Εὐχάς, καὶ μετὰ τὸ Ἀμὴν εἰσφέρουσιν αὐτῷ θερμὴν τὴν Κηρομαστίχην, ἣν ἐκχέει ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ φυτοῦ καὶ συνεφαρμόζει τὰ χαρτία· εἶτα ἐπιλαβόντες οἱ παρατυχόντες τῆς ἁγίας Τραπέζης, τιθέασι ταύτην ἐπὶ τοῦ Κίονος, καὶ τούτων γιγνομένων οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλουσιν εἰς ἦχον β΄ τὸν 144 Ψαλμὸν Ὑψώσω σε ὁ Θεός μου, καὶ ξενομένης τῆς

units.english_text: ...**"For the Consecration is to be honored..."** (*Ἐγκαίνια τιμᾶσθαι*); **"Glory..."** (*Δόξα*), **"Now and forever..."** (*Καὶ νῦν*), **"He Who rests in the Father's bosom..."** (*Ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν κόλπων τῶν πατρικῶν*) are chanted. When the Bishop arrives in front of the main western doors of the church, he deposits the Holy Relics upon the Tetrapod; the Deacon proclaims the Apostolos, and then the Bishop proclaims the Holy Gospel. After this, the Bishop proceeds again in procession around the church, while the Third Ode of the Canon of the Consecration is chanted. When he has again reached the main doors, the Apostolos and Gospel are proclaimed as described above. He proceeds in procession for a third time around the church, while the Sixth Ode of the Canon is chanted. When he comes before the main doors for the final time, he exclaims: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God, unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς εἶ, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, Ἀμήν*), and the Troparion is sung: **"Thou Who on the rock of faith hast established Thy Church..."** (*Ὁ ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ τῆς πίστεως*). As this is sung, the Bishop places the Holy Relics upon the Tetrapod in front of the main doors and recites the Prayer: **"O God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ..."** (*Ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατήρ*), followed by the Prayer of the Entrance.

units.english_text: With the doors of the church shut, the Bishop exclaims: **"Lift up your gates, ye princes; and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter in!"** (*Ἄρατε πύλας, οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν, καὶ ἐπάρθητε, πύλαι αἰώνιοι, καὶ εἰσελεύσεται ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης*, Ps. 23:7 LXX). From inside the church, someone standing there responds: **"Who is this King of glory?"** (*Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης;*). The Bishop replies: **"The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle!"** (*Κύριος κραταιὸς καὶ δυνατός, Κύριος δυνατὸς ἐν πολέμῳ*, Ps. 23:8 LXX). The foregoing questions and answers are repeated three times. After this, the Bishop, taking the Diskarion [Paten] with the Holy Relics, signs the doors three times in the form of a Cross. When the doors have been opened, the Bishop enters the church with the Clergy and all the people with them, while the Dismissal Troparion of the Consecration is chanted in Tone 4: **"As the splendor of the firmament on high, Thou hast revealed the beauty of the holy dwelling of Thy glory here below, O Lord: establish it unto the ages of ages, and accept our supplications unceasingly offered therein through the Theotokos, O Life and Resurrection of all!"** (*Ὡς τοῦ ἄνω στερεώματος τὴν εὐπρέπειαν...*).

units.slavonic_text: "For Consecration is to be honored," Glory, Now and ever, "He who rests on the parental breast" are chanted. When the Bishop has arrived in front of the main doors of the Church, he puts the Holy Relics on a four-legged table; the Deacon reads the Apostolos, then the Bishop reads the Gospel. After this, the Bishop goes again in procession around the Church, while the 3rd Ode of the Canon of the Consecration is chanted. When he has again reached the main doors, the Apostolos and Gospel are read as described above. He goes in procession for a third time around the Church, while the 6th Ode of the Canon is chanted. When he comes to the main doors for the final time, he exclaims "Blessed are You, Christ our God, to the ages of ages. Amen," and the Troparion "You Who on the rock of faith" is sung. As this is sung, the Bishop puts the Holy Relics on the four-legged table [in front of the main doors] and says the Prayer "God and Father," followed by the Prayer of the Entrance. With the doors of the Church shut, the Bishop exclaims "Lift up your gates, you rulers; and be lifted up, you eternal gates, and the King of glory will enter." From inside the Church, some one standing there asks in a challenging manner "Who is this King of glory?" The Bishop replies "The Lord mighty and powerful, the Lord powerful in war." The foregoing questions and answers are repeated three times. After this, the Bishop [raises the Paten with the Holy Relics on it] and with them makes the sign of the Cross on the doors three times. When the doors have been opened, the Bishop enters the Church with the Clergy and all the people with them, while the Apolytikion of the Consecration "As the splendor of the firma- ment above" is chanted. Having entered the Sanctuary, the Bishop places the Holy Relics in the silver case that has been prepared for them and, when he has poured Holy Myron [Myrrh] on them, he makes them secure with the greatest care and attention, while exclaiming three times "Eternal be the memory of the Founders of this holy House." The people respond with "Eternal be the memory." Note: For the sake of greater clarity, the following paragraph is a free translation of Violakis' original text, adding also some information mainly of the Mega Efchologion, pp. 291-325. Then, the Bishop adds the two Prayers "Lord, our God" and "Lord God, our Savior." After the final "Amen," the Bishop places the silver case containing the Holy Relics into the opening in the middle of the central Column, the "plant" [wherein some of the faithful have put slips of paper with the names of their departed ones]. The people respond each time: **"Eternal be the memory!"** (*Αἰωνία ἡ μνήμη*).

units.english_text: Εἶτα ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς ἐκφωνεῖ Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεός, καὶ εὐθὺς φέρεται τὸ σάββανον καὶ περιτίθεται ἐπὶ τὸν Ἀρχιερέα ἐπάνω τῶν ἀρχιερατικῶν αὐτοῦ ἀμφίων ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν ἐπὶ τῷ μὴ φαίνεσθαι τὰ ἀρχιερατικὰ αὐτοῦ ἄμφια καὶ δεσμοῦνται μετὰ ζώνης, περιτυλίσσονται δὲ καὶ οἱ δύο αὐτοῦ βραχίονες μετὰ δύο καινῶν μανδηλίων δεσμουμένων καὶ αὐτῶν ὑπὸ ζώνης, καὶ οὕτω περιβληθέντος τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως, τίθεται ἐπεύχιον ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἁγίων Θυρῶν, καὶ τοῦ Διακόνου εἰπόντος Ἔτι καὶ ἔτι κλίναντες τὰ γόνατα, τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς κλίνας τὰ γόνατα λέγει τὴν Εὐχὴν Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἄναρχος, εἶτα ὁ Διάκονος Ἀντιλαβοῦ, σῶσον, ἐλέησον, ἀνάστησον καὶ διαφύλαξον ἡμᾶς, ἐπισυνάπτων καὶ τὴν μεγάλην Συναπτὴν Ἐν εἰρήνῃ τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν. Μετὰ τὴν ἐκφώνησιν, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς ἔρχεται ἔμπροσθεν τῆς ἁγίας Τραπέζης, καὶ λαβὼν τὰ Νίτρα (ἢ μοσχοσάπωνα) σφραγίζει ταῦτα ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν μερῶν καὶ ῥίπτει αὐτὰ σταυροειδῶς ἐπὶ τῆς ἁγίας Τραπέζης, εἶτα φέρεται χλιαρὸν ὕδωρ, καὶ τοῦ Διακόνου εἰπόντος Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς κλίνας τὴν κεφαλήν, ἐπεύχεται τὸ ὕδωρ μυστικῶς, καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἐκφώνησιν ἐπιχέει αὐτὸ ἐπὶ τῆς Τραπέζης, λέγων Εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, Ἀμήν, καὶ διὰ τοῦ ἐκχυθέντος ὕδατος καὶ τῶν Νίτρων ἐκπλύνει τὴν ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν καὶ σπογγίζει αὐτὴν μετὰ καινῶν σπόγγων, τὸν δὲ Κίονα, ὡς μὴ δυνάμενος ταῖς χερσὶν ἐκπλῦναι, ἐκπλύνει καὶ σπογγίζει αὐτὸν μετὰ τοῦ σπόγγου· τούτων γιγνομένων, ψάλλεται ὁ 83 Ψαλμὸς Ὡς ἀγαπητὰ τὰ σκηνώματά σου, Κύριε· μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀπόπλυσιν καὶ ἀποσπόγγισιν, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς ἐκφωνεῖ Δόξα τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.

units.english_text: ...permanently, the Bishop pours into the cavity the hot wax-mastic (*κηρομαστίχη*) brought to him and adjusts the paper collar around the rim of the opening. Then, the assisting clergy place the marble slab [mensa] on top of the Column, covering the entire Holy Table or securing the central pillar. While the deposition and sealing of the Holy Relics in the central Column takes place, the Choirs chant Psalm 144 [LXX] in Tone 2: **"I will exalt Thee, my God, my King, and I will bless Thy name forever, and unto the ages of ages..."** (*Ὑψώσω σε, ὁ Θεός μου, ὁ Βασιλεύς μου*). While the spilled wax-mastic is scraped away and the stone slab is cleansed, Psalm 22 [LXX] is chanted: **"The Lord is my shepherd, and I shall not want..."** (*Κύριος ποιμαίνει με καὶ οὐδέν με ὑστερήσει*).

units.english_text: Then, the Bishop exclaims: **"Blessed is our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and at once the Savvanon (*σάββανον*), a white linen apron-vestment, is brought to him. The Bishop is vested in it over his sacred archieratical vestments and it is bound with a belt, both in front and behind, so that his vestments are completely covered and protected; his two forearms are likewise wrapped in two new white towels [mandylia], which are also bound with the belt. When the Bishop is thus invested, a prayer mat [*ἐπεύχιον*] is placed before the Royal Doors [Holy Doors]. The Deacon intones: **"Again and again on bended knees, let us pray unto the Lord"** (*Ἔτι καὶ ἔτι κλίναντες τὰ γόνατα, τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*). The Bishop, kneeling down, recites the Prayer: **"O God without beginning and eternal, Who hast brought all things from non-existence into being..."** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἄναρχος καὶ ἀΐδιος*). Then the Deacon intones: **"Help us, save us, have mercy on us, raise us up, and protect us, O God, by Thy grace"** (*Ἀντιλαβοῦ, σῶσον, ἐλέησον...*), to which he appends the Great Litany: **"In peace let us pray unto the Lord"** (*Ἐν εἰρήνῃ τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*). After the Exclamation of this Litany, the Bishop approaches the front of the Holy Table and takes the cakes of scented soap [*νίτρα ἢ μοσχοσάπωνα*]; having signed them with the sign of the Cross on both sides, he lays them upon the Holy Table in cruciform arrangement. Then, lukewarm water is brought forward; the Deacon intones: **"Let us pray to the Lord"** (*Τοῦ Κυρίου δεηθῶμεν*); the Bishop bows his head and blesses the water in secret prayer [*μυστικῶς*]. After the Exclamation, he pours the water over the Holy Table, saying: **"In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen."** (*Εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, Ἀμήν*). With the water poured forth and the cakes of soap, he washes the Holy Table and wipes it with new natural sponges. Because the Column cannot be washed by hands alone, he cleanses and dries it with the sponge. While this sacred ablution is being performed, Psalm 83 [LXX] is chanted: **"How lovely are Thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! My soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord..."** (*Ὡς ἀγαπητὰ τὰ σκηνώματά σου, Κύριε τῶν δυνάμεων*). After the washing and sponging are completed, the Bishop exclaims: **"Glory to our God unto the ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας*)...[^503]

units.slavonic_incipit: permanently, the Bishop pours into the
units.slavonic_text: permanently, the Bishop pours into the opening the hot wax-mastic brought to him and rearranges the papers around the rim of the opening. Then, those assisting the Bishop put a plate or slab on top of the opening, covering the entire Holy Table or merely the opening. While the placement and sealing of the Holy Relics in the central Column is being done, the Choirs chant Psalm 144 "I will exalt You, my God" in Mode II. While the wax-mastic that may have been spilled is being scraped up and the place on which it ran is being cleaned, Psalm 22 "The Lord is my shepherd" is chanted. Then, the Bishop exclaims "Blessed is our God" and at once the Savvanon, a thin white sheet-like garment, is brought to him. The Bishop is dressed in it over his hieratical vestments and tied with a belt, both in front and behind, so that the vestments are not visible, and his two arms are wrapped in two new cloths, which are also tied with a belt. When the Bishop has been so dressed, a prayer mat [or pillow] is placed in front of the Holy Gates and, when the Deacon has said "Again and again on bended knees let us pray to the Lord," the Bishop kneels and says the Prayer "God without beginning." Then the Deacon says "Help us, save us, have mercy on us, raise us up and keep us," to which he adds the Great Litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord." After the Exclamation [of this Litany], the Bishop goes in front of the Holy Table and takes the pieces of scented soap and, having made the sign of the Cross on them on both sides, puts them on the Holy Table in the form of a Cross. Then, lukewarm water is brought, and, when the Deacon has said "Let us pray to the Lord," the Bishop bows his head and prays in a low voice over the water. After the Exclamation, he pours the water over the Holy Table saying "In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Amen." With the water that has been poured and the pieces of soap he washes the Holy Table and sponges it with new sponges. Since he cannot wash the Column with his hands, he washes and dries it with the sponge. While this is going on, Psalm 83 "How lovely Your dwelling, Lord" is chanted. After the washing and the sponging, the Bishop exclaims "Glory to our God unto the ages."

units.english_text: Καὶ λαβὼν Βικίον (Κανίον) ῥοδοστάγμου ἐπιχύσας [ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς] πλύνει τὴν ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν καὶ σπογγίζει μετὰ τῶν Ἀντιμηνσίων, καὶ τούτων γιγνομένων ψάλλεται εἰς ἦχον βαρὺν τὸ Ῥαντιεῖς με ὑσσώπῳ καὶ καθαρισθήσομαι, πλυνεῖς με καὶ ὑπὲρ χιόνα λευκανθήσομαι, εἶτα αὖθις δοξάζει λέγων Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πάντοτε νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ λαβὼν τὸ δοχεῖον τοῦ ἁγίου Μύρου, τοῦ Διακόνου λέγοντος Πρόσχωμεν, ἐπιχέει Μύρον τῇ ἁγίᾳ Τραπέζῃ, ψάλλων τρὶς τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα, ὥσπερ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Βαπτίσματος, καὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ ποιεῖ Σταυροὺς τρεῖς, μέσον ἕνα καὶ δύο ἑκατέρωθεν, καὶ ἀλείφει τῇ χειρὶ διὰ τῶν τριῶν ἐκείνων Σταυρῶν πᾶσαν τὴν ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν σπογγίζων αὐτὴν δι’ Ἀντιμηνσίων· τὸ αὐτὸ ποιεῖ καὶ εἰς τὸν Κίονα τῆς Τραπέζης· τούτων τελουμένων, ψάλλεται ὁ 132 Ψαλμὸς Ἰδοὺ δὴ τί καλόν, ἢ τί τερπνόν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα αὖθις ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς ἐκφωνεῖ Δόξα τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ τὸ Δόξα σοι, ἁγία Τριὰς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· εἶτα ἐφαρμόζει ἐπὶ τῶν τεσσάρων γωνιῶν τῆς Τραπέζης τὰ τέσσαρα ὑφάσματα ἀπεικονισμένους ἔχοντα τοὺς τέσσαρας Εὐαγγελιστάς, ἢ μόνα τὰ ὀνόματα αὐτῶν, προσκολλῶν αὐτὰ διὰ Κηρομαστίχης.

units.english_text: Then, having taken a flagon [*βικίον ἢ κανίον*] of rosewater, the Bishop pours it upon the Holy Table, washes it, and sponges it with the Antimensia.* While this is being done, there is chanted in Tone 7 (Grave Tone): **"Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow"** (*Ῥαντιεῖς με ὑσσώπῳ καὶ καθαρισθήσομαι, πλυνεῖς με καὶ ὑπὲρ χιόνα λευκανθήσομαι*, Ps. 50:9 LXX). Then the Bishop again gives glory, saying: **"Blessed is our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*). Having taken the vessel of Holy Myron, when the Deacon has intoned: **"Let us attend!"** (*Πρόσχωμεν*), the Bishop pours it onto the Holy Table, chanting three times, as at Holy Baptism: **"Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia!"** (*Ἀλληλούϊα*), and makes three Crosses with it, one in the middle and two on either side. With his hands he anoints the entire Holy Table spreading the Myron through these three Crosses, sponging it with the Antimensia. He does the same to the central Column of the Table. While this is being done, Psalm 132 [LXX] is chanted: **"Behold now, what is so good or so pleasant as for brethren to dwell together in unity..."** (*Ἰδοὺ δὴ τί καλόν, ἢ τί τερπνόν*), after which the Bishop again exclaims: **"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen"**; and **"Glory to Thee, O Holy Trinity our God, glory to Thee unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα σοι, ἁγία Τριὰς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων*). Then he secures at the four corners of the Table the four pieces of linen which have imprinted upon them the icons of the Four Evangelists (or their names alone), affixing them firmly with wax-mastic.

units.english_text: After this, the Bishop unfolds the Katasarkion (*κατασάρκιον*, the white linen winding-sheet vestment covering the bare surface of the altar) upon the Holy Table, and its binding cords are tied in the form of a Cross underneath the Holy Table around the Column. While this is being done, Psalm 131 [LXX] is chanted by both Choirs: **"Remember, O Lord, David, and all his meekness..."** (*Μνήσθητι, Κύριε, τοῦ Δαβίδ*), after which the Bishop exclaims again: **"Glory to God unto the ages. Amen."** (*Δόξα τῷ Θεῷ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, Ἀμήν*). Then he washes his hands in a new vessel, or in the sacrarium [*χωνευτήριον*], so that not a single drop may fall outside it [the consecrated water draining directly into the earth]. He dries his hands with a new towel; then he takes the outer vestment of the Holy Table (the Ependytes or Indytion [*ἐπενδύτης ἤτοι τὸ ἐφάπλωμα*]) and spreads it over the Table, while Psalm 92 [LXX] is chanted: **"The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty; the Lord is robed, He hath girded Himself with strength..."** (*Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν, εὐπρέπειαν ἐνεδύσατο*). units.slavonic_text: Then, having taken a wine-jar [container] of rose-water, he [the Bishop] pours it on and washes the Holy Table and sponges it with the Antiminsia.[**] While this is being done, there is chanted in Mode Varys "You will sprinkle me with hyssop and I shall be cleansed; You will wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow." Then the Bishop again gives glory, saying "Blessed is our God, always now and for ever, and to the ages of ages." Having taken the vessel of Holy Myron [Myrrh], when the Deacon has said "Let us attend," the Bishop pours it onto the Holy Table, chanting three times, as at a Baptism, "Alleluia!" and makes three Crosses with it, one in the middle and two on either side. With his hand he anoints the entire Holy Table with these three Crosses, sponging it with the Antiminsia. He does the same to the [central] Column of the Table. While this is being done, Psalm 132 "Behold, how good and pleasant it is" is chanted, after which the Bishop again exclaims "Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. And now and ever, and to the ages of ages. Amen"; and "Glory to You, Holy Trinity, our God, glory to You unto the ages of ages. Amen." Then he arranges on the four corners of the Table the four pieces of cloth which have imprinted on them the icons of the four Evangelists, or simply their names, gluing them with wax-mastic. units.english_text: * *Note on the Consecration of Antimensia:* Antimension (pl. *Antimensia*): A consecrated linen cloth depicting the Deposition / Burial of Our Lord Jesus Christ (the *Plashchanytsia*), containing sewn relics of martyrs. It is unfolded upon the Holy Table before the Liturgy of the Faithful; without a consecrated Antimension, no Divine Liturgy may be celebrated. In this rite, the Bishop sponges the Holy Table with several Antimensia during the washing and chrismation with Holy Myron, thereby consecrating them simultaneously and providing authenticated Antimensia for the altars of other new churches.

Εἶτα ὁ Διάκονος ἐκφωνεῖ Ἐν εἰρήνῃ προέλθωμεν, καὶ ἀναγινώσκεται ὁ Ἀπόστολος παρὰ τοῦ Διακόνου, τὸ δὲ Εὐαγγέλιον ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως· μετὰ ταῦτα κομίζεται τῷ Ἀρχιερεῖ κανδήλα καινὴ καὶ θρυαλλὶς (φυτρί) καὶ ἔλαιον, αὐτὸς δὲ ἰδίαις χερσὶν ἀνάπτει τὴν θρυαλλίδα [ψάλλων συγχρόνως τὸν πρῶτον στίχον τῆς Δοξολογίας, τρίς, εἰς ἦχον Α΄] καὶ ἀποτίθησι τὴν κανδήλαν [****] ἐπὶ τοῦ ἁγίου θυσιαστηρίου. [*****] Εἶτα δὲ ἀποτιθέμενος τό τε σάββανον, τὰ μανδήλια καὶ τὴν ζώνην (ἅτινα διανέμονται τῷ λαῷ), ἐπιτρέπει τοῖς ἐκκλησιαστικοῖς ὑπηρέταις ἀνάψαι τὰς κανδήλας τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ τοὺς κηρούς, ψαλλομένου συγχρόνως τοῦ Δοξαστικοῦ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Καὶ νῦν Τὴν μνήμην τῶν Ἐγκαινίων ἐπιτελοῦντες Κύριε· εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ καὶ τῶν Ἐγκαινίων Ὡς τοῦ ἄνω στερεώματος, ἡ Ἐκτενής, παρὰ τοῦ Διακόνου Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινήν,[******] ἡ Ἐκφώνησις παρὰ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως Ὅτι ἐλεήμων καὶ φιλάνθρωπος, καὶ ἡ Ἀπόλυσις παρὰ τοῦ Ἀρχιερέως·

units.english_text: ...and upon that, the Holy Gospel Book; then, he places in its proper place the sacred Artophorion [Tabernacle].* Then takes place the kissing of the Holy Gospel Book. After the kissing of the Gospel, the Bishop takes the censer and censes the Holy Table, the clergy, and the whole church. While the church is being censed, the Choirs chant Psalm 25 [LXX]: **"Judge me, O Lord"** (*Κρῖνόν με, Κύριε*). While the Bishop is censing, one of the Priests follows him carrying the vessel of Holy Myron; upon each one of the pillars and arches, he traces the sign of the Cross with the Holy Myron, anointing them by means of a sponge soaked in Myron attached to the end of a reed. When the censing and anointing are finished, and at the same time the Psalm is completed, the Bishop gives glory in a loud voice, saying: **"Glory to the holy, all-powerful, and life-creating Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. units.english_text: The Bishop then takes off the white garment [the Savvanon], the cloths [mandylia], and the belt (all of which are distributed to the people as precious sanctified tokens), and permits the church's serving attendants to light the oil lamps and candles throughout the church. At the same time, the Doxastikon [Glory Sticheron] of the Patron Saint of the church is chanted, followed by **"Now and forever..."** (*Καὶ νῦν*): **"While celebrating the commemoration of the Consecration, O Lord, we glorify Thee, the Sanctifier of all!"** (*Τὴν μνήμην τῶν Ἐγκαινίων ἐπιτελοῦντες, Κύριε...*). Then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of the Patron Saint of the church, and that of the Consecration: **"As the splendor of the firmament on high..."** (*Ὡς τοῦ ἄνω στερεώματος τὴν εὐπρέπειαν*); the Litany by the Deacon: **"Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"** (*Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑωθινὴν δέησιν ἡμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ*);‡ the Exclamation by the Bishop: **"For Thou art a merciful God and lover of mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Ὅτι ἐλεήμων καὶ φιλάνθρωπος...*)...[^505]

units.slavonic_text: [Original Greek Text: Ceremony of the Accession of a Patriarch to the Ecumenical Throne (p. 882)]
units.english_text: Φθάσας ὁ Πατριάρχης μετὰ τῆς συνήθους ἐν παρατάξει συνοδίας αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ Πατριαρχεῖα, ἔρχεται ἔμπροσθεν τῆς μεγάλης πύλης τοῦ Ναοῦ ἔνθα ἵσταται ἅπας ὁ Κλῆρος πρὸς προϋπάντησιν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἅγιοι Ἀρχιερεῖς οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτὸν εἰσέρχονται κατ’ εὐθεῖαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν Βῆμα, τέσσαρες δὲ τῶν διακόνων ἐνδύονται τὰς ἱερὰς αὐτῶν στολάς· καὶ κρατοῦντες δικηροτρίκηρα οἱ μὲν δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν θυμιῶσι τὸν Πατριάρχην εἰσερχόμενον ἐν τῷ Ναῷ, οἱ δὲ δύο ἵστανται περὶ αὐτόν· προπορευομένου δὲ τοῦ Πριμικηρίου μὲ τὸ Διβάμβουλον, καὶ τῶν Χορῶν τῶν ψαλτῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, εἰσέρχεται ὁ Πατριάρχης εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν Βῆμα. Τότε ὁ πρῶτος τῇ τάξει Ἀρχιερεὺς φέρων Ἐπιτραχήλιον καὶ Ὠμοφόριον ποιεῖ Εὐλογητόν, ὁ Διάκονος λέγει τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς *Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*, μεθ’ ὃ οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς ψάλλουσι τὸ *Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν* καὶ τὸ *Ὅτε καταβάς*, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς κατὰ τὸ μέγα ἔλεός σου δεόμεθά σου ἐπάκουσον καὶ ἐλέησον*, οἱ Ἀρχιερεῖς τὸ *Κύριε ἐλέησον* τρίς, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τῶν εὐσεβῶν καὶ ὀρθοδόξων χριστιανῶν*, αὖθις τὸ *Κύριε ἐλέησον* τρίς, ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς *Ὅτι ἐλεήμων καὶ...*

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Ceremony of the Accession of a Patriarch to the Ecumenical Throne (p. 883)]
units.english_text: Arriving with his customary entourage in solemn cortège at the Patriarchate, the Patriarch comes before the great portal of the church* where all the clergy have assembled to receive him. The holy Hierarchs who accompany him enter directly into the Holy Sanctuary [Bema]; four of the deacons vest in their sacred vestments; holding the Dikerotrikera, two of them cense the Patriarch as he enters the church, while the other two stand beside him. Preceded by the Primikirios carrying the Divamboulon, and with the Choirs of Chanters singing **"It is truly meet to bless thee, O Theotokos..."** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the Patriarch enters into the Holy Sanctuary.

units.english_text: Then the senior Hierarch in precedence [by seniority of episcopal ordination], vested in Epitrachilion and Omophorion, intones the blessing: **"Blessed is our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*). The Deacon recites the Trisagion Prayers, and the Hierarch exclaims: **"For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία...*). After this, the Hierarchs chant the Dismissal Troparion of Pentecost: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God, Who hast revealed the fishermen to be all-wise, by sending down upon them the Holy Spirit, and through them catching the whole world in Thy net: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!"** (*Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*), and the Kontakion of Pentecost: **"When the Most High came down and confused the tongues, He divided the nations; but when He distributed the tongues of fire, He called all to unity: and with one voice we glorify the All-Holy Spirit!"** (*Ὅτε καταβὰς τὰς γλώσσας συνέχεε...*).†

units.english_text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ὁ Πατριάρχης ἐνδεδυμένος Μανδύαν, Ἐπιτραχήλιον καὶ Ὠμοφόριον ἵσταται ἐνώπιον τῆς ἁγίας Τραπέζης καὶ ποιεῖ Εὐλογητόν, εἶτα ἀναγινώσκει τὸ Τρισάγιον κτλ. ὡς ἀνωτέρω, καὶ γίνεται ἡ Ἀπόλυσις, μεθ’ ἣν ἱσταμένου τοῦ Πατριάρχου ἐν τῇ Ὡραίᾳ Πύλῃ, προσέρχεται ὁ μέγας Λογοθέτης, καὶ διὰ τῆς συνήθους προσφωνήσεως προσκαλεῖ αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Οἰκουμενικὸν Θρόνον, ὁ δὲ Πατριάρχης ποιεῖται τὴν εὐχαριστίαν, καὶ ἀκολούθως προσέρχεται αὐτῷ ὁ Μητροπολίτης Ἡρακλείας καὶ μετὰ τὴν συνήθη προσλαλιὰν ἐγχειρίζει αὐτῷ τὴν Πατριαρχικὴν ῥάβδον, ἀσπαζόμενος τὴν δεξιὰν αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὕτως ἡ Α.Θ.Π. ὁδηγουμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ Μεγάλου Λογοθέτου καὶ τῶν διακόνων ἀνέρχεται εἰς τὸν θρόνον καὶ εὐλογεῖ τὸν λαὸν μετὰ τοῦ τιμίου Σταυροῦ, τῶν χορῶν ψαλλόντων τὸ *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*· μετὰ τοῦτο ὁ Πρωτοψάλτης μετὰ τοῦ Χοροῦ αὐτοῦ ψάλλει τὸν Πατριαρχικὸν πολυχρονισμὸν *Πολυχρόνιον ποιήσαι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς τὸν παναγιώτατον καὶ σεβασμιώτατον ἡμῶν αὐθέντην καὶ Δεσπότην, τὸν οἰκουμενικὸν Πατριάρχην, κύριον κύριον [δεῖνα] . . . Κύριε, φύλαττε αὐτὸν εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*. Μετὰ τὸν πολυχρονισμὸν ὁ ἀπ’ Ἄμβωνος λόγος· εἰς τὸ τέλος οἱ Χοροὶ *Τὸν Δεσπότην καὶ Ἀρχιερέα ἡμῶν*, τοῦ Πατριάρχου εὐλογοῦντος· ἀπὸ τοῦ Βήματος τὸ *Δι’ εὐχῶν τοῦ ἁγίου Δεσπότου ἡμῶν*, καὶ οὕτω λήγει ἡ τελετή.

units.english_text: Following this, the Patriarch, vested in the Mandya, the Epitrachilion, and the Omophorion, stands before the Holy Table and intones: **"Blessed is our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*). Then the Trisagion Prayers are read as above, and the Dismissal is given. After this, while the Patriarch stands in the Beautiful Gate [Royal Doors], the Great Logothete [Chancellor and Grand Representative of the Patriarchate] comes forward and, by means of the customary formal proclamation, invites the Patriarch to ascend the Ecumenical Throne. The Patriarch expresses his thanksgiving; and immediately following, the Metropolitan of Herakleia approaches him and, after the customary congratulatory address, delivers into his hands the Patriarchal Pastoral Staff, kissing his right hand. Thus His All-Holiness the Patriarch, escorted by the Great Logothete and the deacons, ascends the Throne and blesses the people with the Precious Cross, while the Choirs chant: **"For many years, Master!"** (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, Δέσποτα*).

units.slavonic_text: God,” etc. and the Dismissal Prayer: [“May Christ our true God,] “Who sent the All-holy Spirit from heaven as tongues of fire,” without the “Through the prayers.” After the foregoing, the Patriarch, vested in the Mandya, the Epitra- chilion and the Omophorion, stands before the Holy Table and says “Blessed.” Then the Trisagion, etc. is read as above, and then the Dismissal occurs. After this, with the Patriarch standing in the Beautiful Gate, the Great Logothetis [Chief Secretary of the Holy Synod] comes forward, and by means of the customary proclamation invites the Patriarch to the Ecumenical Throne. The Patriarch expresses thanksgiving, and then the Metropolitan of Hiraklia [one of the oldest and highly revered dioceses] after the customary welcoming address bestows him with the Patriarchal Staff, kissing his right hand. Thus, His All Holiness, the Patriarch, accompanied by the Great Logothetis and the Deacons ascends the Throne and blesses the people with the Holy Cross, the Choirs singing “For Many years, [Master].” After this the First-Chanter sings the Polychronion for the Ecumenical Patriarch: “Make him live for many years, O Lord God, Your all-holy and most respected lord and Master, the Ecumenical Patriarch, lord, lord __(name)__. Lord, preserve him for many years.” After the Polychronion, the homily from the Pulpit is given [usually by the Great Logothetis] at the conclusion of which the Choirs sing “Our Bishop and Hierarch,” as the Patriarch blesses. The clergymen inside the Holy Sanctuary intone together “Through the prayers of our Holy Bishop,” and thus ends the ceremony.
units.english_text: After this, the Protopsaltes [First-Chanter] with his Choir chants the Patriarchal Polychronion: **"May the Lord God preserve for many years our most holy and venerable Master and Lord, the Ecumenical Patriarch, Lord [Name]! O Lord, preserve him for many years!"** (*Πολυχρόνιον ποιήσαι Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς τὸν παναγιώτατον καὶ σεβασμιώτατον ἡμῶν αὐθέντην καὶ Δεσπότην, τὸν οἰκουμενικὸν Πατριάρχην, κύριον κύριον...*). Following the Polychronion, the homily from the Ambo is delivered [customarily by the Great Logothete]. At the conclusion of the address, the Choirs chant: **"Our Master and Chief Priest, O Lord, preserve for many years!"** (*Τὸν Δεσπότην καὶ Ἀρχιερέα ἡμῶν, Κύριε, φύλαττε εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), while the Patriarch blesses the assembly. From within the Holy Sanctuary [Bema], the clergy intone: **"Through the prayers of our holy Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us and save us. Amen."** (*Δι’ εὐχῶν τοῦ ἁγίου Δεσπότου ἡμῶν, Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, ἐλέησον καὶ σῶσον ἡμᾶς. Ἀμήν*), and thus the ceremony of accession concludes.*...[^509]

units.english_text: * *Historical and Ecclesiological Context of the Accession Ceremony:* The accession and enthronement ceremony (*Anarrhesis*) of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople is celebrated with ancient Byzantine court and liturgical ceremonial. The Metropolitan of Herakleia exercises the historic right of investiture with the patriarchal crozier by virtue of Herakleia's ancient position as the metropolitan see over Byzantium prior to the establishment of the capital at Constantinople. The Great Logothete represents the imperial civil chancery and lay leadership of the Great Church of Christ.

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Ceremony of the Return of the Patriarch to the Ecumenical Throne (Part 1, p. 887)]
units.english_text: Arriving at the Patriarchate with his customary entourage as aforesaid, the Patriarch comes and stands before the Great Portal of the Church* and vests with the Mandya. The holy Hierarchs who have accompanied him enter immediately into the Holy Sanctuary [Bema]. The Choirs, preceded by the Primikirios bearing the Divamboulon and four deacons, two of them censing the Patriarch as he enters the church, sing: **"It is truly meet to bless thee, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God: more honorable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim: thee who without defilement gavest birth to God the Word, true Theotokos, thee do we magnify!"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*). The Patriarch, standing in the middle of the church, blesses, but he does not carry the Patriarchal Staff. Two of the Hierarchs help him ascend the Throne; and then the Metropolitan of Herakleia comes forward, and after the customary welcoming address bestows the Patriarch with the Patriarchal Staff, kissing his right hand, and then enters the Holy Sanctuary. The Great Logothete stands at the Parathrone [a smaller throne near the Patriarchal throne]. Then the Great Ecclesiarch [Grand Master of Ceremonies] vests the Patriarch with the Epitrachilion and the Omophorion. The Great Archdeacon exclaims: **"Bless, Master!"** (*Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα*). The Patriarch: **"Blessed is our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*). The Archdeacon recites the Trisagion Prayers. The Patriarch pronounces the Exclamation: **"For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*). The First Choir sings the Dismissal Troparion of Saint George in Tone 4: **"As the liberator of captives and defender of the poor, physician of the sick, and champion of monarchs: victorious Great Martyr George, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved!"** (*Ὡς τῶν αἰχμαλώτων ἐλευθερωτής*); and the Second Choir sings the Theotokion: **"Open unto us the gate of compassion, O blessed Theotokos, that hoping in thee we may not perish, but be delivered by thee from dangers: for thou art the salvation of the Christian race!"** (*Τῆς εὐσπλαγχνίας τὴν πύλην ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν*). The Great Archdeacon intones the Ektenia: **"Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee, hear us and have mercy!"** (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς κατὰ τὸ μέγα ἔλεός σου...*). The Choirs respond: **"Lord, have mercy"** (*Κύριε, ἐλέησον*) three times. The Great Archdeacon continues: **"Again let us pray for all devout and Orthodox Christians."** (*Ὑπὲρ τῶν εὐσεβῶν καὶ ὀρθοδόξων χριστιανῶν*); **"For our Archbishop..."** (*Ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἀρχιεπισκόπου ἡμῶν...*); **"That this holy church and this city, and every city and countryside, may be preserved from wrath, plague, famine, earthquake, flood, fire, sword, the invasion of aliens, and civil war..."** (*Ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι...*), etc. The Patriarch intones the Exclamation: **"Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of them that be far off at sea: and be merciful, be merciful, O Master, unto our sins, and have mercy on us!"** (*Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός...*). At the conclusion, the First-Chanter [Protopsaltes] sings the Patriarchal Polychronion, then the homily is delivered from the Pulpit [Ambo, customarily by the Great Logothete]. At the conclusion, the Choirs sing...[^510]

units.english_text: * *Rubrical and Historical Note on the Ceremony of Return:* This solemn ceremony of return (*Epanodos*) was appointed for when an Ecumenical Patriarch returned to Constantinople and reoccupied the patriarchal cathedra after a journey, absence, exile, or synodal reinstallation. The Great Church observed this rite with the same liturgical dignity as the accession, culminating in the acclamation of the Primate and the patriarchal blessing upon the city and the faithful.

units.english_text: Τὴν πρώτην Σεπτεμβρίου ὁ Οἰκουμενικὸς Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὸν πατριαρχικὸν Ναὸν κατὰ τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν καὶ τὸ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον καὶ τὴν Λειτουργίαν, ἵσταται δὲ ἐν τῷ παραθρονίῳ φέρων Ἐπανωκαλύμμαυχον καὶ Χαζράνιον. Μετὰ τὴν Λειτουργίαν, οἱ ἅγιοι Ἀρχιερεῖς ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ Βήματος, ἔνθα ἀκροῶνται αὐτῆς, ἀνέρχονται εἰς τὸ μέγα Συνοδικόν, ὅπου, μετὰ τὴν διανομὴν τοῦ Ἀντιδώρου, ἀνέρχεται καὶ ὁ Πατριάρχης, προπορευομένων τῶν Ἑξαπτερύγων καὶ Λαμπάδων, τοῦ Πριμικηρίου μετὰ τοῦ Διβαμβούλου, καὶ τῶν ψαλτῶν, καὶ ἐνδύεται Ἐπιτραχήλιον καὶ Ὠμοφόριον. Εἶτα ὁ Μ. Ἀρχιδιάκονος ἐκφωνεῖ *Εὐλόγησον Δέσποτα*, ὁ Πατριάρχης [corr. text: ὁ Πατριράρχης] *Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*, ὁ Μ. Ἀρχιδιάκονος τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Πατριάρχης *Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*, καὶ ὁ α΄ Χορὸς ψάλλει τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον *Ὁ πάσης Δημιουργὸς τῆς κτίσεως*, ὁ β΄ τὸ *Ὑπομονῆς στῦλος γέγονας*, ὁ α΄ Χορὸς αὖθις τὸ *Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη*· εἶτα ὁ Μ. Ἀρχιδιάκονος *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς κατὰ τὸ μέγα ἔλεος σου*, οἱ Χοροὶ τὸ *Κύριε ἐλέησον* τρίς, ὁ Δευτερεύων *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τῶν εὐσεβῶν*, ὁ Μ. Ἀρχιδιάκονος *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἀρχιεπισκόπου ἡμῶν*, ὁ Δευτερεύων *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι*, οἱ Χοροὶ τὸ *Κύριε ἐλέησον* ὡς εἴθισται, ὁ Μ. units.english_text: On September 1, the Ecumenical Patriarch comes down to the Patriarchal Church at Vespers and, in the morning, for Matins and the Divine Liturgy. He stands at the Parathrone [a smaller throne near the Patriarchal cathedra] wearing the Epanokalymmavchion [a kamilavkion draped with the monastic veil] and carrying the Chazranion [a plain wooden patriarchal staff]. After the Divine Liturgy, the holy Hierarchs who were listening to the Liturgy from within the Holy Sanctuary [Bema], proceed to the Great Synodikon [the hall of the Holy Synod], where, after the distribution of the Antidoron, the Patriarch also arrives, preceded by the Exapteryga [six-winged seraphic fans] and Candles, the Primikirios with the Divamboulon [two-branched candle], and the Chanters, and vests with the Epitrachilion and the Omophorion.

Amen."** (*Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν*).

units.slavonic_text: On September 1, the Ecumenical Patriarch comes down to the Patriarchal Church at Vespers and, in the morning, for Matins and the Liturgy. He stands at the Parathrone [a smaller throne near the Patriarchal throne] wearing the Epanokalymmafchon [a priest's cap with a black veil draped behind it] and carrying a Chazranion [a plain, unadorned staff]. After the Liturgy, the holy Hierarchs who were listening to the Liturgy from within the Holy Sanctuary, proceed to the Great Synodikon [the room where the Holy Synod meets], where, after the distribution of the Antidoron, the Patriarch also proceeds to the Great Synodikon, preceded by the Exapteryga [six-winged fans] and Candles, the Primikirios with the Divamvulon [two-wicked Candle], the Chanters, and vests with the Epitrachilion and the Omophorion. Then the Great Archdeacon exclaims "Bless, Master"; the Patriarch: "Blessed is our God"; the Archdeacon recites the Trisagion; the Patriarch: "For Yours is." The First Choir sings the Apolytikion "Creator of all the Universe," the Second Choir "You became a column of endurance." The First Choir sings again "Hail, O Woman, full of grace." Then the Great Archdeacon: "Have mercy on us, O God, according to Your great mercy." The Choirs: "Lord, have mercy" (3 times) The Second Deacon: "Again let us pray for all devout [and Orthodox Christians]." The Choirs: "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). The Great Archdeacon: "For our Archbishop." The Choirs: "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). The Second Deacon: "For this Holy Church may be kept." The Choirs: "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). The Great Archdeacon: "Again we pray that the Lord God hears us." The Choirs: "Lord, have mercy" (3 times). The Patriarch as customary: "Hear us, O God," etc., and the Dismissal
units.english_text: The Second Choir chants the Dismissal Troparion of Saint Simeon the Stylite in Tone 1: **"Thou hast become a pillar of endurance, having rivaled the forefathers, O venerable one: Job in his sufferings, Joseph in temptations, and the bodiless angels while yet in the flesh: Simeon our holy father, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved!"** (*Ὑπομονῆς στῦλος γέγονας...*).

units.english_text: *Δεσπότην καὶ Ἀρχιερέα*. Εἶτα ὁ Πατριάρχης ἀναγινώσκει τὴν Πρᾶξιν, συγχωρῶν πάντας τοὺς ἁπανταχοῦ τῆς Οἰκουμένης εὐσεβεῖς καὶ Ὀρθοδόξους χριστιανοὺς πάσης τάξεως καὶ βαθμοῦ· μετὰ τὸ πέρας οἱ Χοροὶ ψάλλουσι τὸν Πολυχρονισμὸν τοῦ Πατριάρχου, οὗτος δὲ ὑπογράφει τὴν Ἰνδικτιῶνα τοῦ ἔτους, ὡς καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι συνοδικοὶ Ἀρχιερεῖς ὑπογράφουσιν ἕκαστος κατὰ τάξιν, φοροῦντες Ἐπιτραχήλιον καὶ Ὠμοφόριον, οἱ δὲ Χοροὶ ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ψάλλουσι τὰ Ἰδιόμελα τῆς ἡμέρας. Μετὰ τὴν ὑπογραφήν, ἀσπάζονται πάντες οἱ παριστάμενοι τὴν δεξιὰν τῆς Α.Θ. Παναγιότητος καὶ οὕτω λήγει ἡ τελετή.

units.english_text: Then the Patriarch reads aloud the Synodal Act [the patriarchal encyclical decree marking the opening of the new Ecclesiastical Year, the Indiction], imparting forgiveness unto all devout and Orthodox Christians of every order and rank throughout the whole civilized world [Oikoumene]. At the conclusion of the reading, the Choirs chant the Patriarchal Polychronion [Acclamation]. The Patriarch then signs the Synodal Act of the Indiction for the new year, followed by all the holy synodal Hierarchs, who sign in order of episcopal seniority, vested in Epitrachilion and Omophorion. In the meantime, the Choirs chant the Idiomelon hymns of the Feast of the Indiction. After the signing is concluded, all those present kiss the right hand of His All-Holiness, and thus ends the service.*...[^513]

units.slavonic_text: prayers, as the Choirs sing "Our Bishop and Hierarch." Then the Patriarch reads the Act [the document stating the beginning of the new ecclesiastical year, i.e. the Indiction of the new year] forgiving all Orthodox Christians of every order and rank, wherever they may be. At the conclusion of the foregoing, the Choirs sing the Polychronion [Acclamation] of the Patriarch, who then signs the Indiction of the year, as do all the other Hierarchs of the Synod according to their seniority of ordination, vested in the Epitrachilion and the Omophorion. In the meanwhile the Choirs chant the Idiomela of the day. After the signing, all those present kiss the right hand of His All-Holiness, and thus ends the service.
units.english_text: * *Translators' Note on the Ceremony of the Indiction:* This patriarchal rite of the Indiction on September 1, as codified in the 1888 Violakis Typikon, has undergone certain ritual modifications in later patriarchal practice. For contemporary order and details of the current ceremonial in the Ecumenical Patriarchate, refer to the annual Patriarchal Yearbooks (Imerologia).

units.slavonic_text: Τῇ ΚΔ΄ Δεκεμβρίου εἰς τὰς Ὥρας σημαίνει τῇ ιβ΄ τῆς νυκτός, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὴν α΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς δ΄ τῆς ἡμέρας. Ὅταν αἱ Ὧραι ψάλλωνται μόναι, σημαίνει εἰς τὴν α΄ τῆς πρωΐας, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς β΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς δ΄. Τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς Χριστοῦ Γεννήσεως, εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον σημαίνει εἰς τὰς θ΄ τῆς νυκτός, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς ι΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὴν α΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν τῆς πρωΐας. Τῇ πρώτῃ τοῦ ἔτους σημαίνει εἰς τὴν α΄ τῆς πρωΐας, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς β΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς δ΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν. Τῇ Ε΄ Ἰανουαρίου εἰς τὰς Ὥρας σημαίνει τῇ ια΄ νυκτός, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς γ΄. Ὅταν αἱ Ὧραι ψάλλωνται μόναι, σημαίνει εἰς τὴν α΄ τῆς πρωΐας, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς β΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς δ΄.

units.slavonic_text: On December 24, the Hours begin and the church bells ring at 6 a.m.; the Patriarch arrives at 7 a.m, the Dismissal at 10 a.m. When the Hours are chanted alone, they begin and then the church bells ring at 7 a.m., the Patriarch arrives at 8 a.m., Dismissal at 10 a.m. On the day of Christ's Birth [December 25], Matins begins at 3 a.m, the Patriarch arrives at 4:30 a.m., Dismissal at 7:30 a.m. On the first of the year [January 1], Matins begins and the church bells ring at 7 a.m., the Patriarch arrives at 8:30 a.m., Dismissal at 10:30 a.m. On January 5 the Hours begin and the church bells ring at 5 a.m., the Patriarch arrives at 6 a.m., Dismissal at 9 a.m. When the Hours are chanted alone, they begin and the church bells ring at 7 a.m., the Patriarch arrives at 8 a.m., Dismissal at 10 a.m.

units.english_text: * *Scholarly Note on Constantinopolitan Feasts Horologion:* This horary rubric preserves the official bell-tolling and patriarchal ceremonial schedule of the Ecumenical Patriarchate in Constantinople. The times distinguish between the days when the Royal Hours are immediately conjoined to the Vesperal Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (requiring an early start before dawn) and when the Paramony falls on a Saturday or Sunday, in which case the Royal Hours are chanted alone in the morning without fasting fast-extension, and the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom is celebrated at the customary morning hour.

provenance.verbatim_source: * *Scholarly Note on Constantinopolitan Feasts Horologion:* This horary rubric preserves the official bell-tolling and patriarchal ceremonial schedule of the Ecumenical Patriarchate in Constantinople. The times distinguish between the days when the Royal Hours are immediately conjoined to the Vesperal Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (requiring an early start before dawn) and when the Paramony falls on a Saturday or Sunday, in which case the Royal Hours are chanted alone in the morning without fasting fast-extension, and the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom is celebrated at the customary morning hour.

units.slavonic_incipit: Τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν Θεοφανίων σημαίνει εἰς
units.slavonic_text: Τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν Θεοφανίων σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ι΄ τῆς νυκτός, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς ια΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς β΄. Τῇ Κυριακῇ τῆς Ὀρθοδοξίας σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ι΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς β΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν. Τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Μ. Πέμπτῃ, εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ια΄, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὴν α΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν. Τῇ ἑσπέρᾳ, εἰς Ἀκολουθίαν τῶν ἁγίων Παθῶν σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, μετὰ ἡμίσειαν ὥραν κατέρχεται ὁ Πατριάρχης, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς δ΄ τῆς νυκτός. Τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Μ. Παρασκευῇ εἰς τὰς Ὥρας σημαίνει τῇ ια΄, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται μετὰ ἡμίσειαν ὥραν, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς γ΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν. Τῇ ἑσπέρᾳ, εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου, σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται μετὰ ἡμίσειαν ὥραν, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς δ΄ νυκτός. Τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ Μ. Σαββάτῳ πρωῒ σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὴν α΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν. Τῇ Κυριακῇ τοῦ Πάσχα σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ε΄ νυκτός, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται μετὰ ἡμίσειαν ὥραν, ἡ Ἀνάστασις εἰς τὰς ς΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς θ΄ τῆς νυκτός. Τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῆς Ἀναστάσεως σημαίνει εἰς τὰς γ΄, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς δ΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὰς ς΄.
units.english_text: Τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Μ. Πέμπτῃ, εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον σημαίνει εἰς τὰς ια΄, ὁ Πατριάρχης κατέρχεται εἰς τὰς ιβ΄, Ἀπόλυσις εἰς τὴν α΄ καὶ ἡμίσειαν.

units.english_text: * *Scholarly Note on Paschal and Holy Week Horology:* In the patriarchal usage of the Ecumenical Throne, this horary schedule codified the traditional times for the solemn Holy Week and Paschal celebrations. The reckoning adheres to the ancient canonical calculation wherein 12 hours of night and 12 hours of day are counted from sundown to sunrise and sunrise to sundown respectively, adjusted to seasonal equinoctial norms. Note the solemn midnight celebration of Pascha commencing at 11:00 p.m. (the bell sounding at the 5th hour of the night) and concluding at 3:00 a.m., followed by the Agape Vespers in the forenoon.

units.slavonic_text: AT WHICH THE PATRIARCH OFFICIATES
units.english_text: * *Scholarly Note on Patriarchal Officiations:* This official calendar designates the stationary feasts wherein the Ecumenical Patriarch is rubrically required to officiate (*chorostatein*) in the Patriarchal Cathedral of Saint George at the Phanar. For the minor immovable commemorations not listed here, the presiding hierarch or a synodal metropolitan officiates by patriarchal delegation. Note that September 1 (Indiction) is uniquely noted as celebrated *from the Parathrone* rather than the high patriarchal throne.

units.slavonic_incipit: Εἰς τὸν Ἀκάθιστον Ὕμνον τὸ δὲ
units.slavonic_text: Εἰς τὸν Ἀκάθιστον Ὕμνον τὸ δὲ πρωῒ ἐν τῷ παραθρονίῳ. Τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Μ. Πέμπτῃ, τὸ πρωῒ εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, καὶ τὸ ἑσπέρας εἰς τὴν Ἀκολουθίαν τῶν Ἁγίων Παθῶν. Τῇ Ἁγίᾳ καὶ Μ. Παρασκευῇ εἰς τὰς Ὥρας καὶ τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, καὶ τὸ ἑσπέρας εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον τοῦ Ἐπιταφίου. Τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ Μ. Σαββάτῳ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν καὶ τὴν Λειτουργίαν. Τῇ Κυριακῇ τοῦ Πάσχα, καὶ τῇ Δευτέρᾳ, Τρίτῃ καὶ Παρασκευῇ τῆς Διακαινησίμου. Τῇ Πέμπτῃ τῆς Ἀναλήψεως. Ἰστέον ὅτι, κατὰ τὴν ἐπικρατήσασαν ἔκπαλαι ἐν τῇ Μ. Ἐκκλησίᾳ συνήθειαν, ὁσάκις ἂν ἐχοροστάτει ὁ Πατριάρχης, συνεχοροστάτουν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ Συνοδικοὶ Ἀρχιερεῖς, ἀλλὰ τανῦν ἐν πᾶσι μὲν τοῖς Ὄρθροις καὶ ταῖς Λειτουργίαις συγχοροστατοῦσι, μόνον ὅμως ἐν τοῖς ἐφεξῆς Ἑσπερινοῖς, ἤτοι ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τοῦ ὀνόματος τῆς Α.Θ. Παναγιότητος, τῆς Α΄ τῆς Ἰνδίκτου, τῆς Παραμονῆς τῶν Χριστουγέννων καὶ τῶν Θεοφανίων, τῆς Α΄ τοῦ ἔτους, τῆς Κυριακῆς τῆς Ὀρθοδοξίας, τῆς Ἀκαθίστου, τῆς ἑορτῆς τοῦ Εὐαγγελισμοῦ, τῆς Κυριακῆς τῶν Βαΐων, τῆς Μ. Πέμπτης, τῆς Μ. Παρασκευῆς, τοῦ Μ. Σαββάτου, τῆς Ἀναστάσεως, τῆς ἑορτῆς τοῦ ἁγίου Γεωργίου, τῆς Κυριακῆς τοῦ Θωμᾶ, καὶ τῆς Κυριακῆς τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Ἐκτὸς δὲ τούτων τῶν ἐπισήμων Χοροστασιῶν, ὁ Οἰκουμενικὸς Πατριάρχης κατερχόμενος ἐν τῷ Ναῷ ἵσταται ἐν τῷ παραθρονίῳ (γεδέκι) μετὰ χαζρανίου καὶ ἄνευ Μανδύου, κατὰ τοὺς Ἑσπερινοὺς τῶν Κυριακῶν τῆς Ἁγ. καὶ Μ. Τεσσαρακοστῆς, τὰς Προηγιασμένας, ἐν τῷ Μεγάλῳ Ἀποδείπνῳ καὶ τῷ Κανόνι τῷ ψαλλομένῳ τὴν Α΄ Ἑβδομάδα τῆς Τεσσαρακοστῆς, τὴν ἑσπέραν τῆς Ἀκολουθίας τοῦ Μεγ. Κανόνος, τὴν πρωΐαν τῆς Ἀκαθίστου, τὴν ἑορτὴν τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου Ἀρχιεπισκόπου Κωνσταντινουπόλεως (ἐὰν μὴ τύχῃ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Κυριακῇ ὅτι ἐὰν βούληται ὁ Πατριάρχης, χοροστατεῖ ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ φέρων Μανδύαν), καὶ τὴν ἑορτὴν τῆς Ἰνδίκτου.
units.english_text: Τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ Μ. Σαββάτῳ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν καὶ τὴν Λειτουργίαν.

provenance.verbatim_source: Τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ Μ. Σαββάτῳ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινὸν καὶ τὴν Λειτουργίαν.

units.slavonic_incipit: The Akathist Hymn, and in the
units.slavonic_text: The Akathist Hymn, and in the morning at the Parathrone. On Holy and Great Thursday, in the morning at the Liturgy and in the evening at the Service of the Holy Passion. On Holy and Great Friday at the Hours and the Vespers, and in the evening at the Matins of the Epitaphios. On Holy and Great Saturday in the morning at Vespers and the Liturgy. On the Sunday of Easter, and Monday, Tuesday and Friday of Bright [Renewal] Week. On Thursday of the Ascension. Note that according to the ancient custom and practice of the Great Church, whenever the Patriarch officiated, the Hierarchs of the Synod officiated with him, but not necessarily at all the Matins and Liturgies, and only at the following Vespers: the Nameday of the Patriarch, the First of the Indiction, the Eve of Christmas and Theophany [Epiphany], the first of the year, the Sunday of Orthodoxy, the Akathist, the Annunciation, Palm Sunday, Holy Thursday, Holy Friday, Holy Saturday, The Resurrection, Saint George, the Sunday of Thomas, and the Sunday of Pentecost. Aside from these formal Officiations, the Ecumenical Patriarch, when he comes down to the Church, stands at the Parathrone (Gedeki) with the Chazranion and without the Mandya, at the Vespers of the Sundays of Holy and Great Lent, the Presanctified Liturgies, the Great Compline and the Canon chanted during the First Week of Great Lent, the evening of the Service of the Great Canon, the morning of the Akathist, the Feast of Our Father among the Saints, John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople (if the Feast does not occur on a Sunday, then if the Patriarch so desires, he officiates from the [Patriarchal] throne wearing a Mandya), and on the Feast of the Indiction.

units.slavonic_text: *(Printed Page 901)*
units.english_text: * *Historical and Rubrical Note on the Parathronion and Synodal Concelebration:* In patriarchal usage, a sharp distinction is drawn between full patriarchal officiation (*chorostasia*)—wherein the Patriarch presides from the elevated cathedra vested in the episcopal Mandya with the synodal Hierarchs stationed with him—and non-pontifical presence at the *Parathrone* (the secondary seat adjacent to the patriarchal throne, known in colloquial Constantinopolitan parlance by the Ottoman loanword *gedeki*), wherein the Primate attends in monastic habit with the unadorned wooden walking cane (*chazranion*). Notice also the critical clarification where the Greek original explicitly affirms that the Holy Synod concelebrates at *all* Matins and Liturgies (*ἐν πᾶσι μὲν τοῖς Ὄρθροις καὶ ταῖς Λειτουργίαις συγχοροστατοῦσι*), restricting synodal attendance only regarding evening Vespers to the major solemnities enumerated.

units.english_text: Ἄν δ’ ἡ χειροτονία συμβῇ ἐν Κυριακῇ ἁπλῇ, λέγονται Καταβασίαι τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, καὶ μετὰ Τὴν τιμιωτέραν ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Ἐξαποστειλάρια πρῶτον τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον εἶτα τὸ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, ἄνευ Θεοτοκίου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους μετὰ τὰ δ΄ Ἀναστάσιμα λέγονται καὶ τὰ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς Παράδοξα σήμερον, Δόξα, Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη. Μετὰ τὴν Δοξολογίαν τὸ Σήμερον Σωτηρία. Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Εἰσοδικὸν Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστάς. Εἶτα τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ Εὐλογητὸς εἶ, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ Κοντάκιον Ὅτε καταβάς. Τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἀπόστολος τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν ἀντὶ τοῦ Αἰνεῖτε, Τὸ Πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθόν.

provenance.verbatim_source: Ἄν δ’ ἡ χειροτονία συμβῇ ἐν Κυριακῇ ἁπλῇ, λέγονται Καταβασίαι τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, καὶ μετὰ Τὴν τιμιωτέραν ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Ἐξαποστειλάρια πρῶτον τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον εἶτα τὸ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, ἄνευ Θεοτοκίου. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους μετὰ τὰ δ΄ Ἀναστάσιμα λέγονται καὶ τὰ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς Παράδοξα σήμερον, Δόξα, Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη. Μετὰ τὴν Δοξολογίαν τὸ Σήμερον Σωτηρία. Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Εἰσοδικὸν Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστάς. Εἶτα τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἀπολυτίκιον, τὸ Εὐλογητὸς εἶ, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ Κοντάκιον Ὅτε καταβάς. Τὸ Τρισάγιον, ὁ Ἀπόστολος τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν ἀντὶ τοῦ Αἰνεῖτε, Τὸ Πνεῦμά σου τὸ ἀγαθόν.

units.slavonic_text: When the Ordination of a Hierarch occurs on any day except Sunday and it is not the feast of a celebrating Saint, we sing all the hymns from Pentecost: the Apolytikia, Kontakia, Kathismata, Canons, Katavasie, Exapostilaria, Praises, Antiphons, Entrance Hymn, Epistle, Gospel and Communion Hymn.
units.english_text: - At the Praises (*Ainoi*): after the four Resurrection Stichera, the Stichera of Pentecost are chanted: **"Glorious things today all the nations have seen..."** (*Παράδοξα σήμερον πάντα τὰ ἔθνη εἶδον...*); **Glory:** **"Heavenly King, Paraclete, Spirit of Truth..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Παράκλητε, τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας...*); **Now and ever:** **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις, Θεοτόκε Παρθένε...*).

units.slavonic_text: If the Ordination occurs on a plain [regular] Sunday, the Katavasie of Pentecost are said, and, following "More honorable," the Ninth Ode of Pentecost. Exapostilaria: first that of the Resurrection then that of Pentecost, without a Theotokion. At the Praises: after the Four Resurrection Stichira we sing those of Pentecost "Strange things today," Glory, "Heavenly King," Now and ever, "Most blessed." After the Doxology, "Today Salvation." At the Liturgy, the Antiphons of Pentecost, the Entrance Hymn "O come let us worship ... who is risen." Then the Resurrection Apolytikion, the "Blessed are You," the Apolytikion of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion "When you came down." The Trisagios Hymn, the Apostolos of Pentecost and the Gospel of the coinciding Sunday, "It is meet." Communion Hymn, instead of "Praise," "Your Spirit."

units.slavonic_text: *(Printed Page 903)*
units.english_text: * *Rubrical Synthesis on Episcopal Ordinations:* The liturgical theology governing episcopal consecration in the Byzantine rite systematically infuses the Pentecostal pneumatological hymns into the Divine Liturgy and Divine Office. Because the episcopate represents the apostolic fullness of the Holy Spirit's descent at Pentecost, the typikon prescribes the Pentecostal proper hymns (Katavasiai, Ode 9, Exapostilaria, Antiphons, and the Pentecost Kontakion "When the Most High descended") to frame the ordination of a bishop across all ordinary days and Sundays.

units.english_text: Ἐν Κυριακῇ δὲ μετὰ Ἁγίου δεδοξασμένου ἄν συμπέσῃ χειροτονία Ἀρχιερέως, μετὰ τὰς Καταβασίας τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς Τὴν τιμιωτέραν καὶ τὴν θ΄ Ὠδὴν τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, τοῦ Ἁγίου, καὶ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους Ἀναστάσιμα β΄, τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς γ΄ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου γ΄, Δόξα, Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη. Μετὰ τὴν Δοξολογίαν Σήμερον σωτηρία. Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, καὶ μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν...ὁ ἀναστάς. Ἀπολυτίκια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον, τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, τοῦ Ἁγίου τῆς ἡμέρας, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ ναοῦ, καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον Ὅτε καταβάς. (Τὰ λοιπὰ ὡς ἀνωτέρω ἐν § Β΄.)

units.slavonic_incipit: ἡμέρας· ἀλλ’ ἐν τοιαύτῃ περιπτώσει προηγοῦνται
units.slavonic_text: ἡμέρας· ἀλλ’ ἐν τοιαύτῃ περιπτώσει προηγοῦνται ἐναντιρρήτως τὰ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς καὶ ἕπονται τὰ τοῦ Ἁγίου.
units.english_text: Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ Θεομητορικῆς ἑορτῆς ἄν τελῆται χειροτονία Ἀρχιερέως, Καταβασίαι ψάλλονται αἱ κεκανονισμέναι τῆς ἐποχῆς, καὶ μόνον Ἐξαποστειλάριον πρὸ τοῦ τῆς ἑορτῆς ψάλλεται τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς· καὶ εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους δύο μόνον Στιχηρὰ ἐκ τῶν τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς. Δόξα τὸ Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Καὶ νῦν τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς δὲ τὴν Λειτουργίαν τὰ Ἀντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς. Ἀπολυτίκια, μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, πρῶτον τὸ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς, δεύτερον τῆς ἑορτῆς, καὶ Ἀπόστολος ἐπίσης τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς.

units.slavonic_incipit: If the ordination of a Hierarch
units.slavonic_text: If the ordination of a Hierarch occurs on a Sunday with a celebrating Saint, after the Katavasie of Pentecost, we sing "More honorable" and the Ninth Ode of Pentecost. Exapostilaria: of the Resurrection, of Pentecost, of the Saint and the Theotokion. At the Praises: two Stichira of the Resurrection, three of Pentecost, and three of the Saint. Glory "Heavenly King," Now and ever "Most blessed." After the Doxology "Today salvation." In the Liturgy, the Antiphons of Pentecost, the Entrance Hymn "Come let us worship ... who is risen." Apolytikia: of the Resurrection, of Pentecost, of the Saint of the day, of the Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion "When You came down." (The rest as above in Situation Two.)
units.english_text: - At the Praises (*Ainoi*): two Stichera of the Resurrection, three of Pentecost, and three of the Saint. **Glory:** **"Heavenly King, Paraclete..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Παράκλητε...*); **Now and ever:** **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις, Θεοτόκε Παρθένε...*).

provenance.verbatim_source: - At the Praises (*Ainoi*): two Stichera of the Resurrection, three of Pentecost, and three of the Saint. **Glory:** **"Heavenly King, Paraclete..."** (*Βασιλεῦ οὐράνιε, Παράκλητε...*); **Now and ever:** **"Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..."** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη ὑπάρχεις, Θεοτόκε Παρθένε...*).

units.slavonic_text: If the ordination of a Hierarch occurs on a Feast of the Theotokos, the Katavasie are those ordained for the season, and only the Exapostilarion of Pentecost is sung before that of the Feast. At the Praises: only two Stichira of Pentecost. Glory, "Heavenly King," Now and ever of the Feast. In the Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast. After the Entrance, first the Apolytikion of Pentecost, then that of the Feast; the Epistle also is that of Pentecost.

units.slavonic_text: If the ordination of a Hierarch occurs on a Feast of the Lord, nothing else of Pentecost is chanted except the Exapostilarion, which is both preceded and followed by that of the Feast. After the Entrance, the Apolytikion of Pentecost from the Holy Sanctuary followed by the Apolytikion of the Feast and nothing more.
units.english_text: - Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Troparion, the Dismissal Troparion of Pentecost: **"Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..."** (*Εὐλογητὸς εἶ, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), the Dismissal Troparion of the commemorated Saint of the day, that of the Patron Saint of the temple, and the Kontakion of Pentecost: **"When the Most High descended..."** (*Ὅτε καταβὰς τὰς γλώσσας συνέχεε...*).

units.english_text: * *Note on Typikon Numbering Erratum and Dominical Precedence:* In the original Greek printed edition of the 1888 Violakis Typikon, this final rubric for Dominical Feasts is erroneously numbered as Situation Seven (§ Ζ΄), skipping numeral Six (§ ΣΤ΄), an editorial misprint corrected here in accordance with facing translations and critical editions. Rubrically, this section encapsulates the supreme liturgical principle of Dominical hierarchy: on a Great Feast of the Lord, the proper festal liturgy remains virtually unassailable, admitting only the singular Exapostilarion and the Sanctuary Dismissal Troparion of Pentecost to accompany the apostolic imposition of hands.

units.slavonic_text: [Original Greek Text: Concerning the Co-Celebration of Clergy (Part 1, p. 906)]
units.english_text: Ὅταν τύχωσι πλείονες τοῦ ἑνὸς Ἱερεῖς συλλειτουργοῦντες, ἀφ’ ἑσπέρας ἂν γένηται Εἴσοδος, ἀπαιτοῦνται τρεῖς τοὐλάχιστον Ἱερεῖς καὶ ψάλλουσιν ἔξωθεν ἡμικύκλιον ἀποτελοῦντες¹ ἐν τῷ μέσῳ τοῦ ναοῦ τὸ **Φῶς ἱλαρὸν** μέχρι τοῦ **καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα θεόν**, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ Βήματος τὸ ἐπίλοιπον, καὶ μετ’ αὐτὸ τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας ἅπαξ ἐκ τοῦ Βήματος καὶ δὶς ἔξωθεν. Εἰς δὲ τὴν Λιτὴν ὁ πρῶτος τῇ τάξει λέγει τὸ **Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός**, καὶ τὸ **Εἰρήνη πᾶσι**· ὁ δεύτερος, τὸ **Δέσποτα πολυέλεε**· καὶ ὁ τρίτος τὸ **Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός**· εἶτα ὁ πρῶτος κατάρχει τὸ **Θεοτόκε Παρθένε** βοηθούντων καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν· ἀλλ’ αὐτὸς μόνος θυμιᾷ καὶ στρέφει περὶ τοὺς ἄρτους μετὰ τοῦ Διακόνου. Τὸ δὲ πρωῒ οὐδὲν ἄλλο ψάλλουσιν οἱ συλλειτουργοῦντες ἱερεῖς ἐκ τοῦ Βήματος πλέον τῶν συνήθων καὶ τῷ ἑνὶ μόνῳ Λειτουργοῦντι ἱερεῖ, εἰμὴ τὸ **Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν καὶ προσπέσωμεν Χριστῷ** κατὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, εἶτα τὸ Ἀπολυτίκιον (ὅτε καὶ θυμιᾷ ὁ πρῶτος τῇ τάξει τὴν ἁγίαν Τράπεζαν καὶ τὰς Εἰκόνας)· τὸ Κοντάκιον, καὶ τὸ **Ἅγιος ὁ Θεὸς** τὴν τρίτην φοράν.² Τὰς Ἐκφωνήσεις λέγουσιν ἐξ ὑπαμοιβῆς ὁ εἷς μετὰ τὸν ἄλλον, εὐλογεῖ δὲ τὰ τίμια Δῶρα ὡς καὶ τὸν λαόν, ὁσάκις ἂν δέῃ, ὁ πρῶτος τῇ τάξει, καὶ κοινωνοῦσι τῶν Ἀχράντων Μυστηρίων κατὰ τάξιν ἕκαστος, τοῦ τελευταίου μεταδιδόντος καὶ τῷ Διακόνῳ.

units.slavonic_text: [English Facing Translation: Concerning the Co-Celebrant (Part 1, p. 907)]
units.english_text: When more than one priest concelebrate, beginning in the evening at Vespers, if an Entrance is performed, at least three priests are required. Standing in the middle of the temple forming a semicircle,¹ they chant outside the Holy Sanctuary the Lucernarium hymn **“O Gladsome Light”** (*Φῶς ἱλαρὸν*) up to the phrase: **“and Holy Spirit, God”** (*καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα θεόν*); and from within the Holy Sanctuary the remainder of the hymn is completed; and after it the Prokimenon of the day is chanted once from within the Holy Sanctuary and twice from outside. At the Litiya, the priest first in rank [by ecclesiastical dignity or order of ordination] intones the petition: **“Hear us, O God our Savior”** (*Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός*), and the blessing: **“Peace be to all”** (*Εἰρήνη πᾶσι*); the second priest intones: **“O Merciful Master”** (*Δέσποτα πολυέλεε*); and the third priest intones: **“Lord Jesus Christ our God”** (*Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός*); then the first priest begins the Artoklasia Troparion: **“O Theotokos Virgin, rejoice”** (*Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*), assisted by the others; but he alone censes and circles around the Loaves together with the Deacon.

units.english_text: In the morning at the Divine Liturgy, the concelebrating priests chant nothing from within the Holy Sanctuary beyond what is customary for a priest celebrating alone, except the Entrance Hymn: **“O come, let us worship and fall down before Christ”** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν καὶ προσπέσωμεν Χριστῷ*) at the Small Entrance. Then is chanted the Dismissal Troparion (during which the priest first in seniority of ordination censes the Holy Table and the sacred Icons); then follows the Kontakion, and the Trisagion **“Holy God”** (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*) for the third time.² The priestly Exclamations are recited by them in order, alternately one after the other. The priest first in rank blesses the Precious Gifts as well as the people, whenever required; and they receive the Pure Mysteries each according to his rank, with the last priest in seniority imparting communion also to the Deacon.

units.slavonic_incipit: When there are more than one
units.slavonic_text: When there are more than one priest co-celebrating, beginning with the evening, at Vespers, if an Entrance is to be performed, at least more than three priests must attend. They sing outside in the middle of the church in a semi-circle,¹ “O Gladsome Light” up to “and Holy Spirit, God.” They complete the rest of the hymn from inside the Holy Sanctuary. After that, the Prokimenon of the day is sung once from the Holy Sanctuary and twice from the outside. At the Liti, the clergyman first in order [rank or order of ordination] says “Hear us, O God” and “Peace be to all”; the second, “O Merciful Master,” and the third “Lord Jesus Christ our God”; then the first begins chanting “Theotokos Virgin” assisted by the others; but only he censes and circles around the Loaves with the Deacon. In the morning, the co-celebrating priests sing nothing from the Holy Sanctuary except the usual and the one celebrating Priest, except “Come let us worship and bow down to Christ” at the Entrance. Then is sung the Apolytikion (during which the first in seniority of ordination censes the Holy Table and the Icons). Then follows the Kontakion, and “Holy God” the third time.² The Exclamations are recited by them in order, alternately one after the other. The clergyman first in order [rank or order of ordination] blesses the Holy Gifts and the people. The clergymen receive the Holy Gifts in order of seniority of ordination, and the last one in seniority gives communion to the Deacon. If the co-celebration takes place among Hierarchs, the first in rank wears the Mandya and stands on the throne until the prescribed time. Then,
units.english_text: * *Scholarly Apparatus on Priestly Concelebration and Order of Seniority:* Although all presbyters share equally in the sacerdotal grace of the priesthood and owe mutual honor and respect to one another, they nevertheless precede each other strictly according to their ecclesiastical offices (*offikia*) or according to seniority of ordination. Note the solemn patriarchal caution against liturgical accretions born of clerical ambition: presbyters must never chant the episcopal acclamation *“Lord, save the pious”* (*Κύριε σῶσον τοὺς εὐσεβεῖς*), nor may they introduce individual spoken commemorations of the living and the dead while holding the Holy Gifts after the Great Entrance, adhering strictly to the summary and established traditional formula: *“May the Lord God remember us all in His kingdom.”*

units.english_text: Τὸ **Ἅγιος ὁ Θεὸς** ἀφοῦ ψαλῇ δὶς ἔξωθεν, τὸ τρίτον λέγεται ἀπὸ τοῦ Βήματος, τὸ τέταρτον ἔξωθεν καὶ αὖθις τὸ πέμπτον ἔσωθεν. Εἶτα, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, ἔξωθεν, ὡς καὶ τὸ **Ἅγιος ἀθάνατος**, καὶ μετ’ αὐτὸ ψάλλεται πάλιν ἐκ τοῦ Βήματος ἀργότερον τὸ **Ἅγιος ὁ Θεὸς** κατὰ Στάσεις τέσσαρας ἐναλλὰξ ὑπὸ τῶν δύο δεξιᾷ καὶ ἀριστερᾷ ἱσταμένων Ἀρχιερέων καὶ Ἱερέων καὶ εὐλογεῖ ὁ προεξάρχων διὰ τῶν δικηροτρικήρων λέγων τὸ **Κύριε, Κύριε, ἐπίβλεψον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ**. Μετὰ τὸ **Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς**, ψάλλεται αὖθις ἔξωθεν ὑπὸ τοῦ δεξιοῦ Χοροῦ τὸ **Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός**, ἀφοῦ ὁ Διάκονος εἴπῃ τὴν Ἐκφώνησιν **Δύναμις**. Τότε ψάλλεται ἔσωθεν τὸ **Κύριε σῶσον τοὺς εὐσεβεῖς** καὶ ἔξωθεν ἐπαναλαμβάνεται δὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Χορῶν· αὖθις ἔσωθεν ψάλλεται τὸ **Καὶ ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν**.

units.english_text: The Trisagion **“Holy God”** (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*), after it is chanted twice outside by the choirs, is chanted the third time from within the Holy Sanctuary, the fourth time outside, and the fifth time immediately from within the Holy Sanctuary. Then **“Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit: Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen”** outside, as well as the phrase: **“Holy Immortal, have mercy on us”** (*Ἅγιος ἀθάνατος, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*); and after that, again from within the Holy Sanctuary, **“Holy God”** is chanted in a slower melody in four stases alternately by the two ranks of hierarchs and priests standing on the right and left sides; and the presiding hierarch blesses with the dikerotrikera, intoning: **“Lord, Lord, look down from heaven and behold, and visit this vine, and perfect that which Thy right hand hath planted”** (*Κύριε, Κύριε, ἐπίβλεψον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ...*). After the response: **“Have mercy on us”** (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*), **“Holy God”** is chanted again outside by the right choir, after the deacon proclaims the exclamation: **“Dynamis!”** (*Δύναμις*). Then from within the Holy Sanctuary is chanted: **“Lord, save the pious”** (*Κύριε σῶσον τοὺς εὐσεβεῖς*), and outside it is repeated twice by the choirs; again from within the Holy Sanctuary is chanted: **“And hear us”** (*Καὶ ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν*). Then the Acclamation (*Phemē*) of the Patriarch is intoned once inside and twice outside; and if the presiding hierarch is a Metropolitan and the concelebrants are Bishops, the Acclamation of the Metropolitan is likewise chanted, both inside and outside; but if all are Metropolitans or all are Bishops, the Acclamation of the first in rank is omitted.

Then **“Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit: Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. units.slavonic_incipit: entering the Holy Sanctuary, he gives
units.slavonic_text: entering the Holy Sanctuary, he gives and receives³ forgiveness from his future co-celebrants, and thus they all vest. During the Doxology they exit the Holy Sanctuary preceded by the Priests, the last one to exit being the Chief Celebrant bearing the Miter on his head and the Pastoral Staff in his right hand. At the Entrance, singing with the rest of the Hierarchs and the Priests the Entrance Hymn, he blesses with the Dikirotrikira, enters the Holy Sanctuary first followed by the other Hierarchs and Priests, and censes around the Holy Table and the Prothesis*, the Icons and the people from the gates of the Holy Sanctuary, chanting the Apolytikion⁴ and lastly the Kontakion. The “Holy God,” after it is sung twice outside, the third is sung from the Holy Sanctuary, the fourth outside, and immediately the fifth inside. Then “Glory, Now and ever” outside, as well as “Holy Immortal”; and after that, again from the Holy Sanctuary “Holy God” is sung in a slower tempo in four segments alternately by the two ranks of Hierarchs and Priests standing on the right side and on the left. The Chief Celebrant blesses with the Dikirotrikira, chanting “Lord, Lord, look down from heaven.” After “Have mercy on us,” the right Choir sings “Holy God [the entire Trisagios Hymn]” as soon as the Deacon proclaims “Dynamis! [with Strength!]” Then, inside the Holy Sanctuary is sung “Lord, save the faithful”; it is repeated twice outside by the Choirs; then, inside is sung “And hear us.” Then the Fimi [Acclamation] of the Patriarch is sung once inside and twice outside. If the presiding Hierarch is a Metropolitan and the co-celebrants are Bishops, then the Fimi [Acclamation] of the Metropolitan is also sung, inside and outside; if they are all Metropolitans or all Bishops, the Fimi of the clergyman first in rank is omitted. In every situation of a blessing, the first in rank blesses, and he is the one who receives the Holy Gifts from the hands of the Deacon and the Priest during the Second Entrance and he commemorates the living and the dead; but the exclamations are divided in order and manner even down to the co-celebrating Priests. The Holy Gifts are blessed only by the Chief Celebrant, but the Hierarchs take communion by their own hand; the Priests and Deacons receive the Gifts from the Hierarch last in seniority of ordination.
units.english_text: In every occasion of blessing, the first in rank blesses; and he receives the Holy Gifts from the hands of the deacon and the priest during the Great Entrance and commemorates the living and the dead; but the exclamations are distributed in succession so as to extend even down to the concelebrating priests. The Holy Gifts are consecrated and blessed only by the presiding hierarch; but the hierarchs commune of the Pure Mysteries with their own hand, whereas the priests and the deacons receive communion from the hands of the hierarch lowest in episcopal seniority.*...[^521]

units.english_text: * *Scholarly Apparatus on Hierarchical Concelebration:* When bishops concelebrate with their presiding Metropolitan, or Metropolitans with their presiding Patriarch, the junior hierarchs kiss the right hand of the Primate upon exchanging the liturgical kiss of peace and mutual forgiveness before vesting. If a Memorial Service (*Mnemosynon*) coincides with the Liturgy, after the Dismissal Troparion of the saint of the day, the Dismissal Troparion of the Departed is chanted from within the Holy Sanctuary: *“Remember, O Lord, as Thou art good, Thy servants, and forgive whatever sins they have committed in this life; for none is sinless except Thee Who art able to grant rest unto the departed”* (*Μνήσθητι Κύριε ὡς ἀγαθὸς τῶν δούλων σου*). Notice the intricate four-stasis distribution of the slow hierarchical Trisagion between the right and left stations of the clergy framing the episcopal blessing with the dikirion and trikirion (*dikerotrikera*).
